Statements I, II and III: this is the official answer. It reflects the Commerce Ministry/Spices Board position on turmeric in 2022-23. Turmeric exports were around USD 200 million, and the National Turmeric Board (Nizamabad, Telangana) was set up to improve research, value addition and exports.
related: Turmeric scientific name: Curcuma longa, family Zingiberaceae.
National Turmeric Board is headquartered at Nizamabad, Telangana, launched January 2025.
Active compound of turmeric is curcumin; Lakadong variety has very high curcumin.
Spices Board of India is headquartered at Kochi and covers 52 scheduled spices.
1997 US turmeric patent was revoked after a CSIR challenge, a landmark biopiracy case.
Erode in Tamil Nadu is called the Yellow City or Turmeric City.
Sangli in Maharashtra is one of Asia's biggest turmeric markets.
ICAR-Indian Institute of Spices Research is at Kozhikode, Kerala.
statements: I — Correct: India is the world's largest producer and exporter of turmeric. India produces about 70-80% of global turmeric and holds the largest export share. The crop is grown on about 3 lakh hectares, with output of about 10-11 lakh tonnes. Main export markets include Bangladesh, the UAE, the USA, Malaysia and Iran. Turmeric is among the key spices regulated and promoted by the Spices Board of India (Ministry of Commerce, HQ Kochi), which lists it among the 52 scheduled spices. India also consumes most of what it produces domestically.

II — Correct: more than 30 varieties of turmeric are grown in India. Examples are Salem, Erode local, Alleppey Finger, Rajapore, Sangli, Duggirala, Lakadong, Pratibha, Prabha, Suvarna, Suguna, Sudarshana and Roma. Lakadong from Jaintia Hills, Meghalaya has high curcumin (about 7-12%) and a GI-related profile. Varieties differ in curcumin content, duration (7-9 months) and colour. Research on turmeric is led by ICAR-Indian Institute of Spices Research, Kozhikode, and the Indian Council of Agricultural Research system.

III — Correct: Maharashtra, Telangana, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu are major turmeric-producing States. Telangana and Maharashtra are usually top by area and output, followed by Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, and also Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, West Bengal and Assam. Nizamabad (Telangana), Sangli and Hingoli (Maharashtra) and Erode (Tamil Nadu, known as Yellow City) are major trade centres. Sangli is one of Asia's biggest turmeric markets. Turmeric needs warm, humid climate with 1,000-2,000 mm rainfall and well-drained loamy soil.
summary: The answer is (d): all three statements are correct. India dominates world turmeric production and exports (about 70% or more of global output), grows more than 30 varieties, and its main producing States are Maharashtra, Telangana, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.
topic_notes: Turmeric (Curcuma longa) belongs to the ginger family, Zingiberaceae. It is a tropical perennial herb grown for its rhizomes, which are boiled, dried and polished. India has the largest share of world production (about 70%+), consumption and exports. Production is about 10-11 lakh tonnes from roughly 3 lakh hectares. Leading States are Telangana, Maharashtra, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, followed by Andhra Pradesh and Odisha. Key markets are Nizamabad, Sangli, Erode and Duggirala. Over 30 varieties are grown, among them Lakadong, Salem, Alleppey, Rajapore and Erode local. Active compound curcumin gives the yellow colour and medicinal value. India has fought patent claims: in 1997 the US patent on turmeric wound healing, granted to University of Mississippi Medical Center researchers, was revoked after a CSIR challenge in 1997 (patent cancelled), an important biopiracy case. The Spices Board (Kochi, under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry) regulates spice exports and oversees 52 scheduled spices. The National Turmeric Board was announced in October 2023 and launched in January 2025 at Nizamabad. Other spice topics UPSC may ask: saffron in Kashmir (GI tag), black pepper (Kerala, Karnataka), cardamom (queen of spices, Idukki), chilli (Andhra Pradesh, Guntur), cumin and coriander (Gujarat, Rajasthan), and ginger (Assam, Kerala). Good prelims practice is to link spices with GI tags, such as Alleppey Green Cardamom and Lakadong Turmeric, and with export data.

question:
Which of the following are the evidences of the phenomenon of continental drift?
I. The belt of ancient rocks from Brazil coast matches with those from Western Africa. Il. The gold deposits of Ghana are derived from the Brazil plateau when the two continents lay side by side. Ill. The Gondwana system of sediments from India is known to have its counterparts in six different landmasses of the Southern Hemisphere. Select the correct answer using the code given below
subject: Geography
detail: Continental drift was proposed by Alfred Wegener in 1912 (published 1915, 'The Origin of Continents and Oceans'). He argued that all continents formed a single supercontinent, Pangaea, which broke up about 200 million years ago into Laurasia and Gondwanaland. His evidences were: (1) Matching coastlines (the Sir Edward Bullard computer fit at 1000 fathom depth); (2) Rock-type similarity, where ancient rock belts of Brazil match those of western Africa; (3) Tillite, glacial deposits of the Gondwana system, found in India, Africa, South America, Australia, Antarctica and the Falkland Islands (the six landmasses); (4) Placer deposits, such as the gold of Ghana, which has no source rocks locally and is believed to come from the Brazil plateau; (5) Distribution of fossils such as Mesosaurus and Glossopteris. Since I, II and III each match these standard NCERT evidences, none can be eliminated. Options (a), (b) and (d) each wrongly reject a valid statement. The key is to recall the NCERT list: continental fit, rock similarity, tillite, placer deposits, fossils.
explanations: Wrong: it leaves out statement II, which is also a valid evidence (Ghana gold placer deposits).
Wrong: it leaves out statement III, the Gondwana system sediments found across six southern landmasses.
Correct: statements I, II and III are all standard evidences of continental drift.
Wrong: it leaves out statement I, the match of the Brazil and West Africa ancient rock belts.
keyfact: Evidence for continental drift: coastline fit, matching rock belts, tillite (Gondwana), placer gold (Ghana-Brazil) and fossils.
option_notes: Statements I and III only: this combination would be correct only if the Ghana gold placer link were not an evidence. It is, so this option is incomplete. It includes rock-belt matching and the Gondwana sediments, which are both genuine evidences used by Wegener and in NCERT.

Statements I and II only: it would omit the Gondwana system. The Gondwana sediments are among the strongest evidences, since tillite shows glaciation across India, Africa, South America, Australia and Antarctica. The option is therefore incomplete.

Statements I, II and III: this is the full set. Wegener's evidences include coastline fit, rock similarity, tillite, placer deposits and fossil distribution. This option captures rock belts, placer gold and Gondwana sediments, and is the official answer.

Statements II and III only: it would drop the Brazil-West Africa rock belt match. That match, about 2 billion year old rock belts on both sides of the Atlantic, is a classic piece of evidence, so the option is incomplete.
related: Alfred Wegener proposed continental drift in 1912.
Pangaea split into Laurasia and Gondwanaland.
Mesosaurus fossils are found in South Africa and Brazil.
Seafloor spreading was proposed by Harry Hess in 1961.
Vine and Matthews explained magnetic striping on ocean floors in 1963.
Plate tectonics was formulated in 1967 by McKenzie, Parker and Morgan.
India's Gondwana coal is found in the Damodar, Mahanadi and Godavari valleys.
statements: I — Correct: The ancient rock belts of the Brazil coast match those of western Africa, indicating the two were once contiguous. The Brazilian and West African belts are about 2 billion years old and have similar rock ages and structure. Wegener used such geological continuity, along with the jigsaw fit of the South Atlantic coasts, as proof that South America and Africa were joined within Gondwanaland before separating in the Mesozoic.

II — Correct: The gold deposits of Ghana have no local source rocks, so they are regarded as placer deposits derived from the Brazil plateau when Africa and South America lay side by side. Placer deposits are minerals concentrated by water in sediments. NCERT cites this as evidence from the Gulf of Guinea coast, supporting the idea that the two continents shared a drainage and geological history before drifting apart.

III — Correct: The Gondwana system of sediments in India, named after the Gondwana region of central India, contains coal, tillite and plant fossils. Its counterparts occur in India, South Africa, South America, Australia, Antarctica and Madagascar, six southern landmasses. The Gondwana sequence spans late Carboniferous to Jurassic. The tillite shows a widespread glaciation, which is best explained if these landmasses were joined near the South Pole. India's Gondwana beds hold most of its coal.
summary: The answer is (c): all three statements are accepted evidences of continental drift. Matching ancient rock belts across the Atlantic, the Ghana gold placer deposits linked to the Brazil plateau, and the Gondwana sediments found in six southern landmasses all point to continents once joined.
topic_notes: Continental drift theory was put forward by Alfred Wegener, a German meteorologist, in 1912. He proposed that all continents formed a single landmass, Pangaea, surrounded by the global ocean Panthalassa. About 200 million years ago Pangaea split into Laurasia (north) and Gondwanaland (south). Drift forces proposed were pole-fleeing force (due to Earth's rotation and equatorial bulge) and tidal force (Moon and Sun). Evidences: continental fit, rock-age similarity, tillite deposits, placer deposits, and fossils such as Mesosaurus (a freshwater reptile in South Africa and Brazil) and Glossopteris flora. Criticism: the forces were too weak to move continents. Later evidences led to new theories. Post-war studies of the ocean floor found mid-oceanic ridges, and Harry Hess proposed seafloor spreading in 1961. Palaeomagnetism and the magnetic striping on both sides of ridges (Vine and Matthews, 1963) supported it. In 1967 McKenzie, Parker and Morgan formulated plate tectonics, with seven major plates (Pacific, North American, South American, African, Eurasian, Indo-Australian, Antarctic) and several minor plates. Plate boundaries are divergent, convergent and transform. Convection currents in the mantle, as proposed by Arthur Holmes, are the driving mechanism. India moved north after separating from Gondwana, collided with Eurasia and raised the Himalayas, and the Deccan Traps formed as it passed over the Réunion hotspot. Possible next questions: Pangaea's breakup, plate boundaries, Wegener versus Hess, and the Gondwana coalfields.

question:
Consider the following statements :
Statement I : The amount of dust particles in the atmosphere is more in subtropical and temperate areas than in equatorial and polar regions.
Statement II : Subtropical and temperate areas have less dry winds. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct [ P.T.O
subject: Geography
detail: This question comes from the NCERT chapter on the composition and structure of the atmosphere. Dust particles (solid particles or aerosols) come from fine soil, smoke-soot, ash, pollen, sea salt, and meteoritic debris. They are concentrated in the lower atmosphere. NCERT states that dust is more abundant in subtropical and temperate regions because of dry winds there, and less abundant in equatorial and polar regions. The subtropical belts (about 20-35 degrees N and S) lie under descending dry air of the high-pressure zones. They contain the major deserts: the Sahara, Arabia, Thar, Australian deserts, and Kalahari. Dry, loose soil and strong winds lift large quantities of dust. Temperate interiors, such as the loess areas, also have dry winds. The equatorial region is humid and rainy, so rain washes dust out. Polar areas have little loose, dry soil because of ice cover. Dust acts as hygroscopic nuclei for condensation, and it causes scattering that produces the colours of sunrise, sunset and the sky. Elimination: Statement I is true, and Statement II contradicts the NCERT reasoning, so only (c) fits.
explanations: Wrong. This option treats Statement II as correct and as the explanation. Statement II is factually wrong, because the dry winds in these areas are more, not less.
Wrong. This option also treats Statement II as correct. Statement II is not correct, so the option fails whether or not it explains Statement I.
Correct. Statement I matches NCERT, and Statement II is false because subtropical and temperate areas have more dry winds, which cause more dust.
Wrong. This option calls Statement I incorrect, but Statement I is correct. It also treats Statement II as correct, which is false.
keyfact: Dust is most abundant in subtropical and temperate areas because dry winds there lift loose soil, and equatorial and polar areas have less dust.
option_notes: Both statements correct with II as the explanation. This is the standard assertion-reason format in UPSC. It would hold only if dry winds were fewer and that fewer winds led to more dust, which makes no physical sense. Dust generation needs dry, loose soil and strong winds. The real explanation is more dry winds in the subtropics and temperate interiors.

Both statements correct but II is not the explanation. This format is used when both statements are true yet unconnected. Here Statement II is factually false, because the dry subtropical belts and desert-bordering temperate areas have more dry winds. So the option is invalid even though the format is common.

Statement I correct and Statement II incorrect. This is the correct answer. Dust is more abundant in subtropical and temperate regions because of dry winds, deserts and loose soils. Equatorial regions are humid and rainy, and polar regions are icy, so both have less dust. Statement II reverses the actual condition.

Statement I incorrect and Statement II correct. This is the reverse of the true position. Statement I is correct, since dust is indeed more in subtropical and temperate areas, and Statement II is wrong, since dry winds are more there. UPSC often uses reversed options like this as distractors.
related: Atmosphere composition by volume: N2 78%, O2 21%, Ar 0.93%, CO2 about 0.04%.
Water vapour decreases from equator to poles and with altitude.
Dust and aerosols act as hygroscopic nuclei for condensation.
The Harmattan is a dry, dusty northeasterly wind from the Sahara toward the West African coast.
Loo is a hot, dry summer wind in northwest India and Pakistan.
Foehn and Chinook are warm, dry downslope winds on the leeward side of mountains.
The ozone layer lies in the stratosphere at about 15-35 km.
Troposphere is thickest at the equator (about 18 km) and thinnest at the poles (about 8 km).
statements: 1 — Correct: NCERT says dust is more abundant in subtropical and temperate regions than in equatorial and polar regions. Dust (aerosol) particles come from soil, smoke, ash, pollen, sea salt and meteors. They are concentrated in the lower troposphere. They serve as hygroscopic nuclei around which water vapour condenses to form clouds and fog, and they scatter light, producing red sunsets and the blue sky. Hot deserts at 20-35 degrees (the Sahara, Thar, Arabia) are major sources. Dust storms such as the Harmattan and Saharan dust travel across oceans. Equatorial rain and polar ice reduce the amount of dust.

2 — Incorrect: Subtropical and temperate areas have more dry winds, not fewer, and this explains the larger dust load. The subtropical high-pressure belts have descending, dry air and many deserts. Examples of dry winds are the Loo in the Indo-Gangetic plain, the Harmattan from the Sahara toward West Africa, the Sirocco and Khamsin from North Africa, and the Foehn and Chinook in temperate mountain regions. The equatorial belt is humid with convectional rain, and polar areas are cold and ice-covered. These conditions mean little dry-wind lifting of dust there.
summary: The answer is (c). Statement I is correct because dust is more abundant over subtropical and temperate latitudes than over equatorial and polar regions. Statement II is incorrect because these areas, especially the subtropical belts, have more dry winds, not fewer, and that dryness is part of why dust is abundant.
topic_notes: Atmospheric composition: Nitrogen is about 78%, oxygen about 21%, argon about 0.93%, and carbon dioxide about 0.04% by volume. Water vapour varies from 0 to 4% and decreases from the equator toward the poles. Dust, or solid particles, includes smoke, soot, ash, pollen, sea salt and fine soil. It is found mainly in the lower troposphere and is concentrated in subtropical and temperate regions because of dry winds. Dust is much less abundant in equatorial regions, where rain removes it, and in polar regions. Roles of dust and aerosols: they act as hygroscopic nuclei for condensation and cloud formation; they scatter and reflect sunlight, causing the blue sky and the red colours at sunrise and sunset; and they influence visibility, health and climate. Large volcanic eruptions can inject aerosols into the stratosphere and cool the globe, as with Pinatubo in 1991. Ozone is concentrated in the stratosphere at about 15-35 km and absorbs ultraviolet radiation. Layers of the atmosphere are the troposphere (about 8 km at the poles and 18 km at the equator), the stratosphere, the mesosphere, the thermosphere (which holds the ionosphere), and the exosphere. Dry winds and dust events include the Loo, Harmattan, Sirocco, Khamsin, Simoom, and Foehn and Chinook winds. Pressure belts: the subtropical highs lie at about 30 degrees, and the Sahara and other hot deserts lie under them. Likely angles for the future are particulate matter PM2.5 and PM10, the Air Quality Index, dust storms in Rajasthan and the Thar, Saharan dust crossing the Atlantic, and the role of aerosols in cloud seeding and climate change.

ocr: Consider the following statements : Statement I : In January, in the Northern Hemisphere, the isotherms bend equatorward while crossing the landmasses, and poleward while crossing the oceans. Statement II : In January, the air over the oceans is warmer than that over the landmasses in the Northern Hemisphere. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements? (a) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I (b) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I (c) Statement I is correct but
subject: Geography
detail: Isotherms are lines joining places with equal temperature (reduced to sea level). They would run parallel to latitudes if the Earth's surface were uniform, but the unequal heating of land and water deflects them. Water has a high specific heat, mixes by currents and waves, and allows heat to penetrate deeper, so it heats and cools slowly. Land has a low specific heat, is opaque, and heats and cools quickly. In January (Northern Hemisphere winter) the land loses heat rapidly and becomes colder than the sea at the same latitude. Oceans hold the stored heat and are further warmed by warm currents such as the Gulf Stream/North Atlantic Drift and the Kuroshio. Hence warm air over the oceans pushes isotherms poleward, for example over the North Atlantic off Norway, while cold continental interiors such as Siberia and Canada pull isotherms equatorward. In July the pattern reverses. The elimination logic is as follows. Statement II is factually true. It is also the direct cause of the bending in Statement I, so (b) fails. (c) and (d) deny a true statement.
explanations: Correct. Both statements are true, and the warmer ocean air of Statement II is the reason the isotherms bend poleward over oceans and equatorward over land in Statement I.
Wrong. Although both statements are correct, Statement II does explain Statement I, because the land-sea temperature contrast is the cause of the bending.
Wrong. Statement II is correct, since oceans are warmer than land in the Northern Hemisphere in January.
Wrong. Statement I is correct, because the bending of isotherms is exactly as described. Only a reversed description would be wrong, and that applies to July.
keyfact: In January in the Northern Hemisphere, isotherms bend equatorward over cold land and poleward over warm oceans, because water heats and cools more slowly than land.
option_notes: Both statements correct and II explains I is the standard 'reasoning' option in UPSC assertion-type questions. It applies when the second statement states the cause of the first. Here, differential heating and cooling of land and water explains the isotherm pattern. This is the official answer.

Both statements correct but II does not explain I applies when the two statements are true but independent. For example, 'The Equator receives the most insolation' and 'Doldrums are a low-wind belt' would be related but not causal. It is the commonest trap option in this format, but here the link is causal, so it is wrong.

Statement I correct but II incorrect would hold if the isotherm description were true but the oceans were colder than land. In January the opposite holds. In July the Northern Hemisphere oceans are cooler than the land, so Statement II would be wrong in that month. The month matters.

Statement I incorrect but II correct would apply if the isotherm bending were reversed, as in July in the Northern Hemisphere, when isotherms bend poleward over land and equatorward over oceans. In January the description in Statement I is accurate, so this option fails.
related: Normal lapse rate is about 6.5°C per 1000 m, also called vertical temperature gradient.
Isotherms are lines joining places of equal temperature, reduced to sea level.
In July, Northern Hemisphere isotherms bend poleward over land and equatorward over oceans.
Thermal equator lies on average near 5°N and shifts with the apparent movement of the Sun.
Gulf Stream and North Atlantic Drift keep north-west European ports ice-free in winter.
Earth's albedo is about 35% of incoming insolation.
Southern Hemisphere isotherms are more parallel because of the dominance of oceans.
Verkhoyansk and Oymyakon in Siberia record the greatest annual range of temperature in the Northern Hemisphere.
statements: I — Correct: In January in the Northern Hemisphere, isotherms bend equatorward over the landmasses (cold land) and poleward over the oceans (warm water). Isotherms join places with the same temperature, usually reduced to sea level to remove altitude effects. The bending shows the land-sea contrast. It is most striking in the North Atlantic, where the Gulf Stream and North Atlantic Drift carry heat towards Norway, and over the cold Siberian and Canadian interiors. In the Southern Hemisphere, which has much more ocean, isotherms are far more parallel to the latitudes. In July the bending reverses: isotherms bend poleward over land and equatorward over oceans.

II — Correct: In January the air over Northern Hemisphere oceans is warmer than over the landmasses at the same latitude. Water has a high specific heat, so it warms and cools slowly. Heat penetrates deep into water through mixing, currents and waves, and the stored heat is released slowly in winter. Land is opaque, has a low specific heat and cools quickly, producing intense winter highs such as the Siberian High. Warm ocean currents (Gulf Stream, Kuroshio) add to oceanic warmth. This is why coastal places have a maritime climate with a low annual range and continental interiors have a high annual range, as at Verkhoyansk.
summary: The answer is (a): both statements are correct and Statement II explains Statement I. In January the oceans in the Northern Hemisphere are warmer than the landmasses at the same latitude, so isotherms bend poleward over oceans and equatorward over continents.
topic_notes: Distribution of temperature is controlled by latitude, altitude, distance from the sea (continentality), ocean currents, prevailing winds, cloud cover and relief. Isotherms are lines joining places of equal temperature, usually reduced to sea level to remove the altitude effect. They would run east-west if the Earth's surface were uniform. Land-sea contrast makes them bend. In January in the Northern Hemisphere, isotherms bend equatorward over land (cold continents) and poleward over oceans (warm currents). In July, isotherms bend poleward over land and equatorward over oceans. The Southern Hemisphere has more ocean, so its isotherms are more regular and parallel, and the deviation is smaller. Water has a high specific heat, is transparent, and mixes by currents, so it warms and cools slowly. Land is opaque, has a low specific heat, and heats and cools quickly. The Gulf Stream and North Atlantic Drift keep north-west Europe warm, with ports such as Hammerfest and Murmansk staying ice-free. The Labrador and Oyashio cold currents cool eastern Canada and Japan's north-east. The coldest Northern Hemisphere regions in winter are Siberia (Verkhoyansk, Oymyakon) and Greenland, and the hottest in summer are the subtropical deserts. Annual range of temperature is highest in continental interiors and lowest in the equatorial oceans. Thermal equator is the line joining the highest mean temperature at each longitude. It moves north in July and south in January, and lies north of the geographic equator on average, near 5°N. Temperature inversion, lapse rate (about 6.5°C per km, the normal lapse rate), and heat budget (insolation 100 units, 35 reflected as albedo) are other related angles.

question:
Consider the following statements :
Statement I : In the context of effect of water on rocks, chalk is known as a very permeable rock whereas clay is known as quite an impermeable or least permeable rock.
Statement II : Chalk is porous and hence can absorb water. Statement III : Clay is not at all porous. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I
Both Statement II and Statement III are correct but only one of them explains Statement I Only one of the Statements II and
Ill is correct and that explains Statement I Neither Statement II nor State
subject: Geography
detail: Porosity and permeability are different properties. Porosity is the proportion of void space in a rock, which decides how much water it can hold. Permeability is how easily water flows through those voids, which depends on pore size, connectivity and fractures. Chalk is a soft, fine-grained limestone made of calcite from microscopic marine organisms (coccoliths). It is porous and also jointed, so it absorbs water and lets it percolate. This is why chalk forms good aquifers, for example in the London Basin and the North and South Downs. Clay is made of very fine particles (under 0.002 mm). Its total porosity can be high, often 40-70 percent, but the pores are so small that molecular attraction holds water tightly and blocks flow. So clay is an aquiclude, an impermeable layer. Statement III says clay is 'not at all porous', which is factually wrong, so it cannot explain Statement I. Statement II gives the right reason for chalk's permeability. Elimination: since III is false, options (a) and (b), which need both statements correct, fall. Option (d), which says neither is correct, fails because II is correct. That leaves (c).
explanations: (a) is wrong because it requires both II and III to be correct. III is false, since clay is porous but its pores are too small and unconnected to transmit water.
(b) is wrong because it also treats III as correct. Clay does have pores, so 'not at all porous' is incorrect.
(c) is correct. Only Statement II is true, and chalk's porosity and fissures explain why it is permeable, which is Statement I. Statement III is false.
(d) is wrong because Statement II is true: chalk is porous and absorbs water. So it is not the case that neither statement is correct.
keyfact: Porous does not mean permeable: clay is porous but nearly impermeable because its pores are tiny and unconnected, whereas chalk is porous and permeable.
option_notes: Option (a) says both II and III are correct and both explain I. This is the trap for students who equate impermeability with zero porosity. Clay in fact has high total porosity, often higher than sand, but its pores are microscopic. Water is held by surface tension and electrostatic forces and cannot flow through. A rock is called impermeable because of poor pore connectivity and small pore size, not because it has no pores.

Option (b) says both II and III are correct but only one explains I. It is still wrong because III is false. Remember that porosity is the capacity to store fluid, while permeability is the capacity to transmit it. Clay stores plenty of water but transmits very little. Sand and gravel have both high porosity and high permeability. Chalk has high porosity and, because of fissures, moderate to high permeability, which makes it a valuable aquifer.

Option (c), the correct option, says only one of II and III is correct and that it explains I. It is true because the porosity of chalk supports its permeability. In geology, aquifers are permeable water-bearing rocks such as chalk, sandstone and gravel. Aquicludes are impermeable layers such as clay and shale. Aquitards are leaky, low-permeability layers. This distinction is central to groundwater occurrence, springs and artesian wells.

Option (d) says neither II nor III is correct. It is wrong because chalk is porous and does absorb water. Chalk is a soft limestone with porosity commonly 30-50 percent. Its jointing also lets water percolate, which is why chalk downs have dry surfaces, few surface streams and a spring line at the foot of the escarpment where chalk meets impermeable clay. Chalk aquifers feed rivers such as the Thames and the Test.
related: Porosity is the capacity of a rock to store water, while permeability is its capacity to transmit water.
Clay has high porosity but very low permeability, so it acts as an aquiclude.
An aquifer is a permeable water-bearing rock such as sand, gravel, sandstone or chalk.
In an artesian well, water rises under pressure from a confined aquifer between impermeable layers.
Chalk is a Cretaceous biogenic limestone; the White Cliffs of Dover are chalk.
Limestone dissolves by carbonation, producing karst features such as sinkholes and caves.
A spring line forms at the base of a chalk escarpment where it meets impermeable clay.
The Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) is India's apex body for groundwater assessment.
statements: I — Correct: Chalk is a permeable rock and clay is impermeable or least permeable, which is the standard textbook view. Permeable rocks such as chalk, sandstone and limestone allow water to pass through. Impermeable rocks such as clay, shale and unfractured granite hold water at the surface or block its downward movement. Permeable rock above impermeable rock gives aquifers, springs and the spring line, and impermeable layers create surface drainage, ponds and marshes. Chalk escarpments are dry-topped, while clay vales are wet and drain by surface streams. Confined aquifers sit between two impermeable layers (aquicludes), and artesian wells draw from them.

II — Correct: Chalk is porous, so it absorbs water, and this explains why it is permeable. Chalk is a soft, white, fine-grained biogenic limestone made mostly of calcium carbonate from coccolithophore plates, laid down in the Cretaceous (the name comes from Latin creta, chalk). Famous exposures include the White Cliffs of Dover and the North and South Downs. It is also jointed, so water moves through both matrix and fissures. It has porosity of roughly 30-50 percent, although its small pore throats limit the flow through the matrix itself. Chalk aquifers supply much of south-east England's water. As a carbonate rock it is also slowly dissolved by carbonic acid, forming karst-like features.

III — Incorrect: Clay is porous, so 'not at all porous' is false. Clay is fine-grained sediment of hydrous aluminium silicate minerals such as kaolinite, illite and montmorillonite. Its particles are platy and under 0.002 mm. Total porosity is high, but the pores are microscopic and poorly connected, so permeability is extremely low. The key point is that high porosity does not mean high permeability. Clay swells when wet, which seals pores further. It is used in pottery, bricks, cement, and as liners for landfills and ponds. Wet clay holds a lot of water, which is why clay soils are waterlogged and slow to drain.
summary: The answer is (c). Only Statement II is correct, and it explains Statement I. Chalk is porous with well-connected pores and fissures, so it absorbs and transmits water. Clay is porous too, but its pores are extremely tiny and poorly connected, so water cannot pass through it. This makes Statement III wrong.
topic_notes: Rocks and water. Porosity is the percentage of a rock's volume that is empty space. Permeability is the ability of connected voids to transmit fluid. A rock can be porous without being permeable, as clay shows. Pumice and shale are other examples of this. Permeable rocks include sandstone, gravel, chalk, jointed limestone and fractured basalt. Impermeable rocks include clay, shale, slate and unfractured granite. Hydrogeological terms: aquifer (water-bearing, permeable), aquiclude (impermeable), aquitard (poorly permeable), water table (top of the saturated zone), confined aquifer and artesian well (water rises under pressure), and spring (water table meets the surface). Geomorphic effects: chalk and limestone areas have dry valleys, few surface streams and a spring line at the base of escarpments. Limestone dissolves by carbonation, producing karst features such as sinkholes, caves, stalactites and stalagmites. Clay-rich areas show surface runoff, high drainage density, waterlogging and gullying. Granite is impermeable but weathers by exfoliation and chemical decay along joints, giving tors and spheroidal weathering. Chalk is a Cretaceous biogenic limestone, and the Cretaceous period is named after it. Soil connection: clay soil has high water-holding capacity but poor drainage and aeration. Sandy soil drains fast, with low retention. Loam is the best balance. In India, the Deccan basalt is largely impermeable except at fractures and weathered zones, so its groundwater potential is limited. The alluvial Indo-Gangetic plain is the best aquifer region. Karst is found in Meghalaya, Chhattisgarh (Kutumsar) and Uttarakhand. Possible future angles: the types of weathering, groundwater recharge, artesian wells, soil texture and the Central Ground Water Board.

ocr: Consider the following statements : Without the atmosphere, & temperature would be well below freezing point everywhere on the Earth’s surface. Heat absorbed and trapped by the atmosphere maintains our planet’s average temperature. Atmosphere’s gases, like carbon Ill. dioxide, are particularly good at absorbing and trapping radiation. Which of the statements given above are correct? I and III only (a) I and II only (b) I, Il and Ill (c) II and III only (d)
subject: Geography
detail: The question tests the natural greenhouse effect. Solar radiation is mostly shortwave and passes through the atmosphere. About 30% is reflected (planetary albedo, roughly 0.3), and the rest is absorbed by the surface and atmosphere. Earth re-emits this energy as longwave infrared radiation. Greenhouse gases (water vapour, CO2, CH4, N2O, O3, CFCs) absorb and re-radiate part of it back toward the surface. This keeps the average surface temperature near +15°C. Without the atmosphere, the effective radiative equilibrium temperature would be about -18°C (some texts say -19°C), so the surface would be well below freezing everywhere. This is why statement I is correct. Statement II describes the heat-trapping mechanism and is correct. Statement III is correct because triatomic gases like CO2 absorb infrared strongly, while N2 and O2 are largely transparent to it. Elimination logic: the three statements are mutually consistent and each is a textbook fact. Once you confirm any two are correct, only (c) can be right, because (a), (b) and (d) each wrongly exclude one of them. The natural greenhouse effect is essential for life. Concern arises only from the enhanced greenhouse effect caused by human emissions.
explanations: (a) I and III only is wrong because it leaves out statement II. Statement II is correct, since the atmosphere does absorb and trap heat and thereby maintains the average temperature.
(b) I and II only is wrong because it leaves out statement III. Gases like CO2 are indeed particularly good at absorbing and trapping infrared radiation.
(c) I, II and III is correct. All three are textbook statements of the natural greenhouse effect, and this matches the official answer.
(d) II and III only is wrong because it leaves out statement I. Without the atmosphere, the surface temperature would be about -18°C, well below freezing.
keyfact: The natural greenhouse effect, via CO2 and other infrared-absorbing gases, lifts Earth's average temperature from about -18°C to about 15°C.
option_notes: Option (a) pairs statements I and III. It is a partial answer that treats the temperature effect and the gas property as correct while ignoring the mechanism statement. Statement I states the consequence of having no atmosphere, with a baseline of roughly -18°C. Statement III states a property of greenhouse gases, which absorb infrared. Such partial combinations are common UPSC distractors. Always verify each statement independently rather than guessing from the pattern of options.

Option (b) pairs statements I and II. It covers the no-atmosphere temperature fact and the heat-trapping role of the atmosphere but excludes the statement about gases. Statement III is nonetheless factually sound. Triatomic and more complex molecules such as CO2, H2O, CH4 and N2O have vibrational modes that absorb infrared. Diatomic N2 and O2 do not absorb it significantly. This property is why they are classed as greenhouse gases.

Option (c) says all three statements are correct and is the official answer. It reflects the natural greenhouse effect. The atmosphere is largely transparent to shortwave solar radiation but absorbs longwave terrestrial radiation. This raises the surface temperature from about -18°C to about 15°C. The key distinction for exams is between the natural greenhouse effect, which is beneficial and necessary, and the enhanced greenhouse effect, which causes global warming.

Option (d) pairs statements II and III. It accepts the mechanism and the gas property but rejects the baseline temperature claim in statement I. That claim is correct. The calculated effective temperature of Earth without greenhouse warming is about 255 K, or -18°C, derived from the balance between absorbed solar energy and emitted radiation using the Stefan-Boltzmann law. The observed mean is about 288 K, or 15°C.
related: Without the greenhouse effect, Earth's average temperature would be about -18°C instead of about 15°C.
Water vapour is the most abundant greenhouse gas, and CO2 is the main driver of human-caused warming.
GWP over 100 years: CO2 = 1, CH4 about 28-30, N2O about 265-300.
The Montreal Protocol (1987) phases out ozone-depleting substances, and the Kigali Amendment (2016) targets HFCs.
The Paris Agreement (2015) aims to hold warming well below 2°C and pursue 1.5°C.
Earth's albedo is about 0.3, meaning about 30% of incoming solar radiation is reflected back to space.
The atmosphere is mostly N2 (78%) and O2 (21%), which are not greenhouse gases.
India's net-zero target is 2070, announced at COP26, Glasgow, in 2021.
statements: 1 — Correct: Without the atmosphere, Earth's surface temperature would be about -18°C, far below freezing, because the natural greenhouse effect would be absent. Earth's average surface temperature is about 15°C, so the greenhouse effect adds roughly 33°C of warming. The Moon has no atmosphere. Its day side reaches about 120°C and its night side falls to about -170°C, which shows how an atmosphere moderates temperature and reduces diurnal range. Venus, with a dense CO2 atmosphere, has a surface temperature of about 460°C or more.

2 — Correct: The atmosphere absorbs outgoing longwave radiation from the Earth and re-emits part of it downward. This maintains the planet's heat budget and average temperature. Incoming insolation is about 100 units. Roughly 35 units are reflected back (albedo), 14 are absorbed by the atmosphere, and 51 reach the surface. The surface returns this as terrestrial radiation, and the atmosphere's retention of heat balances the budget. The IPCC assesses how changes in greenhouse gases alter this balance, which is measured as radiative forcing in W/m². The Earth's heat budget is a standard UPSC topic.

3 — Correct: Greenhouse gases such as CO2, CH4, N2O, water vapour and ozone absorb infrared radiation well because of their molecular structure. Nitrogen and oxygen, which make up about 99% of dry air, do not absorb it significantly. CO2 is about 0.04% (over 420 ppm) of the atmosphere. Global warming potential (GWP) compares gases over a given period, usually 100 years. CO2 is the reference with a GWP of 1, methane is about 28-30, and N2O is about 265-300. SF6 and some HFCs have GWPs in the thousands or higher. Water vapour is the most abundant greenhouse gas and acts mainly as a feedback.
summary: The correct answer is (c): all three statements are correct. The atmosphere traps outgoing terrestrial (infrared) radiation through greenhouse gases such as CO2, water vapour, methane and N2O. This natural greenhouse effect keeps Earth's average surface temperature near 15°C instead of about -18°C.
topic_notes: The topic is the Earth's heat budget and the greenhouse effect. Solar radiation (insolation) is shortwave and peaks in visible wavelengths. Earth's terrestrial radiation is longwave infrared. The atmosphere is largely transparent to incoming shortwave radiation but absorbs outgoing longwave radiation. In the standard textbook budget, of 100 units of insolation, about 35 units are reflected (27 from clouds, 6 from the atmosphere by scattering, 2 from ice and snow), 14 are absorbed by the atmosphere, and 51 are absorbed by the surface. The surface radiates 51 units back, and the budget balances. Albedo is about 0.3, and the Earth's overall budget is balanced with no net gain or loss. The natural greenhouse effect raises the surface temperature by about 33°C. The main greenhouse gases are water vapour (the largest contributor to the natural effect), CO2, CH4, N2O, O3 and fluorinated gases (HFCs, PFCs, SF6, NF3). CO2 concentration has risen from about 280 ppm pre-industrial to over 420 ppm. Global warming potential (GWP) is measured relative to CO2. The IPCC (1988, by WMO and UNEP) assesses climate science. UNFCCC was adopted in 1992, the Kyoto Protocol in 1997, the Paris Agreement in 2015 (aiming to keep warming well below 2°C and pursue 1.5°C), and India's updated NDCs and its net-zero target for 2070 are linked topics. Other angles include ozone depletion (Montreal Protocol 1987, Kigali Amendment 2016 on HFCs), aerosols (which cool by reflecting sunlight), Earth's temperature zones, the lapse rate, and the role of the stratosphere. Planetary comparisons are also asked. Venus has a runaway greenhouse effect, Mars has a thin atmosphere, and the Moon has no atmosphere and hence extreme temperatures.

ocr: Consider the following statements about the Rashtriya Gokul Mission : It is important for the upliftment of i rural poor as majority of low producing indigenous animals are with small and marginal farmers and landless labourers. It was initiated to promote I. indigenous cattle and _ buffalo rearing and conservation in a scientific and holistic manner. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? I only (a) (b) II only Both I and II (c) Neither I nor II (a) [P.T.0.
subject: Economy
detail: The Rashtriya Gokul Mission was launched in December 2014 under the National Programme for Bovine Breeding and Dairy Development. It aims to develop and conserve indigenous bovine breeds in a scientific and holistic manner, enhance milk production and productivity, and make milk production more remunerative for farmers. Indigenous cattle and buffalo are largely reared by small and marginal farmers, landless labourers and women, so breed improvement directly supports rural livelihoods and nutrition. Key components include Gokul Grams (integrated indigenous cattle centres), the National Kamdhenu Breeding Centres, the Centres of Excellence, the National Bovine Genomic Centre, the High Genetic Merit bull programme, sex-sorted semen, IVF and embryo transfer, and the Pashu Sanjivani and e-Pashuhaat initiatives. The scheme is implemented through the State Implementing Agencies and is now part of the restructured Rashtriya Gokul Mission (2021-26) under the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying. Elimination logic: Statement I states the socio-economic rationale and is accurate. Statement II states the mission's objective and is accurate. Since both are correct, only (c) survives, and (a), (b) and (d) are eliminated.
explanations: (a) Wrong: it rejects Statement II, but the mission's objective is exactly the scientific and holistic conservation and development of indigenous cattle and buffalo.
(b) Wrong: it rejects Statement I, but the socio-economic rationale of benefiting small and marginal farmers, landless labourers and the rural poor is correct.
(c) Correct: both statements are accurate, one stating the socio-economic importance and the other the purpose of the mission.
(d) Wrong: it denies both statements, yet both are correct.
keyfact: Rashtriya Gokul Mission (Dec 2014) = scientific conservation and development of indigenous cattle and buffalo, benefiting small and marginal farmers and landless labourers.
option_notes: Option (a), 'I only', would mean that only the rural-poor rationale is valid. The rationale rests on the fact that livestock ownership in India is concentrated among small and marginal farmers and landless households. Livestock gives income, nutrition, draught power and risk cover. It contributes roughly 4-5% of national GDP and about 30% of agricultural GVA. It is wrong here because the mission's stated purpose is also correct.

Option (b), 'II only', would mean that only the objective is valid. The objective is to promote indigenous cattle and buffalo rearing and conservation. Indigenous cattle breeds include Gir, Sahiwal, Red Sindhi, Tharparkar and Rathi, and buffalo breeds include Murrah, Jaffrabadi and Nili-Ravi. It is wrong because the socio-economic rationale in Statement I is also correct.

Option (c), 'Both I and II', is the official answer. RGM is a central sector scheme under the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying). It was launched in 2014 and restructured for 2021-26. It conserves indigenous breeds, improves productivity, and benefits small farmers through breeding services at the farm gate. Its main tools are AI, sex-sorted semen, IVF and Gokul Grams.

Option (d), 'Neither I nor II', would mean both statements are false. That contradicts the scheme's guidelines, which stress the livelihood of marginal farmers and the conservation of native breeds. Such an option is typically a distractor in UPSC questions about government schemes whose descriptions are accurate paraphrases of official objectives.
related: RGM was launched in December 2014 under NPBBDD.
Nodal agency: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying.
Gokul Grams are integrated indigenous cattle centres.
e-Pashuhaat is a portal for bovine germplasm.
Rashtriya Kamdhenu Aayog was constituted in 2019.
India is the world's largest milk producer.
NDDB was established in 1965 at Anand; Operation Flood began in 1970.
Gir, Sahiwal, Red Sindhi, Tharparkar and Rathi are indigenous cattle breeds.
statements: I — Correct: Most low-producing indigenous animals are held by small and marginal farmers, landless labourers and women, so improving them uplifts the rural poor. Livestock is a key source of supplementary income, nutrition and insurance against crop failure. India has the largest livestock population in the world and is the largest milk producer (about 24% of global output). Dairying employs many women. Indigenous breeds are hardy, disease-resistant and suited to local climates, but their productivity is low, which is why genetic upgradation under RGM matters.

II — Correct: RGM was initiated to conserve and develop indigenous bovine breeds scientifically and holistically. It was launched in December 2014 under the National Programme for Bovine Breeding and Dairy Development. It aims to increase milk production and productivity, propagate high-genetic-merit indigenous bulls, distribute disease-free bulls for natural service, and promote the use of AI. Gokul Grams are established as integrated indigenous cattle centres. The mission also covers buffalo development and it is implemented through the State Livestock Development Boards. It was restructured and continued for 2021-26 with a larger outlay.
summary: The answer is (c) Both I and II. The Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM) targets conservation and scientific development of indigenous bovine breeds, and because most low-producing indigenous animals are held by small and marginal farmers and landless labourers, it is important for the rural poor.
topic_notes: Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM) was launched in December 2014 as part of the National Programme for Bovine Breeding and Dairy Development (NPBBDD). It was continued and restructured for 2021-26 with an outlay of about Rs 2,400 crore. The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying is the nodal agency. Objectives include the development and conservation of indigenous breeds, genetic upgradation of the non-descript cattle population, enhancing milk production and productivity, and making dairying remunerative. Components: Gokul Grams (integrated indigenous cattle centres), National Kamdhenu Breeding Centres in Andhra Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, the National Bovine Genomic Centre for Indigenous Breeds (NBGC-IB), the Indigenous Breeds Genomic Chip, sex-sorted semen, IVF and embryo transfer, and e-Pashuhaat, a portal linking breeders and farmers. Rashtriya Kamdhenu Aayog was set up in 2019 for conservation and protection of cows. Related schemes: the National Livestock Mission, the National Programme for Dairy Development, the Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF), the Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme, the Dairy Processing and Infrastructure Development Fund, and the National Animal Disease Control Programme for foot-and-mouth disease and brucellosis. Other facts: India is the world's largest milk producer, and the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB), Anand, was founded in 1965 by Verghese Kurien (Operation Flood from 1970). The 20th Livestock Census (2019) counted about 303 million bovines. Indigenous breeds include Gir (Gujarat), Sahiwal (Punjab), Red Sindhi, Tharparkar and Rathi. UPSC may ask about breed-to-state matches, scheme-to-ministry matches, or the institutions involved.

question:
Consider the following statements :
Statement I : Studies indicate that carbon dioxide emissions from cement industry account for more than 5% of global carbon emissions.
Statement II : Silica-bearing clay is mixed with limestone while manufacturing cement. Statement III : Limestone is converted into lime during clinker production for cement manufacturing. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I
Both Statement II and Statement III are correct but only one of them explains Statement I
Only one of the Statements II and Ill is correct and that explains Statement I
Neither Statement II nor Statement Ill is correct
subject: Environment
detail: Cement is made by grinding limestone (calcium carbonate) with clay, shale or other silica-, alumina- and iron-bearing materials into a raw meal. The meal is heated in a rotary kiln to about 1450 degrees C. At roughly 800-900 degrees C, calcination occurs: CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2. The lime then reacts with silica, alumina and iron oxide at higher temperatures to form clinker (alite, belite, aluminate, ferrite). Clinker is ground with about 5% gypsum to control setting time, giving Ordinary Portland Cement. Cement accounts for about 7-8% of global CO2 emissions, so 'more than 5%' is correct. About 60% of the emissions are process emissions from calcination, and the remaining 30-40% come from fuel burned to heat the kiln. So Statement III directly explains the high emissions. Statement II is true but is only the raw-material mix. The clay supplies silica, not CO2, so it does not explain the emissions. Option (a) fails because both do not explain Statement I. Option (c) fails because both statements are correct. Option (d) fails because both are correct. Hence (b).
explanations: Wrong. Both II and III are correct, but Statement II (clay mixing) does not explain CO2 emissions. Only calcination in III does.
Correct. Both II and III are factually correct, and only III explains the high CO2 share in I, because limestone calcination releases CO2.
Wrong. It claims only one of II and III is correct, but both are correct.
Wrong. It says neither is correct, but both statements are accurate descriptions of cement manufacture.
keyfact: Cement CO2 is mostly from calcination of limestone (CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2) in clinker making; clay supplies silica but does not explain the emissions.
option_notes: Option (a) says both II and III explain I. This would be true only if clay mixing emitted CO2. Clay supplies silica and alumina and adds no process CO2. The idea behind it, that raw materials drive emissions, is only half right: carbonate raw material (limestone) matters, but clay does not.

Option (b), the correct one, treats II and III as true but only III as the explanation. It reflects the two-source emission structure in cement: process emissions from calcination (about 60%) and fuel combustion (about 40%). Cement is therefore a hard-to-abate sector, with major net-zero routes being CCUS, blended cements and alternative fuels.

Option (c) says only one of II and III is correct. In fact, both are true. Clay (silica-bearing) is blended with limestone, and limestone is calcined to lime during clinkering. A student who doubts II may confuse it with the later addition of gypsum, which controls setting and is not part of the raw mix.

Option (d) says neither II nor III is correct. This is wrong. Portland cement chemistry involves lime, silica, alumina and iron oxide. Clinker is a sintered product formed at about 1450 degrees C in a rotary kiln. Clinker is not the same as cement, which is clinker ground with gypsum.
related: Cement accounts for roughly 7-8% of global CO2 emissions.
Calcination: CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2, the main process emission.
Gypsum (3-5%) is added to clinker to control setting time.
Clinker is formed at about 1450 degrees C in a rotary kiln.
LC3 (limestone calcined clay cement) can cut clinker use and emissions.
India is the world's second-largest cement producer after China.
Fly ash and slag are used to make Portland Pozzolana and Portland Slag Cement.
Cement is a hard-to-abate sector; CCUS is a key decarbonisation tool.
statements: 1 — Correct: Cement is estimated to contribute about 7-8% of global anthropogenic CO2, which is above 5%. It is one of the largest industrial emitters, after power and alongside steel. Roughly 0.6-0.9 tonne of CO2 is released per tonne of cement. India is the second-largest cement producer after China. Emissions come from calcination (about 60%) and from fuel combustion. Decarbonisation options include blended cements (fly ash, slag), alternative fuels, clinker substitution, and carbon capture.

2 — Correct: Limestone supplies calcium, while clay, shale or sand supplies silica, alumina and iron oxide. They are crushed and blended in about a 3:1 ratio into raw meal. This composition is needed to form calcium silicates, the compounds that give cement its strength. Clay is an aluminosilicate, which is why it is called silica-bearing. This step does not itself release CO2. Cement hardens by hydration, not by drying. Gypsum is added later.

3 — Correct: In the kiln, limestone (CaCO3) is calcined to quicklime (CaO) with CO2 released. The lime then fuses with silica, alumina and iron oxide into nodules called clinker at about 1450 degrees C. Clinker is cooled and ground with gypsum to make Portland cement. This process emission is unavoidable without carbon capture or limestone substitution. It is the main reason the cement industry is classed as hard-to-abate, and it explains Statement I.
summary: The answer is (b). Statement I (cement CO2 above 5% of global emissions) is correct, as are Statements II and III. Only Statement III explains the emissions: calcination of limestone into lime releases CO2. Mixing silica-bearing clay with limestone is a raw-material step and does not itself produce CO2.
topic_notes: Cement manufacture has four stages: quarrying and crushing of limestone, raw meal preparation (limestone about 75-80% plus clay, shale or sand, with iron ore or bauxite as correctives), pyroprocessing, and finish grinding. In pyroprocessing, the meal passes through a preheater and then a rotary kiln. Calcination at 800-900 degrees C produces lime and CO2, and clinkering at 1400-1450 degrees C forms the main compounds: alite C3S, belite C2S, C3A and C4AF. Clinker is cooled and ground with about 3-5% gypsum, which retards flash setting. Types of cement include OPC (grades 33, 43 and 53), Portland Pozzolana Cement (with fly ash), Portland Slag Cement and white cement. Emissions: about 0.9 tonne of CO2 per tonne of clinker, with about 60% from process emissions and the rest from fuel and electricity. Globally the sector accounts for about 7-8% of CO2. India is the second-largest producer, and its cement intensity is lower than the global average because of high blended-cement use. Decarbonisation routes are lower clinker-to-cement ratio, fly ash and slag blending, alternative fuels and raw materials (co-processing waste), waste heat recovery, carbon capture, utilisation and storage, and new binders such as LC3 (limestone calcined clay cement). Policy: PAT scheme under the Bureau of Energy Efficiency, the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme under the Energy Conservation Act amendment, and the Global Cement and Concrete Association's net-zero roadmap. Other industries UPSC may link: steel (blast furnace), aluminium, fertiliser (ammonia), and green hydrogen.

question:
Consider the following statements :
Statement I : At the 28th United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP28), India refrained from signing the Declaration on Climate and Health’.
Statement II : The COP28 Declaration on Climate and Health is a binding declaration; and if signed, it becomes mandatory to decarbonize health sector. Statement III : If India’s health sector is decarbonized, the resilience of its health-care system may _ be compromised. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement II and Statement Til are correct and both of them explain Statement I
Both Statement II and Statement Ill are correct but only one of them explains Statement I
Only one of the Statements II and Ill is correct and that explains Statement I
Neither Statement II nor Statement Ill is correct
subject: Environment
detail: At COP28 in Dubai (30 Nov to 12 Dec 2023), the UAE presidency with WHO launched the COP28 UAE Declaration on Climate and Health on 3 Dec 2023, the first health-focused declaration at a COP. About 120+ countries endorsed it. It commits signatories to build climate-resilient, sustainable, low-carbon health systems, to include health in their NDCs and adaptation plans, and to increase finance for climate and health. India did not sign. Its stated concern was that the declaration could push the health sector toward decarbonization targets, which would conflict with the need to expand health infrastructure and could limit its development space and the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities (CBDR). The official key (c) treats only one of II and III as correct and as explaining I. Elimination: (d) fails because the official answer accepts one statement as correct. (a) and (b) fail because both II and III cannot be accepted together. Between II and III, the key accepts II as the explanation for India's refusal. Note that the declaration is in fact voluntary and non-binding, so this question rests on the official key.
explanations: (a) is wrong because Statement III is not accepted as correct by the official key, so both II and III cannot be correct and explain I.
(b) is wrong because it also needs both II and III to be correct, but only one of them is accepted.
(c) is right: exactly one of II and III is correct (II), and it explains why India refrained from signing.
(d) is wrong because the official key accepts one of the two statements as correct, so it is not true that neither is.
keyfact: India did not sign the COP28 Declaration on Climate and Health (3 Dec 2023), fearing decarbonization pressure on its health sector; the official answer is (c).
option_notes: Option (a) says both statements are correct and both explain I. It would imply that decarbonization compromises resilience, a claim the declaration itself rejects, since it ties low-carbon and resilient health systems together. The WHO Operational Framework (2023) supports building climate-resilient and low-carbon systems at the same time. This is why the option is rejected in the official key.

Option (b) says both statements are correct but only one explains I. It is wrong because III is not accepted as correct. Such options are typical of UPSC's multi-statement format in which the relation between statements is tested alongside their truth. The declaration was backed by WHO, the UAE presidency and over 120 countries, including many European and developing nations.

Option (c) is the official answer. Only Statement II is accepted as correct, and it explains India's non-signing: the concern that the declaration would pressure the health sector to decarbonize. India's stand at COP28 was grounded in CBDR, equity and development needs. India also did not endorse the Global Renewables and Energy Efficiency Pledge, which aimed to triple renewables by 2030.

Option (d) says neither II nor III is correct. It is wrong under the official key, which accepts II. Although in practice the declaration is non-binding and voluntary, UPSC's key treats the statement as the explanation. Remember that COP decisions are adopted by consensus, while declarations are voluntary and signed by countries individually.
related: COP28 was held in Dubai, UAE, from 30 Nov to 12 Dec 2023, with Sultan Al Jaber as president.
The COP28 Declaration on Climate and Health was launched on 3 Dec 2023 by the UAE presidency and WHO.
India declared a net-zero target for 2070 at COP26 in Glasgow (2021).
The Loss and Damage Fund was operationalised on the first day of COP28, with the World Bank as interim host.
India proposed to host COP33 in 2028.
NPCCHH, the National Programme on Climate Change and Human Health, was launched in 2019.
The Global Stocktake is conducted every five years under Article 14 of the Paris Agreement.
COP29 was held in Baku, Azerbaijan, in 2024.
statements: 1 — Correct: India did not sign the declaration at COP28. The COP28 UAE Declaration on Climate and Health was announced on 3 Dec 2023 by the UAE presidency and WHO, and it was the first COP declaration devoted to health. Roughly 120 countries endorsed it, and it calls for climate-resilient and low-carbon health systems, health in NDCs, and more finance. India and China were among the large emitters that did not sign. India's concern was about the implications for its health sector and development needs.

2 — Correct (as per the official key): It is the statement accepted as explaining India's non-signing. India saw the declaration as potentially obliging decarbonization of health systems. In reality, COP declarations are political and voluntary, but the key treats this as the explanatory statement. Health-sector emissions are about 4.6 to 5% of global emissions. WHO and Health Care Without Harm have pushed for net-zero health systems, and the UK and the NHS set a net-zero target of 2040 for direct emissions. India's health system is still expanding.

3 — Incorrect: As per the official key, this statement is not accepted as correct. Decarbonizing health care does not inherently compromise resilience, since the declaration itself links low-carbon with climate-resilient health systems through solar-powered clinics, efficient cold chains and green buildings. Climate-resilient health care is a WHO priority under the Operational Framework for Building Climate Resilient and Low Carbon Health Systems (2023). India's National Programme on Climate Change and Human Health (NPCCHH, 2019) is the main domestic programme.
summary: The answer is (c). Statement I is correct: India did not sign the COP28 Declaration on Climate and Health. Statement II is the correct one among II and III in the official key, and it explains India's refusal: the declaration was perceived as binding or pressuring the health sector to decarbonize. Statement III is treated as incorrect.
topic_notes: COP28 was held at Expo City, Dubai, from 30 Nov to 12 Dec 2023 under UAE presidency (Sultan Al Jaber). Its key outcome was the first Global Stocktake (GST) under the Paris Agreement, with the UAE Consensus calling for transitioning away from fossil fuels in energy systems in a just, orderly and equitable manner to achieve net zero by 2050. The Loss and Damage Fund was operationalised on day one, with the World Bank as interim host, and initial pledges of about 700 million US dollars. The Global Renewables and Energy Efficiency Pledge aimed to triple renewable capacity to at least 11,000 GW and double energy efficiency improvements by 2030; India did not sign it. The Declaration on Climate and Health (3 Dec 2023) was the first health-focused declaration. Other COP28 initiatives include the Declaration on Sustainable Agriculture, Resilient Food Systems and Climate Action (about 134 countries), the Global Cooling Pledge, the Oil and Gas Decarbonization Charter, and the Declaration on Hydrogen. India proposed the Green Credit Initiative at COP28 and offered to host COP33 in 2028. Health and climate links: WHO calls climate change the greatest health threat; the health sector accounts for about 4.6% of global emissions. India's relevant programmes include NPCCHH under the National Health Mission and the National Action Plan on Climate Change, India's NDC update (2022) with 45% emissions-intensity reduction by 2030 and 50% non-fossil electric capacity, and the 2070 net-zero target announced at COP26. Next COPs are COP29 in Baku (2024, the New Collective Quantified Goal on finance) and COP30 in Belém, Brazil (2025).

question:
Consider the following statements :
Statement I : Scientific studies suggest that a shift is taking place in the Earth’s rotation and axis.
Statement II : Solar flares and associated coronal mass ejections bombarded the Earth’s outermost atmosphere with tremendous amount of energy. Statement III : As the Earth’s polar ice melts, the water tends to move towards the equator. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I
Both Statement II and Statement Til are correct but only one of them explains Statement I
Only one of the Statements Il and Ill is correct and that explains Statement I
Neither Statement II nor Statement Ill is correct 15 [ P.T.O
subject: Science & Tech
detail: Earth's rotation axis and spin rate change slightly because of mass redistribution, a process called polar motion and length-of-day variation. Studies, for example a 2023 paper in Geophysical Research Letters and NASA/JPL work, show that melting of Greenland, Antarctic and glacier ice, together with groundwater pumping, has moved mass from high latitudes towards the equator and shifted the rotational pole by several centimetres to metres per year. This works like a skater extending their arms: mass moving to the equator increases the moment of inertia, which slows rotation slightly and lengthens the day by milliseconds. Solar flares are sudden bursts of radiation from the Sun, and coronal mass ejections (CMEs) are ejections of plasma and magnetic field. They hit the magnetosphere and upper atmosphere (thermosphere and ionosphere), causing geomagnetic storms, auroras, radio blackouts and satellite drag. Statement II is therefore factually true, but these effects do not alter the rotation or axis of the solid Earth. Elimination: (a) and (c) wrongly say II explains I. (d) wrongly says that II and III are not both correct. This leaves (b).
explanations: (a) Wrong: Statement II is correct, but it does not explain Statement I, so 'both explain' fails.
(b) Correct: Both II and III are true facts, and only III (ice-melt mass redistribution) explains the shift in rotation and axis.
(c) Wrong: It says only one of II and III is correct, but both are correct; it also reaches a conclusion that rests on that false premise.
(d) Wrong: It says neither II nor III is correct, but both are factually accurate.
keyfact: Polar ice melt moves water towards the equator and shifts Earth's rotation and axis, whereas solar flares and CMEs only disturb the upper atmosphere and magnetosphere.
option_notes: Option (a) claims that both II and III explain I. The distinction matters because solar activity is a space-weather phenomenon. Its effects are on the magnetosphere, ionosphere, satellites, communication and power grids, not on Earth's axis. Mass redistribution on Earth, such as ice melt, groundwater pumping and dam impoundment, is what changes the spin and the pole position. UPSC often builds statement-explanation questions on such cause-effect traps.

Option (b) is the correct choice. It holds that II and III are both true facts but only III explains I. It reflects the standard distinction between space-weather effects (auroras, geomagnetic storms, radio blackouts) and geophysical effects on rotation (polar motion, change in length of day). Examples of the latter include ice melt, groundwater loss, the 2004 Sumatra earthquake (which shortened the day by microseconds) and the 2011 Tohoku earthquake (which shifted the axis by about 17 cm).

Option (c) says only one of II and III is correct. This would be the right type of answer if one statement were false. Here that is not the case, since both statements are true. A common trap is to assume solar activity is irrelevant and therefore 'incorrect'. Statements must be judged on their own accuracy first, and then on whether they explain the other statement.

Option (d) says neither II nor III is correct. It would only apply if both were false. Solar flares and CMEs do bombard the upper atmosphere, as seen in the May 2024 geomagnetic storm, and polar melt water does redistribute towards the equator. Both are established scientific facts, so (d) fails.
related: Aditya-L1 was launched on 2 September 2023 and reached its halo orbit around Sun-Earth L1 on 6 January 2024.
Solar flares are classified A, B, C, M and X, and X is the strongest class.
CMEs take roughly 1 to 3 days to reach Earth and can cause geomagnetic storms.
The Carrington Event of 1859 was the most intense recorded geomagnetic storm.
Melting ice moves mass to the equator, which slows Earth's spin and lengthens the day.
The Chandler wobble has a period of about 433 days.
The IERS decides on leap seconds, based on Earth rotation data.
Milankovitch cycles are eccentricity (~100,000 years), obliquity (41,000 years) and precession (~26,000 years).
statements: 1 — Correct: Studies show that the Earth's rotation and axis are shifting. This is measured as polar motion, with the pole drifting about 10 cm per year in recent decades, and as small changes in the length of the day. Causes include ice melt, groundwater extraction, mantle and core processes, and large earthquakes. The International Earth Rotation and Reference Systems Service (IERS) monitors these changes. Leap seconds are linked to variations in rotation. The Chandler wobble is a natural wobble with a period of about 433 days. Milankovitch cycles are much slower changes in axial tilt (about 22.1° to 24.5°), precession and eccentricity.

2 — Correct but not explanatory: Solar flares and CMEs do release huge amounts of energy that hit the outer atmosphere. Flares are sudden bursts of electromagnetic radiation, and CMEs are huge plasma clouds that take 1 to 3 days to reach Earth. They cause geomagnetic storms (the May 2024 storm was the strongest in about two decades), auroras, disruption of GPS and radio, and power-grid risk. The Carrington Event of 1859 is the classic example. The Sun is in Solar Cycle 25, which is about 11 years long. India's Aditya-L1 mission, launched in September 2023 to the Sun-Earth L1 point, studies these phenomena. The effects are on the magnetosphere and ionosphere, not the Earth's axis.

3 — Correct and explanatory: Melting polar ice sends meltwater towards the equator because of Earth's rotation, centrifugal bulge and gravity. The Earth is an oblate spheroid, about 21 km wider at the equator. Mass moving to lower latitudes increases the moment of inertia, so rotation slows and the day lengthens. It also shifts the rotation axis through redistribution of mass. Greenland and Antarctic ice loss raises sea level, and the loss of ice weight also causes isostatic rebound. This is the mechanism behind the 2023 study by Seo and colleagues, which linked groundwater depletion to a pole shift of about 80 cm over 1993 to 2010.
summary: The answer is (b). Statements II and III are both factually correct, but only Statement III (polar ice melt moving water towards the equator) explains the shift in Earth's rotation and axis. Solar flares and CMEs hit the outer atmosphere and cause geomagnetic and ionospheric disturbances, not a change in the rotation or axis of the solid Earth.
topic_notes: Earth's rotation, axis and space weather. The Earth rotates about its axis once in about 23 h 56 min (sidereal day), and its axis is tilted about 23.5° to the orbital plane. Three kinds of change matter. (1) Polar motion: the rotation pole wanders relative to the crust. Drivers are the Chandler wobble (about 433 days), the annual wobble, ice melt and groundwater use. Since the 1990s the drift has been about 10 cm per year towards the east. (2) Length of day: it varies by milliseconds because of tides, atmosphere and ocean circulation, core-mantle coupling and mass redistribution. Ice melt lengthens the day, while the 2004 Sumatra earthquake shortened it by about 6.8 microseconds. Tidal friction from the Moon lengthens it by about 1.7 ms per century. (3) Long-term cycles: Milankovitch cycles of eccentricity (about 100,000 years), obliquity (41,000 years) and precession (about 26,000 years). The IERS in Paris and Frankfurt monitors Earth rotation and decides on leap seconds, while IAU and BIPM work with it on time standards. Space weather: the Sun's 11-year cycle, sunspots, solar flares (classified A, B, C, M, X), CMEs, the solar wind, geomagnetic storms (the Kp index and Dst index), auroras, and the Carrington Event (1859). Effects are on satellites, GPS, HF radio, pipelines and power grids. Protective factors are the magnetosphere and ozone layer. Missions: Aditya-L1 (ISRO, 2 September 2023, halo orbit at L1), Parker Solar Probe, SOHO, Solar Orbiter. Climate link: Greenland and Antarctic ice loss drives sea-level rise of about 3.7 mm per year recently.

question:
Consider the following statements : Statement : Article 6 of the Paris Agreement on climate change is frequently discussed in global discussions on sustainable development and climate change.
Statement II : Article 6 of the Paris Agreement on climate change sets out the principles of carbon markets. Statement III : Article 6 of the Paris Agreement on climate change intends to promote inter-country non-market strategies to reach their climate targets. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I
Both Statement II and Statement III are correct but only one of them explains Statement I
Only one of the Statements II and Ill is correct and that explains Statement I
Neither Statement II nor Statement Ill is correct
subject: Environment
detail: Article 6 of the Paris Agreement (2015) provides for voluntary international cooperation so that countries can meet their Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) with more ambition and lower cost. It has three parts. Article 6.2 allows bilateral or multilateral cooperative approaches, in which countries trade Internationally Transferred Mitigation Outcomes (ITMOs), with corresponding adjustments to avoid double counting. Article 6.4 creates a centralised UN-supervised mechanism, the Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism (PACM), which succeeds the Kyoto Protocol's Clean Development Mechanism. Article 6.8 sets up a framework for non-market approaches (NMA), covering finance, technology transfer and capacity building, without trading credits. Statement II is correct because Articles 6.2 and 6.4 set out the principles and rules of carbon markets. Statement III is correct because Article 6.8 promotes non-market approaches. Both features explain why Article 6 is so widely discussed, since it shapes carbon pricing, climate finance and sustainable development. The rulebook was finalised at COP29 in Baku (2024). Options (b), (c) and (d) fail because each denies that one or both statements are correct or explanatory.
explanations: Correct. Statement II (carbon markets, Articles 6.2 and 6.4) and Statement III (non-market approaches, Article 6.8) are both true, and both are core parts of Article 6, so both explain why it is frequently discussed.
Incorrect. It claims only one statement explains Statement I, but both market and non-market mechanisms are integral parts of Article 6 and both explain its prominence.
Incorrect. It claims only one of Statements II and III is correct, but both are correct.
Incorrect. It claims neither statement is correct, but Article 6 does address both carbon markets and non-market approaches.
