Related global frameworks: the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (COP15, December 2022) has the 30x30 target to protect 30% of land and oceans by 2030, and restoring 30% of degraded ecosystems is Target 2. The UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration runs from 2021 to 2030, led by UNEP and FAO. The Bonn Challenge aims to restore 350 million hectares by 2030, and India has pledged 26 million hectares. Other EU climate instruments include the European Climate Law (climate neutrality by 2050), Fit for 55, the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) and the EU Deforestation Regulation. India's biodiversity law is the Biological Diversity Act 2002, amended in 2023, and its national agencies include the National Biodiversity Authority and the CAMPA fund for afforestation.

question:
Consider the following statements :
I. Panchayats at the intermediate level exist in all States. Il. To be eligible to be a Member of a Panchayat at the intermediate level, a person should attain the age of thirty years. Ill. The Chief Minister of a State constitutes a commission to review the financial position of Panchayats at the intermediate levels and to make recommendations regarding the distribution of net proceeds of taxes and duties, leviable by the State, between the State and Panchayats at the intermediate level. Which of the statements given above are not correct?
subject: Polity
detail: Part IX of the Constitution (Articles 243 to 243O), inserted by the 73rd Amendment Act, 1992 (in force 24 April 1993), governs Panchayats. Article 243B provides a three-tier system, but the proviso allows States with a population below 20 lakh to skip the intermediate tier. Small States and Union Territories such as Goa, Manipur, Sikkim and Mizoram, among others, therefore have no intermediate Panchayat, and Statement I fails. Article 243F sets disqualification and eligibility for membership: a person must be at least 21 years old (the age for State Legislature eligibility is 25, but Panchayats use 21), so the figure of thirty in Statement II is wrong. Article 243I requires the Governor, not the Chief Minister, to constitute a State Finance Commission every five years to review Panchayat finances and recommend the distribution of net tax proceeds between the State and Panchayats at all levels. Statement III is wrong on the authority, and the Commission's remit covers all levels, not only the intermediate one. Since each statement is flawed, the question asks for those not correct, and the answer is all three.
explanations: Wrong. Statements I, II and III are all incorrect, so choosing only I and II leaves out the incorrect Statement III.
Wrong. This leaves out Statement II, which is also incorrect because the age requirement is 21 years, not thirty.
Wrong. This leaves out Statement II, which is also incorrect since the minimum age is 21 years.
Correct. All three statements are incorrect: the intermediate tier is not universal, the eligibility age is 21, and the Governor, not the Chief Minister, constitutes the State Finance Commission.
keyfact: Panchayat member age is 21; the Governor (not the CM) appoints the State Finance Commission (Art 243I); States under 20 lakh population may skip the intermediate tier.
option_notes: I and II only: this option marks the first two statements as the incorrect ones. Statement I concerns the intermediate tier of Panchayats, which is optional for States with population below 20 lakh under Article 243B. Statement II concerns the minimum age for membership, which is 21 under Article 243F. This option is incomplete because Statement III is also wrong, as the Governor constitutes the State Finance Commission under Article 243I.

I and III only: this option marks Statements I and III as incorrect. It is incomplete because Statement II is also incorrect. Statement I fails because small States need not have an intermediate tier. Statement III fails because the Governor, not the Chief Minister, appoints the State Finance Commission, which reviews finances at all tiers. The minimum age of 21 is the point it misses.

Same as option (c) in substance (OCR variant of I and III only): it identifies Statements I and III as incorrect but misses that Statement II is also wrong. The key facts are the Article 243B exemption for States under 20 lakh population, the Governor's role in constituting the State Finance Commission every five years under Article 243I, and the age of 21 under Article 243F.

I, II and III: all three statements are incorrect, which is the official answer. The relevant provisions are Articles 243B (structure and exemption), 243F (membership eligibility at 21) and 243I (State Finance Commission constituted by the Governor every five years). The 73rd Amendment Act came into force on 24 April 1993, now celebrated as National Panchayati Raj Day.
related: 73rd Amendment Act came into force on 24 April 1993; National Panchayati Raj Day is 24 April.
Article 243B(2): States with population under 20 lakh may skip the intermediate tier.
Minimum age for Panchayat membership is 21 years (Article 243F).
State Finance Commission is constituted by the Governor under Article 243I every five years.
State Election Commission for Panchayat polls is under Article 243K.
Eleventh Schedule lists 29 subjects for Panchayats.
PESA Act 1996 extends Panchayat provisions to Fifth Schedule Scheduled Areas.
Rajasthan's Nagaur adopted Panchayati Raj first on 2 October 1959.
statements: I — Incorrect: Article 243B(2) exempts States with a population under 20 lakh from creating the intermediate tier. The 73rd Amendment mandated a three-tier structure (village, intermediate, district) with this exception. Smaller States and Union Territories, for example Goa, Sikkim, Manipur, Mizoram and several UTs, have only a two-tier or one-tier system. The intermediate tier is called Panchayat Samiti, Mandal Parishad, Taluka Panchayat or Block Panchayat depending on the State. Members are elected directly, while the chairperson is elected as the State law provides. Reservation for SC, ST and women (not less than one-third) applies at every tier, as under Article 243D. Panchayat terms run five years under Article 243E.

II — Incorrect: Article 243F makes a person eligible for Panchayat membership at 21 years of age, in line with the 73rd Amendment. Disqualification is determined by the State's laws, or by laws for the State Legislature, but a person can't be disqualified on grounds of being under 25 if they are 21 or older. The same age applies at all three tiers. Thirty years is not a constitutional requirement for Panchayats. The Constitution sets 25 years for State Legislative Assembly membership, 30 for Legislative Council and Rajya Sabha, and 35 for President and Vice-President. Disqualification questions are decided by an authority the State Legislature specifies.

III — Incorrect: Under Article 243I, the Governor constitutes the State Finance Commission within one year of the 73rd Amendment's commencement and every five years thereafter. It reviews Panchayat finances and recommends how net tax, duty, toll and fee proceeds are distributed between the State and Panchayats, grants-in-aid from the Consolidated Fund of the State, and measures to improve Panchayat finances. Its recommendations are laid before the Legislature with an action-taken memorandum. Article 243Y applies similar rules to Municipalities. The Central Finance Commission under Article 280(3)(bb) recommends measures to augment the State Consolidated Fund to supplement Panchayat resources. The Chief Minister has no role in constituting the Commission, and its remit covers all Panchayat tiers.
summary: The answer is (d): all three statements are incorrect. The intermediate tier is not mandatory in every State, the minimum age for Panchayat membership is 21 years, and the State Finance Commission is constituted by the Governor, not the Chief Minister.
topic_notes: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, added Part IX (Articles 243 to 243O) and the Eleventh Schedule (29 subjects) to the Constitution. It came into force on 24 April 1993. Panchayati Raj is a State subject (Entry 5, List II), and Article 40 (a Directive Principle) had earlier encouraged village Panchayats. Key provisions: Gram Sabha (Article 243A); three-tier structure with exemption for States under 20 lakh population (243B); direct elections to all seats (243C); reservation for SC/ST in proportion to population and not less than one-third of seats for women (243D); five-year term, with fresh elections within six months of dissolution (243E); minimum age of 21 for membership (243F); powers, authority and responsibilities (243G); taxes and finances (243H); State Finance Commission constituted by the Governor every five years (243I); audit of accounts (243J); State Election Commission, headed by a State Election Commissioner appointed by the Governor, to conduct elections (243K); application to Union Territories (243L); exemption of Scheduled Areas and certain areas such as Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram, and hill areas of Manipur and Darjeeling (243M); continuance of existing laws for one year (243N); bar on court interference in electoral matters (243O). The PESA Act, 1996 extends Panchayats to Fifth Schedule Scheduled Areas. Earlier committees: Balwant Rai Mehta (1957, three-tier), Ashok Mehta (1977, two-tier), and L.M. Singhvi and G.V.K. Rao committees. Rajasthan (Nagaur, 2 October 1959) was the first State to adopt Panchayati Raj. Ministry of Panchayati Raj was created in 2004. The 74th Amendment covers urban local bodies. Reservations for OBCs are left to State laws under Article 243D(6).

question:
Consider the following statements in respect of BIMSTEC :
I. It is a regional organization consisting of seven member States till January 2025. Il. It came into existence with the signing of the Dhaka Declaration, 1999. Ill. Bangladesh, India, Sri_ Lanka, Thailand and Nepal are founding member States of BIMSTEC.
IV. In BIMSTEC, the subsector of ‘tourism’ is being led by India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
subject: Current Affairs
detail: BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) was formed on 6 June 1997 through the Bangkok Declaration. It began as BIST-EC with four members (Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka, Thailand). Myanmar joined on 22 December 1997, when it was renamed BIMST-EC. Nepal and Bhutan joined in February 2004, and the name became BIMSTEC at the 2004 summit. The Dhaka Declaration of 1999 is not the founding document. The permanent Secretariat is in Dhaka, and the BIMSTEC Charter was adopted at the 5th Summit in Colombo in 2022. The 6th Summit was held in Bangkok in April 2025. Sector leadership was rationalised into seven pillars: Bangladesh leads trade, investment and development; Bhutan leads environment and climate change; India leads security; Myanmar leads agriculture and food security; Nepal leads people-to-people contact; Sri Lanka leads science, technology and innovation; Thailand leads connectivity. In the older sector list, tourism was led by India, but UPSC treats statement IV as incorrect. Statement I is correct, since there are seven members and none were added by January 2025. Eliminating II and III removes (a), (b) and (c), leaving (d).
explanations: (a) is wrong because Statement II is incorrect: BIMSTEC was founded by the Bangkok Declaration of 1997, not a 1999 Dhaka Declaration.
(b) is wrong because both II and III are incorrect. The founding date is wrong, and Nepal was not a founding member.
(c) is wrong because Statement IV is treated as incorrect, since India leads security, not tourism, among the seven current pillars.
(d) is correct because only Statement I holds: BIMSTEC had seven members until January 2025.
keyfact: BIMSTEC: Bangkok Declaration 1997, four founders, seven members till January 2025, Secretariat in Dhaka.
option_notes: Statements I and II together. I is correct, but II is wrong because the Dhaka Declaration 1999 was not the founding document. The founding instrument was the Bangkok Declaration of 6 June 1997. Dhaka is the seat of the permanent Secretariat, which was established in 2014 and funded largely by India.

Statements II and III together. Both are wrong. II misdates and misplaces the founding document. III wrongly includes Nepal as a founder, though Nepal joined in 2004. The founding four were Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka and Thailand, and Myanmar joined later in 1997.

Statements I and IV together. I is correct, but IV is treated as incorrect. India leads the security pillar. The earlier sector list, with 14 priority sectors, was consolidated into seven pillars led by different members.

Statement I only. It is the official answer. BIMSTEC had seven members until January 2025, all around the Bay of Bengal region of South and Southeast Asia. Its Secretariat is in Dhaka, and its Charter was adopted in March 2022 at the Colombo summit.
related: BIMSTEC was founded by the Bangkok Declaration on 6 June 1997.
Founding members of BIST-EC were Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka and Thailand.
Myanmar joined in December 1997, and Nepal and Bhutan in 2004.
BIMSTEC Secretariat is in Dhaka.
BIMSTEC Charter was adopted at the Colombo summit in 2022.
The 6th BIMSTEC Summit was held in Bangkok in April 2025.
Pakistan and Afghanistan are SAARC members but not BIMSTEC members.
India leads the security pillar in BIMSTEC.
statements: I — Correct: BIMSTEC had seven member states until January 2025 (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Thailand). It links South Asia and Southeast Asia around the Bay of Bengal. It began with four members in 1997. Myanmar joined in December 1997, and Nepal and Bhutan in 2004. Its Secretariat is in Dhaka, and its Charter was adopted in 2022. The grouping covers about 1.8 billion people, and India sees it as central to its Neighbourhood First and Act East policies, particularly since SAARC has stalled.

II — Incorrect: BIMSTEC was founded by the Bangkok Declaration on 6 June 1997, not by a Dhaka Declaration in 1999. It was initially called BIST-EC. Myanmar joined on 22 December 1997 and the name changed to BIMST-EC. The first summit was held in Bangkok in 2004, the same year Nepal and Bhutan joined. Dhaka hosts the Secretariat, which was inaugurated in 2014, with India providing major funding. Students should remember Bangkok 1997 as the founding date and place.

III — Incorrect: The founding members were Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka and Thailand, forming BIST-EC. Nepal was not a founder and joined only in 2004, along with Bhutan. Myanmar joined in December 1997. Because the list includes Nepal as a founder, the statement is wrong. Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka and Thailand are in the Bay of Bengal region, while Nepal and Bhutan are landlocked members. Their inclusion extended the grouping's reach to the Himalayan region.

IV — Incorrect: As UPSC treats it, the statement is wrong. BIMSTEC cooperation was reorganised into seven pillars, each led by a member state: Bangladesh (trade, investment and development), Bhutan (environment and climate change), India (security, including counter-terrorism and disaster management), Myanmar (agriculture and food security), Nepal (people-to-people contact), Sri Lanka (science, technology and innovation) and Thailand (connectivity). Tourism was originally an older sector led by India, but it is not one of the seven current pillars. The reorganisation reduced the 14 earlier priority sectors into these pillars.
summary: The answer is (d): only Statement I is correct. BIMSTEC had seven members (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Thailand) through January 2025. Statements II, III and IV each contain a factual error about its founding, its founding members or its sector leadership.
topic_notes: BIMSTEC is a regional grouping linking South Asia and Southeast Asia. It was founded on 6 June 1997 by the Bangkok Declaration as BIST-EC with Bangladesh, India, Sri Lanka and Thailand. Myanmar joined in December 1997, and Nepal and Bhutan in 2004, when the name BIMSTEC was adopted. It has seven members, covers about 1.8 billion people and a combined GDP of roughly 5 trillion dollars. The Secretariat is in Dhaka, and the Secretary General is rotated alphabetically. Summits: first in Bangkok (2004), second in Dhaka (2008), third in Myanmar (2018), fourth in Kathmandu (2018), fifth in Colombo (2022, held virtually), and sixth in Bangkok (April 2025). The Charter was adopted in 2022, giving the group legal personality. Cooperation sectors were rationalised into seven pillars led by Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand. Key projects include the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project, the India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway, the BIMSTEC Free Trade Agreement negotiations, the Master Plan for Transport Connectivity, and the Coastal Shipping Agreement. India favours BIMSTEC because SAARC is stalled and Pakistan is not a member, and BIMSTEC serves as a link between India's Neighbourhood First and Act East policies. Disaster management exercises and the BIMSTEC Energy Centre in Bengaluru are also important. Likely future angles include the member list, observer and dialogue partners, the Bay of Bengal's geography, and comparisons with SAARC, ASEAN and BBIN.

question:
Who amongst the following are members of the Jury to select the recipient of ‘Gandhi Peace Prize’?
I. The President of India Il. The Prime Minister of India Ill. The Chief Justice of India
IV. The Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Select the correct answer using the code given below
subject: Polity
detail: The Gandhi Peace Prize was instituted by the Government of India in 1995, on the occasion of the 125th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi. It is an annual award for social, economic and political transformation through non-violence and other Gandhian methods. It is open to all persons regardless of nationality, race, language, caste, creed or gender. The award carries Rs 1 crore (convertible in any currency), a citation, a plaque and an attractive traditional handicraft/handloom item. The selection is made by a jury consisting of the Prime Minister (Chairperson), the Chief Justice of India, the Leader of the Single Largest Opposition Party in the Lok Sabha, plus one eminent person nominated by the government (the Speaker of the Lok Sabha has also been included in some compositions). Elimination logic: the President is the constitutional head and typically presents awards, but is not on the selection committee, so any option containing I (b, d) is out. Option (a) omits the CJI. Only (c) matches the composition. The first recipient (1995) was Julius Nyerere. Recent recipients include Gita Press, Gorakhpur (2021) and Sultan Qaboos (2019, Oman).
explanations: (a) is wrong because it leaves out the Chief Justice of India, who is a jury member.
(b) is wrong because it includes the President, who is not on the jury, and omits the Leader of Opposition.
(c) is correct: the PM, CJI and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha are jury members, matching the official answer.
(d) is wrong because it includes the President and omits the PM and Leader of Opposition.
keyfact: Gandhi Peace Prize jury = PM (chair) + CJI + Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha + one eminent person; the President is not a member.
option_notes: Option (a): the PM and the Leader of Opposition are both jury members, but this option is incomplete. The Gandhi Peace Prize jury also includes the CJI and one eminent person. The prize was instituted in 1995, carries Rs 1 crore and is administered by the Ministry of Culture. It honours non-violent contributions to social, economic and political change.

Option (b): this combination (President, PM, CJI as read from the OCR) wrongly includes the President. The President of India is the constitutional head under Article 52 and generally confers national awards such as the Bharat Ratna and Padma awards on the Government's recommendation, but is not on this jury. The Gandhi Peace Prize jury has no presidential role.

Option (c): the PM, CJI and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha make up the jury, along with one eminent person. The PM is the chair. This three-member ex officio structure is also seen in other selection panels, including that for the CBI Director. The award, instituted in 1995, was most recently given to Gita Press (2021).

Option (d): the President and the CJI only. This is wrong because the President is not a member and the PM and Leader of Opposition are left out. The CJI is the head of the judiciary under Articles 124 and 126 and sits on several statutory selection committees, including the Gandhi Peace Prize jury.
related: Gandhi Peace Prize was instituted in 1995 on Gandhi's 125th birth anniversary.
The prize carries Rs 1 crore, a citation, a plaque and a traditional handicraft item.
Julius Nyerere of Tanzania was the first recipient (1995).
Gita Press, Gorakhpur received the 2021 prize and Sultan Qaboos of Oman the 2019 prize.
Sheikh Mujibur Rahman (2020) received the prize posthumously.
The CBI Director is selected by a committee of PM, CJI and Leader of Opposition.
The Ministry of Culture administers the Gandhi Peace Prize.
ISRO won the Gandhi Peace Prize for 2014.
statements: I — Incorrect: The President of India is not a jury member. The President is the head of State and generally confers national awards, but the Gandhi Peace Prize jury is composed of the PM, the CJI, the Leader of Opposition and one eminent person. The prize was instituted in 1995 on Gandhi's 125th anniversary and is administered by the Ministry of Culture. It is given annually for contributions to social, economic and political transformation through non-violence. The award includes Rs 1 crore, a citation, a plaque and a handicraft item.

II — Correct: The Prime Minister chairs the jury. The PM leads this high-level committee, which selects the awardee from nominations and also from the jury's own suggestions. The Gandhi Peace Prize is open to individuals and institutions worldwide. Past recipients include Julius Nyerere (1995), A. T. Ariyaratne (1996), Gerhard Fischer (1997), Nelson Mandela (2000), Baba Amte, Desmond Tutu, Chandi Prasad Bhatt, ISRO (2014), Sulabh International (2016), the Ramakrishna Mission (2020), Gita Press (2021) and Sultan Qaboos of Oman (2019).

III — Correct: The Chief Justice of India is a jury member, ensuring judicial and non-partisan participation. The CJI also sits on other high-level selection panels, for example for the CBI Director (with the PM and LoP). The Gandhi Peace Prize jury is similar in composition to such committees. The award is non-discriminatory and open to all, irrespective of nationality, race, language, caste, creed or gender. It is announced by the Ministry of Culture.

IV — Correct: The Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha (the leader of the single largest opposition party) is a jury member, giving the committee a bipartisan character. The post has statutory recognition under the Salary and Allowances of Leaders of Opposition in Parliament Act, 1977. The Leader of Opposition also sits on selection committees for the CBI Director, Lokpal, CVC, CIC and NHRC. For the Gandhi Peace Prize, they sit with the PM and CJI.
summary: The correct answer is (c): the Prime Minister, the Chief Justice of India and the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha (the OCR'd code '1, Wand IV' reads as II, III and IV). The Gandhi Peace Prize jury is a high-level body of the PM (chair), CJI, LoP in Lok Sabha plus one eminent person. The President is not a jury member; the President only presents the award.
topic_notes: The Gandhi Peace Prize was instituted in 1995 by the Government of India to mark the 125th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi. It recognises contributions to social, economic and political transformation through non-violence and Gandhian methods. It is open to all, irrespective of nationality, race, language, caste, creed or gender. The award consists of Rs 1 crore, a citation, a plaque and a traditional handicraft or handloom item. The Ministry of Culture administers it. A jury chaired by the PM and including the CJI, the Leader of the Single Largest Opposition Party in the Lok Sabha and one eminent person selects the awardee. Notable recipients: Julius Nyerere (1995, first), A. T. Ariyaratne (1996), Gerhard Fischer (1997), Ramakrishna Mission (1998), Baba Amte (1999), Nelson Mandela and Grameen Bank (2000), Desmond Tutu (2005), Chandi Prasad Bhatt (2013), ISRO (2014), Vivekananda Kendra (2015), Akshaya Patra and Sulabh International (2016), Yohei Sasakawa (2018), Sultan Qaboos bin Said (2019), Sheikh Mujibur Rahman (2020, posthumous), Gita Press (2021). Related high-level committees with the PM, CJI and LoP: CBI Director, Lokpal, CVC and CIC selection panels. Other awards: Bharat Ratna (Article 18 does not cover them; they are not titles), Jnanpith, Dadasaheb Phalke Award, the Nobel Peace Prize (Gandhi never received it). Prelims often asks about the composition of selection committees and recent awardees.

question:
GPS-Aided Geo Augmented Navigation (GAGAN) uses a system of ground stations to provide necessary augmentation. Which of the following statements is/are correct in respect of GAGAN?
I. It is designed to provide additional accuracy and integrity. Il. It will allow more uniform and high quality air traffic management. Ill. It will provide benefits only in aviation but not in other modes of transportation. Select the correct answer using the code given below
subject: Economy
detail: GAGAN (GPS Aided GEO Augmented Navigation) was developed jointly by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) and the Airports Authority of India (AAI), with Raytheon as the technology partner. It is an SBAS like the US WAAS, European EGNOS and Japanese MSAS. Ground reference stations (INGRES) receive GPS signals, and master control centres compute correction and integrity messages. These are uplinked to geostationary satellites (GSAT-8, GSAT-10, GSAT-15), which broadcast them to user receivers on the L1 and L5 frequencies. This gives the accuracy and integrity needed for precision approaches (APV-1) and uniform, high-quality air traffic management across the Indian Flight Information Region. DGCA certified GAGAN for RNP 0.1 in 2013 and for APV 1 approaches in 2015. IndiGo made the first LPV approach landing at Kishangarh in 2022. Elimination: statement III uses the word 'only', which is false because GAGAN also benefits railways, surveying, maritime, agriculture, disaster management, location-based services and the like. This removes (a) and (b). Statement II is true, which removes (c). That leaves (d).
explanations: Wrong: statement III says GAGAN benefits only aviation, which is false, so all three cannot be correct.
Wrong: it includes III, which is false, and it leaves out I, which is true.
Wrong: statement I is correct, but II is also correct, so 'I only' is incomplete.
Correct: I and II are true, since GAGAN gives added accuracy and integrity and supports uniform, high-quality air traffic management. III is false because its benefits extend beyond aviation.
keyfact: GAGAN is India's ISRO-AAI SBAS that augments GPS for accuracy and integrity, mainly for aviation but with wider uses (the 'only aviation' claim is wrong).
option_notes: Option (a) would make all three statements correct. GAGAN's benefits are not limited to aviation, because it also serves railways, maritime users, surveying, agriculture and disaster management. The 'only' in III is the usual UPSC trap. GAGAN is India's SBAS, developed by ISRO and AAI, and uses geostationary satellites to broadcast corrections to GPS signals.

Option (b) pairs II with III. II is true but III is false. GAGAN is mainly meant for civil aviation, but it can be used in many other sectors. It is interoperable with WAAS (USA), EGNOS (Europe) and MSAS (Japan). It has been certified for APV-1 operations, and it will help Indian airports that lack ILS.

Option (c) says only statement I is correct. It is a partial answer, because GAGAN also supports uniform, high-quality air traffic management, so II is also correct. GAGAN improves integrity, accuracy and availability. Integrity means timely warnings when the GPS signal should not be used, which is essential for safety-of-life applications such as landing aircraft.

Option (d) is the official answer. GAGAN adds accuracy and integrity to GPS and supports better air traffic management. The ground segment has 15 reference stations (INGRES), 3 uplink stations and 2 master control centres, at Bengaluru and Delhi. It was launched in 2008 and certified for RNP 0.1 in 2013 and APV-1 in 2015. India is the fourth country to have SBAS.
related: GAGAN is India's SBAS, developed by ISRO and AAI.
GAGAN augments GPS, whereas NavIC is an independent regional navigation system.
NavIC has 7 satellites and covers India plus a region extending about 1,500 km beyond.
GAGAN's satellites include GSAT-8, GSAT-10 and GSAT-15.
The master control centres are at Bengaluru and Delhi.
Other SBAS systems are WAAS (USA), EGNOS (Europe) and MSAS (Japan).
DGCA certified GAGAN for APV-1 approach in 2015.
IndiGo made the first GAGAN-based LPV landing at Kishangarh in 2022.
statements: I — Correct: GAGAN corrects GPS errors and provides integrity alerts. SBAS broadcasts ionospheric and satellite clock/ephemeris corrections, plus integrity warnings when a signal is unreliable. This lets aircraft use GPS for precision-type approaches (APV-1), with accuracy of about 3 m. GAGAN was built by ISRO and AAI. It was declared operational for en-route navigation in 2013 and for approach operations in 2015. It covers the Indian FIR and extends from Africa to Australia. Its geostationary satellites are GSAT-8, GSAT-10 and GSAT-15.

II — Correct: GAGAN provides seamless, uniform navigation coverage over the Indian airspace and neighbouring regions. This supports better air traffic management through more efficient routes, fewer ground-based navigational aids, shorter separation, fuel savings and better runway access, especially at airports without ILS. Interoperability with WAAS, EGNOS and MSAS gives continuity across regions. Indian airports have used LPV procedures for approaches, and IndiGo made the first LPV landing at Kishangarh in 2022. GAGAN also supports ICAO's performance-based navigation goals.

III — Incorrect: GAGAN is mainly designed for civil aviation, but the claim that it benefits only aviation is wrong. Its signals can be used in railways (train tracking, signalling and safety), maritime navigation, surveying and mapping, agriculture, disaster management, logistics, telecom timing and location-based services. A GAGAN-based intelligent navigation system (GIN) is used by fishermen for ocean-state and warning messages. It is also available as an augmentation signal for road and personal navigation. The word 'only' makes the statement false.
summary: The correct answer is (d): statements I and II are correct, and statement III is wrong. GAGAN is India's Satellite Based Augmentation System (SBAS). It improves the accuracy and integrity of GPS signals, mainly for civil aviation and air traffic management, but its benefits also extend to other sectors.
topic_notes: GAGAN is India's SBAS, built by ISRO and AAI at a cost of about ₹774 crore. SBAS augments GNSS signals (GPS) using ground reference stations and geostationary satellites. The ground segment has 15 Indian Reference Stations (INGRES), the Indian Master Control Centre (INMCC) and Indian Land Uplink Stations (INLUS), with the main control centres at Bengaluru and Delhi. The space segment uses GSAT-8, GSAT-10 and GSAT-15, which carry GAGAN payloads on L1 and L5. DGCA certified GAGAN for RNP 0.1 en-route in 2013 and for APV-1 approach in 2015. It is interoperable with WAAS, EGNOS and MSAS. Other regional systems are Russia's SDCM and China's BDSBAS. India is the fourth country or region after the US, Europe and Japan to have an SBAS. IndiGo made the first LPV approach at Kishangarh in 2022. Benefits include fuel savings, better access to airports without ILS, safer landings, and use in railways, surveying, agriculture, disaster management and maritime navigation. NavIC (IRNSS) is separate: it is India's independent regional navigation satellite system with 7 satellites, covering India and about 1,500 km beyond, with the Standard Positioning Service and the Restricted Service. GAGAN augments GPS, whereas NavIC is an independent constellation. Other global systems are GPS (USA), GLONASS (Russia), Galileo (EU) and BeiDou (China). QZSS is Japan's regional system. UPSC may ask about the definition of SBAS, the agencies involved, the satellites, or a comparison between GAGAN and NavIC.

question:
Consider the following statements regarding AI Action Summit held in Grand Palais, Paris in February 2025 :
I. Co-chaired with India, the event builds on the advances made at the Bletchley Park Summit held in 2023 and the Seoul Summit held in 2024. Il. Along with other countries, US and UK also signed the declaration on inclusive and sustainable Al. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
subject: Current Affairs
detail: The AI Action Summit was held at the Grand Palais, Paris, on 10-11 February 2025. It was co-chaired by French President Emmanuel Macron and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, and it continued the series begun at Bletchley Park, UK (November 2023, AI Safety Summit, which produced the Bletchley Declaration) and Seoul (May 2024, AI Seoul Summit). The Paris summit shifted the emphasis from pure safety toward action, public-interest AI, innovation, and inclusion. It produced the 'Statement on Inclusive and Sustainable Artificial Intelligence for People and the Planet', signed by around 60 countries, including India, China, France, and others. The United States (VP JD Vance attended and criticised heavy regulation) and the United Kingdom declined to sign, the UK citing concerns over national security and global governance clarity. Elimination logic: Statement I is factually accurate, so (b) and (d) go. Statement II is false because both the US and UK refused to sign, so (c) goes. That leaves (a). India announced it would host the next summit, the AI Impact Summit, in 2026 in New Delhi.
explanations: Correct: Statement I is accurate (France-India co-chairs, builds on Bletchley and Seoul) and Statement II is false, since the US and UK did not sign.
Wrong: Statement II is incorrect because the US and UK declined to sign the declaration, and Statement I is correct, so 'II only' cannot be right.
Wrong: this requires Statement II to be correct, but the US and UK refused to sign the declaration.
Wrong: Statement I is correct, since India co-chaired with France and the summit built on the earlier two summits.
keyfact: Paris AI Action Summit (Feb 2025) was co-chaired by France and India after Bletchley (2023) and Seoul (2024); the US and UK did not sign its declaration.
option_notes: Option (a) 'I only' is the official answer. It reflects that the summit was co-chaired by France and India and continued the Bletchley-Seoul-Paris sequence, while the claim about US and UK signing is wrong. Statement-number options like this one are tested by splitting the claims and verifying each separately.

Option (b) 'II only' would be right only if the US and UK had signed the declaration. They did not. It is a trap built on the assumption that major AI powers would sign. In practice, about 60 countries signed, including China and India, while the US and UK abstained.

Option (c) 'Both I and II' would need both statements true. It is wrong because Statement II is false. The Paris statement was not universal, and the lack of US and UK backing was widely reported as a sign of divisions over AI governance.

Option (d) 'Neither I nor II' would need Statement I to be false too. But the co-chairing by France and India and the lineage from Bletchley Park 2023 and Seoul 2024 are accurate, so this option is wrong.
related: Bletchley Park AI Safety Summit: 1-2 November 2023, UK, Bletchley Declaration.
Seoul AI Summit: May 2024, Frontier AI Safety Commitments.
Paris AI Action Summit: 10-11 Feb 2025, co-chaired by Macron and Modi.
India will host the AI Impact Summit in 2026 in New Delhi.
The US and UK did not sign the Paris declaration on inclusive and sustainable AI.
IndiaAI Mission approved March 2024, outlay about ₹10,372 crore.
EU AI Act is the first comprehensive AI law, in force from August 2024.
GPAI was launched in 2020; India is a founding member.
statements: I — Correct: France and India co-chaired the summit, and it followed Bletchley (2023) and Seoul (2024). The AI Action Summit was the third in the global series on AI governance. Bletchley Park (1-2 Nov 2023) produced the Bletchley Declaration on frontier AI risks, signed by 28 countries and the EU. Seoul (21-22 May 2024) produced the Seoul Declaration and the Frontier AI Safety Commitments. Paris (10-11 Feb 2025) at the Grand Palais was co-chaired by Macron and Modi, and its themes were public-interest AI, the future of work, innovation and culture, trust in AI, and global AI governance. India will host the next edition in 2026.

II — Incorrect: the US and UK did not sign the Paris declaration. The 'Statement on Inclusive and Sustainable AI for People and the Planet' was endorsed by about 60 countries, including India, China, France, Germany, Canada, Australia and Japan, plus the African Union and the EU. The US, represented by VP JD Vance, objected to excessive regulation and to language it saw as restrictive. The UK said the text lacked practical clarity on global governance and did not sufficiently address national security. The declaration stresses openness, ethics, accessibility, sustainability of AI, and avoiding market concentration.
summary: The answer is (a): only Statement I is correct. The Paris AI Action Summit (10-11 February 2025) was co-chaired by France and India and followed the Bletchley Park (2023) and Seoul (2024) summits, but the US and UK did not sign the Paris declaration on inclusive and sustainable AI.
topic_notes: Global AI summit series: Bletchley Park, UK (1-2 Nov 2023) was the first AI Safety Summit and produced the Bletchley Declaration, recognising risks from frontier AI, signed by 28 countries and the EU, including the US, China and India. Seoul (21-22 May 2024), co-hosted by South Korea and the UK, produced the Seoul Declaration and the Frontier AI Safety Commitments from leading companies. Paris AI Action Summit (10-11 Feb 2025), Grand Palais, was co-chaired by France and India, with a shift toward action, public-interest AI, sustainability, and inclusion. The outcome was the Statement on Inclusive and Sustainable AI for People and the Planet, signed by about 60 countries; the US and UK did not sign. Launches included a Public Interest AI platform and incubator and initiatives on AI and energy. India's next role: it will host the AI Impact Summit in 2026 in New Delhi. Other AI governance anchors: the Global Partnership on AI (GPAI, launched 2020, India is a member and was chair in 2024), the OECD AI Principles (2019), the UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI (2021), the EU AI Act (in force Aug 2024, the first comprehensive AI law, risk-based), the US Executive Order on AI (Oct 2023, later rescinded by the Trump administration in Jan 2025), and the UN General Assembly resolution on AI (March 2024). In India, the IndiaAI Mission was approved in March 2024 with an outlay of about ₹10,372 crore, focused on compute, datasets, and foundation models. Possible questions: host cities and years, the signatories and abstainers, declaration names, and India's role.

ocr: Consider the following pairs : International Year of the : 2026 I. Woman Farmer International Year of te 2027 is Sustainable and Resilient Tourism International Year of Peace : 2025 Ill. and Trust International Year of Asteroid : 2029 Awareness and Planetary Defence How many of the — given above are correctly matched (a) Only one (b) Only two (c) Only three (ad) All the four 41 [P.T.O.
subject: Science & Tech
detail: UN International Years are proclaimed by the UN General Assembly (sometimes on the recommendation of ECOSOC or a specialised agency such as FAO or UNESCO) to draw global attention to a theme. This question tests recent UN-proclaimed observances, a favourite UPSC current-affairs area. The facts to hold are: 2025 is the International Year of Peace and Trust (also the Year of Quantum Science and Technology, and of Glaciers' Preservation); 2026 is the International Year of the Woman Farmer (also Rangelands and Pastoralists, and Volunteers for Sustainable Development); 2027 is the International Year of Sustainable and Resilient Tourism; 2029 is the International Year of Asteroid Awareness and Planetary Defence, linked to the close approach of asteroid Apophis on 13 April 2029. Elimination logic: if a student knows even two pairs are right, options (a) and (b) are ruled out. Knowing three correct pairs leaves only (c) or (d), and the fourth pair, 2029 Apophis, is easily confirmed by its astronomical logic. In 'how many pairs' questions, check each pair independently, because UPSC often makes all items correct or all incorrect.
explanations: Wrong: it says only one pair is correct, but all four pairs match the UN proclamations.
Wrong: it says only two pairs are correct, but all four are correct, so the count is understated.
Wrong: it says only three pairs are correct, but the fourth pair (Asteroid Awareness and Planetary Defence, 2029) is also correct.

Correct: 2026 for the Woman Farmer, 2027 for Sustainable and Resilient Tourism, 2025 for Peace and Trust, and 2029 for Asteroid Awareness and Planetary Defence are all accurate, so all four pairs are correctly matched.
keyfact: 2025 Peace and Trust; 2026 Woman Farmer; 2027 Sustainable and Resilient Tourism; 2029 Asteroid Awareness and Planetary Defence (Apophis flyby, 13 April 2029).
option_notes: Only one: this would mean exactly one pair is right. It is a typical distractor in 'how many pairs' questions, designed to catch students who know just one observance. The UPSC convention is that each pair is judged independently, so counting carefully matters. Here the count is four, not one.

Only two: this would mean exactly two of the four pairs are right. It tempts students who confuse the years of the Woman Farmer (2026) and Tourism (2027), or who are unsure about Peace and Trust. Swapping years between the pairs would be the usual trap, but none of the years here is swapped.

Only three: this is the most tempting wrong option, because the 2029 Asteroid Year is the least familiar of the four. Students who doubt it as obscure or fictional would choose three. It is real: it is tied to the Apophis flyby on 13 April 2029, so the count is four.

All the four: this is the correct option. The 2025, 2026, 2027 and 2029 pairings all match UNGA proclamations. In such questions UPSC sometimes makes every item correct, so students should not assume that at least one pair has been altered.
related: 2023 was the International Year of Millets, proposed by India and adopted by the UNGA.
The asteroid Apophis will pass about 32,000 km from Earth on 13 April 2029.
NASA's DART mission (2022) changed the orbit of Dimorphos, a moonlet of the asteroid Didymos.
2025 is the 80th anniversary of the UN, founded on 24 October 1945.
UN Tourism, formerly UNWTO, is headquartered in Madrid.
International Asteroid Day is observed on 30 June.
15 October is the International Day of Rural Women.
International Years are proclaimed by the UN General Assembly.
statements: I — Correct: The International Year of the Woman Farmer is 2026, proclaimed by the UNGA. It highlights women's role in agriculture and food security and the gaps they face in access to land, credit, technology and markets. FAO is expected to lead the observance. Women make up a large share of the agricultural workforce, especially in developing countries, yet hold a small share of land titles. 2026 also carries the Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists.

II — Correct: The International Year of Sustainable and Resilient Tourism is 2027, proclaimed by the UNGA. UN Tourism (formerly UNWTO, headquartered in Madrid) is the lead agency. The theme promotes tourism that is low-carbon, climate-resilient and inclusive, supports local communities, and contributes to the SDGs. World Tourism Day is observed on 27 September each year. Tourism is a major contributor to GDP and jobs, but it is vulnerable to climate shocks and pandemics.

III — Correct: The International Year of Peace and Trust is 2025, proclaimed by the UNGA on the initiative of Turkmenistan, which stresses trust-building, dialogue and cooperation between nations. 2025 also marks the 80th anniversary of the UN, founded on 24 October 1945. The year is linked to the UN Charter's aim of maintaining international peace and security. Other 2025 years include Quantum Science and Technology, and Glaciers' Preservation.

IV — Correct: The International Year of Asteroid Awareness and Planetary Defence is 2029, proclaimed by the UNGA. The asteroid 99942 Apophis, about 340 m across, will pass within roughly 32,000 km of Earth on 13 April 2029, closer than geostationary satellites. The year promotes awareness and international cooperation on near-Earth object detection and deflection. Related events include NASA's DART mission (2022), which altered the orbit of the asteroid Dimorphos, and International Asteroid Day on 30 June.
summary: The answer is (d): all four pairs are correctly matched. The UN General Assembly has proclaimed 2025 as the International Year of Peace and Trust, 2026 as the International Year of the Woman Farmer, 2027 as the International Year of Sustainable and Resilient Tourism, and 2029 as the International Year of Asteroid Awareness and Planetary Defence.
topic_notes: International Years are proclaimed by the UN General Assembly to focus attention on issues of global concern. International Days are also set by the UNGA or by specialised agencies such as UNESCO, WHO and FAO. Some recent and upcoming International Years: 2023 was the International Year of Millets (proposed by India, and adopted by the UNGA in March 2021); 2024 was the International Year of Camelids; 2025 is the International Year of Quantum Science and Technology, of Peace and Trust, and of Glaciers' Preservation (with the Decade of Action for Cryospheric Sciences 2025-2034); 2026 is the International Year of the Woman Farmer, of Rangelands and Pastoralists, and of Volunteers for Sustainable Development; 2027 is the International Year of Sustainable and Resilient Tourism; and 2029 is the International Year of Asteroid Awareness and Planetary Defence. Apophis (99942) is an Aten-class near-Earth asteroid, and the OSIRIS-APEX mission is to study it in 2029. Planetary defence ties into NASA's DART mission, ESA's Hera mission and the UN-endorsed International Asteroid Warning Network (IAWN) and Space Mission Planning Advisory Group (SMPAG). Other relevant angles: UN Tourism is a specialised agency; FAO leads many agricultural years; UNESCO leads years in science and culture; the 2030 Agenda and the SDGs frame most of these themes. UPSC frequently pairs year and theme, or asks which agency leads the observance, so revise the lead agency along with each year. For the Woman Farmer year, also remember India's Mahila Kisan Sashaktikaran Pariyojana (MKSP) under DAY-NRLM, and that 15 October is the International Day of Rural Women.

question: Consider the following statements with regard to BRICS : I. 16th BRICS Summit was held under the Chairship of Russia in Kazan. Il. Indonesia -has become a _ full member of BRICS. Ill. The theme of the 16th BRICS Summit was Strengthening Multiculturalism for Just Global Development and Security. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
subject: Current Affairs
detail: BRICS is an informal grouping of major emerging economies with no charter or secretariat. The chair rotates annually and hosts the summit. Russia chaired in 2024 and held the 16th Summit at Kazan, Tatarstan, on 22-24 October 2024. It was the first summit after the 2024 expansion, which added Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the UAE. Saudi Arabia was invited but has not formally confirmed, and Argentina declined. Kazan also created a new 'partner country' category. Brazil, as the 2025 chair, announced on 6 January 2025 that Indonesia had been admitted as a full member. Statement III is a classic UPSC trap: one word in the official theme was swapped. The correct theme is 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security'. Multilateralism, meaning reform of global institutions such as the UN, IMF and WTO, is the core BRICS concern. Multiculturalism is not. The elimination logic is that I is certainly true and II is true, so only (a) fits. Options (b) and (c) include III and are wrong, and (d) omits II.
explanations: Correct: statements I and II are both factually true, and III is false because of the wrong word 'Multiculturalism'.
Wrong: it includes statement III, which misstates the theme, and omits II, which is true.
Wrong: it also includes statement III with the altered theme, and omits II. It is effectively the same combination as (b).
Wrong: statement I is true, but II is also true, so 'I only' is incomplete.
keyfact: 16th BRICS Summit: Kazan, Russia (Oct 2024), theme 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security'; Indonesia full member from January 2025.
option_notes: I and II: this is the correct combination. It pairs the Kazan summit under Russia's chairship (October 2024) with Indonesia's full membership (announced 6 January 2025). Both facts are checkable. Kazan was the first summit of the expanded BRICS, and Indonesia is the first Southeast Asian full member. Remember that III fails only because 'Multilateralism' was replaced by 'Multiculturalism'.

The 1 and III combination (an OCR variant). It would be right only if III were true and II false. III uses the wrong word, and II is in fact true. The real theme was 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security'. Multilateralism means reform of global bodies such as the UN Security Council, IMF and WTO to give emerging economies more voice, and it is a recurring BRICS theme.

I and III: it wrongly accepts the 'Multiculturalism' theme and rejects Indonesia's membership. Students should remember that BRICS summit themes usually involve multilateralism, inclusivity, the Global South or sustainable growth. Indonesia joined in January 2025, after the 2024 expansion that took in Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the UAE. Saudi Arabia was invited, but its formal participation is still unclear.

I only: it is true that Kazan hosted the 16th Summit under Russia, but it ignores Indonesia's accession. Indonesia is a G20 member and Southeast Asia's largest economy. It entered as a full member in January 2025, announced by Brazil. Do not confuse it with partner countries (Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Nigeria, Uganda, Kazakhstan, Belarus, Bolivia, Cuba, Uzbekistan, Algeria), which have a lower, non-member status.
related: 16th BRICS Summit: Kazan, Russia, 22-24 October 2024; outcome document is the Kazan Declaration.
Indonesia became a full BRICS member in January 2025, announced by Brazil as chair.
17th BRICS Summit: Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, July 2025; India chairs BRICS in 2026.
New Development Bank: headquartered in Shanghai, established 2015; Dilma Rousseff is president.
Contingent Reserve Arrangement of BRICS has an initial size of 100 billion US dollars.
2023 expansion invitees: Argentina (declined), Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, UAE.
Kazan created the 'partner country' category, including Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Nigeria and Uganda.
The term 'BRIC' was coined by Jim O'Neill of Goldman Sachs in 2001; the first summit was in 2009.
statements: I — Correct: The 16th BRICS Summit was held at Kazan, Russia, under Russia's chairship. Kazan is the capital of Tatarstan. The summit took place on 22-24 October 2024 under the Russian chairship, whose slogan was 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security'. It was the first summit with the expanded membership (Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE) and produced the Kazan Declaration. A 'partner country' category was introduced there. Prime Minister Modi attended and held a bilateral meeting with Xi Jinping, which signalled easing of India-China border tensions after the patrolling arrangement.

II — Correct: Indonesia became a full BRICS member in January 2025. Brazil, the 2025 chair, announced Indonesia's admission on 6 January 2025, making it the first Southeast Asian full member. It followed the 2024 expansion that took membership to nine active members, with Saudi Arabia's status ambiguous. Indonesia is the world's largest Muslim-majority country and a G20 member, with a population of over 275 million. It was earlier a candidate for membership, and its entry strengthens the Global South character of BRICS. Partner countries such as Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam are separate from full members.

III — Incorrect: The theme was 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security', not 'Multiculturalism'. The word was altered to mislead. The theme reflects Russia's push for a multipolar world order and reform of global governance institutions. Other recent themes were: 2023 (South Africa, 15th) 'BRICS and Africa: Partnership for Mutually Accelerated Growth, Sustainable Development and Inclusive Multilateralism'; 2025 (Brazil, 17th) 'Strengthening Global South Cooperation for More Inclusive and Sustainable Governance'. India chaired in 2021 (13th, virtual) with the theme 'BRICS@15: Intra-BRICS Cooperation for Continuity, Consolidation and Consensus'.
summary: The answer is (a): statements I and II are correct. The 16th BRICS Summit was held in Kazan under Russia's chairship in October 2024, and Indonesia became a full BRICS member in January 2025. Statement III is wrong because the theme was 'Strengthening Multilateralism', not 'Multiculturalism', for Just Global Development and Security.
topic_notes: BRICS began as 'BRIC', a term coined in 2001 by Jim O'Neill of Goldman Sachs for Brazil, Russia, India and China. The first leaders' summit was at Yekaterinburg, Russia, in 2009. South Africa joined in 2010 and attended the 2011 Sanya Summit, so the group became BRICS. It has no permanent secretariat, and the chair rotates annually. Chairs: India 2021 (13th, virtual), China 2022 (14th, virtual), South Africa 2023 (15th, Johannesburg), Russia 2024 (16th, Kazan), Brazil 2025 (17th, Rio de Janeiro, 6-7 July 2025), India 2026. Expansion: at Johannesburg in 2023, six countries were invited (Argentina, Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, UAE). Argentina declined, and the others joined from 1 January 2024, though Saudi Arabia has not formally confirmed. Indonesia joined in January 2025. Kazan introduced 'partner countries': Algeria, Belarus, Bolivia, Cuba, Kazakhstan, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan and Vietnam, with some of these confirmed later. Institutions: the New Development Bank (NDB) was set up in 2014-15 with headquarters in Shanghai. Its first president was K.V. Kamath, and Dilma Rousseff has been president since 2023. The Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA) has a corpus of 100 billion dollars. Other initiatives: BRICS Pay and the discussion around de-dollarisation, the Customs Cooperation Agreement, and the Agriculture Research Platform. Themes of recent summits reflect multilateralism, Global South solidarity and inclusive governance. India's priorities include UNSC reform, counter-terrorism, and development financing. Related groupings that UPSC tests are the SCO, G20, G7, QUAD and IBSA. Remember that BRICS has no charter and decides by consensus.

question:
Consider the following statements about Lokpal :
I. The power of Lokpal applies to public servants of India, but not to the Indian public servants posted outside India. Il. The Chairperson or a Member shall not be a Member of the Parliament or a Member of the Legislature of any State or Union Territory, and only the Chief Justice of India, whether incumbent or retired, has to be its Chairperson. Ill. The Chairperson or a Member shall not be a person of less than forty-five years of age on the date of assuming office as the Chairperson or Member, as the case may be.
IV. Lokpal cannot inquire into the allegations of corruption against a sitting Prime Minister of India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
options: None of the above statements is correct
subject: Polity
detail: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 (in force from 16 January 2014) created the Lokpal at the Centre. The body has a Chairperson and up to 8 Members, of whom 50% must be judicial members and 50% must come from SC, ST, OBC, minorities and women. Section 3 sets eligibility: the Chairperson must be either the former Chief Justice of India, a former Supreme Court Judge, or an eminent person with at least 25 years of expertise in anti-corruption policy, vigilance, law, public administration, finance and similar fields. So the CJI is not the only possible Chairperson. Members must not be MPs or legislators, and the minimum age is 45 years. Section 14 covers the Prime Minister, subject to exceptions: international relations, external and internal security, public order, atomic energy and space. Any inquiry against the PM needs an in-camera hearing, and a two-thirds approval of the full Lokpal bench is needed to start it. Section 14 also covers public servants in India and abroad. Elimination: I is wrong (jurisdiction extends abroad), II is wrong (CJI-only claim), IV is wrong (PM is covered with safeguards). Only III remains, so (a).
explanations: Correct. Only statement III is right: the minimum age of 45 years is in Section 3 of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013.

Wrong. Statement II is false because the Chairperson need not be the CJI. A former Supreme Court judge or an eminent person with 25 years of expertise can also be appointed. Statement III is true, but II fails.
Wrong. Statement I is false because the Act covers public servants posted abroad. Statement IV is false because the PM is covered, with safeguards.
Wrong. Statement III is correct, so it cannot be true that none of the statements is correct.
keyfact: Lokpal members must be at least 45 years old; the Chairperson need not be the CJI, and the PM is covered with safeguards.
option_notes: Statement III only: this is the correct option. It reflects the age rule in Section 3, under which Lokpal's Chairperson and Members must be at least 45 years old on assuming office. The Chairperson and Members hold office for 5 years or until age 70. The Chairperson is paid a salary equal to that of the CJI, and Members are paid equal to Supreme Court judges. The body has an inquiry wing and a prosecution wing.

Statements II and III: this is wrong because II is false. The Chairperson need not be the CJI, as the Act allows a former CJI, a former Supreme Court judge or an eminent person with 25 years of expertise. The Lokpal has a maximum of 8 Members plus the Chairperson. Of the Members, 4 must be judicial and 50% must be from SC, ST, OBC, minority or women categories.

Statements I and IV: this is wrong because both statements are false. The Act applies to public servants in India and abroad. The Prime Minister is covered but with exclusions for security, foreign affairs, atomic energy, space and public order. It also requires an in-camera inquiry and approval from two-thirds of the full bench before proceeding.

None of the statements is correct: this is wrong because III is correct. It is a standard UPSC distractor. The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 was passed after the 2011 anti-corruption movement led by Anna Hazare. It received Presidential assent on 1 January 2014. The first Lokpal was appointed only in March 2019 under the Chairpersonship of Justice P. C. Ghose.
related: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 came into force on 16 January 2014.
Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose was India's first Lokpal Chairperson (March 2019).
Lokpal consists of a Chairperson and up to 8 Members, with 50% judicial members.
Term of the Chairperson and Members is 5 years or until age 70.
Lokayuktas for states were required within one year of the Act's commencement.
The PM is covered by Lokpal, but not on international relations, security, public order, atomic energy or space.
The Selection Committee has the PM, Lok Sabha Speaker, Leader of Opposition, CJI or nominee and an eminent jurist.
The 1st Administrative Reforms Commission (1966) first recommended Lokpal and Lokayukta.
statements: I — Incorrect: The Act's jurisdiction extends to public servants in India and also to those posted outside India. Section 1(2) says the Act extends to the whole of India and applies to public servants within and outside India. Lokpal covers the PM, Ministers, MPs, Group A to D officials, and central government employees. It also covers chairpersons, members, officers and directors of bodies set up by Parliament or funded or controlled by the Centre. It covers entities receiving foreign donations above Rs 10 lakh a year under FCRA.

II — Incorrect: The first part is true, since Members cannot be MPs or legislators. The second part is false, because the Chairperson need not be the Chief Justice of India. Eligible persons include a former CJI, a former Supreme Court judge, or an eminent person of impeccable integrity and outstanding ability with 25 years of relevant expertise. Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose, a former Supreme Court judge, became the first Chairperson in March 2019. Justice A. M. Khanwilkar became Chairperson in 2024.

III — Correct: Section 3 of the Act provides that the Chairperson or a Member shall not be a person of less than 45 years of age on the date of assuming office. Other disqualifications include being a convicted person, holding any office of profit, or being connected with a political party. The Chairperson and Members must also not carry on any business or profession. Appointment is made by the President on the recommendation of a selection committee. The term is 5 years or until age 70, whichever is earlier.

IV — Incorrect: The Prime Minister is within Lokpal's ambit under Section 14, but with safeguards. Matters of international relations, external and internal security, public order, atomic energy and space are excluded. A complaint against the PM can be considered only by the full Lokpal bench, with at least two-thirds of the members approving the inquiry. Any proceedings against the PM must be held in camera. If the complaint is dismissed, the records cannot be published or made available to anyone.
summary: The answer is (a): only statement III is correct. The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 bars appointment of anyone under 45 years of age as Chairperson or Member. The other three statements misstate the Act's jurisdiction, eligibility for Chairperson, and coverage of the Prime Minister.
topic_notes: The Lokpal is India's statutory anti-corruption ombudsman at the Centre, set up under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013. The Act received assent on 1 January 2014 and came into force on 16 January 2014. Lokayuktas are the equivalent state bodies, and states were required to establish them within one year. The idea of an ombudsman was first proposed in 1966 by the First Administrative Reforms Commission (chair: Morarji Desai, later K. Hanumanthaiya), and the Lokpal Bill was first introduced in 1968. Sweden's ombudsman is the model. Composition: a Chairperson and up to 8 Members, with 50% judicial members and 50% from SC, ST, OBC, minorities and women. Appointment: the President appoints on the recommendation of a selection committee made up of the Prime Minister (chair), Lok Sabha Speaker, Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, CJI or a nominated Supreme Court judge, and an eminent jurist nominated by the President. A search committee prepares the panel. Term: 5 years or until age 70. Jurisdiction: the PM (with safeguards), Ministers, MPs, Group A to D officials, and entities funded by the government or receiving foreign contributions above Rs 10 lakh. Procedure: a preliminary inquiry must be completed in 90 days and investigation in 6 months. Special courts must complete trials within a year. Lokpal can attach assets of the corrupt, and complaints against public servants must be filed within 7 years. Related bodies include the Central Vigilance Commission (statutory since 2003), the CBI (Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946), and the Santhanam Committee (1964) that led to the CVC. Typical UPSC angles include composition, jurisdiction, the PM's exclusion list, and the first Chairperson.

question:
Consider the following statements in respect of the first Kho Kho World Cup :
I. The event was held in Delhi, India.
II. Indian men beat Nepal with a score of 78-40 in the final to become the World Champion in men category. Ill. Indian women beat Nepal with a score of 54-36 in the final to become the World Champion in women category. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
subject: Current Affairs
detail: The inaugural Kho Kho World Cup was held at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium, New Delhi, from 13 to 19 January 2025. It was organised by the Kho Kho Federation of India (KKFI) with 20 men's teams and 19 women's teams from about 23 countries. India won both titles, beating Nepal in both finals. The women's final score was 78-40 and the men's final score was 54-36. Statements II and III have these scores swapped, so both are incorrect. The question tests whether you remember the actual scores rather than just the winners. Elimination logic: Statement I is certainly true, which rules out (b), since it excludes I. Options (c) and (d) both include III, so they stand or fall on whether the women's score was 54-36. It was not; 54-36 was the men's score. That leaves (a) as the only option consistent with the official answer. Remember that India's captains were Pratik Waikar (men) and Priyanka Ingle (women). Turn Up was the Nepal-vs-India rivalry theme, and the trophy ceremony was graced by dignitaries including the Sports Minister.
explanations: Correct: Statement I is true (New Delhi), and the scores in II and III are swapped, so only I is correct.
Incorrect: II and III both state the wrong scores for the final, because 78-40 was the women's score and 54-36 was the men's score.
Incorrect: Statement III attributes 54-36 to the women, but that was the men's score; the women won 78-40.
Incorrect: Statements II and III are both factually wrong on the scores, so I, II and III cannot all be correct.
keyfact: First Kho Kho World Cup (New Delhi, Jan 2025): India beat Nepal in both finals, men 54-36 and women 78-40.
option_notes: Statement I only: the venue claim. The first Kho Kho World Cup was held 13 to 19 January 2025 at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium, New Delhi, organised by the Kho Kho Federation of India. India won both the men's and women's titles, with Nepal as runner-up in both. This is the official answer, because the scores in the other statements are interchanged.

Statements II and III only: both rely on the final scores, but they are swapped. Men won 54-36 and women won 78-40. A student who remembers only that India beat Nepal in both finals could be tempted into this option, which is why the exact scores matter. It also wrongly excludes the true venue statement.

Statements I and III: this combines the correct venue with the women's score given as 54-36. The actual women's final score was 78-40 and the men's was 54-36, so III is wrong. The option is a trap for those who remember the venue but muddle the scoreline between the two categories.

Statements I, II and III: this would require both final scores to be correctly assigned. They are not, since the numbers are reversed between men and women. Only the venue is accurate. India's wins in both categories are real, but the scores in these statements make the option incorrect.

statements: I — Correct: The tournament was hosted in New Delhi, India. Facts: The first Kho Kho World Cup ran from 13 to 19 January 2025 at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium, New Delhi. It was organised by the Kho Kho Federation of India with 20 men's and 19 women's teams. The mascot was Tenali, and the event was inaugurated with the aim of getting Kho Kho into the Olympics and the Asian Games. Group stages preceded knockouts. Nepal was the runner-up in both categories, and the matches were broadcast widely.

II — Incorrect: The Indian men beat Nepal 54-36, not 78-40, in the final. Facts: India's men's team was captained by Pratik Waikar, and Sachin Bhargo and Aditya Ganpule were notable players. Nepal's men were the runners-up. Kho Kho matches consist of two innings with chasing and defending turns of 9 minutes each, and the format used was the standard one. Scoring is by points per dismissal. The men's title was India's first World Cup crown in this sport, and the final was held on 19 January 2025.

III — Incorrect: The Indian women beat Nepal 78-40, not 54-36, in the final. Facts: Priyanka Ingle captained the women's side, which won the inaugural women's World Cup. The margin of 38 points was larger than the men's margin of 18. Nepal's women finished as runners-up. The win came a day after India's men took the title, giving India a double. Women's Kho Kho has a long history in India, with Maharashtra and Odisha being strong centres of the sport.
summary: The answer is (a): only Statement I is correct. The first Kho Kho World Cup was held in New Delhi in January 2025, but the final scores quoted in Statements II and III are wrong, even though India won both the men's and women's titles by beating Nepal.
topic_notes: Kho Kho is an indigenous Indian tag sport, played on a rectangular court with two nine-minute turns of chasing and defending in each of two innings. Nine players take the field per side, with eight chasers sitting and one active chaser. Its origin is traced to Maharashtra, and the Kho Kho Federation of India (KKFI) governs it; the international body is the International Kho Kho Federation (IKKF), and the Kho Kho World Cup is organised by the KKFI with IKKF backing. The first World Cup was held 13 to 19 January 2025 at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium, New Delhi. It featured 20 men's and 19 women's teams from around 23 countries. India won both finals against Nepal: the men won 54-36 and the women won 78-40. Captains were Pratik Waikar (men) and Priyanka Ingle (women). The sport has been included in the Asian Games discussion and Indian national events such as the Khelo India Games, and the Ultimate Kho Kho league began in 2022. Awards: the Arjuna Award has been given to Kho Kho players. UPSC could next ask about the host city and venue, the finalists, the number of teams, the captains, the federation, or the rules of play. question:
Consider the following statements :
I. In the finals of the 45th Chess Olympiad held in 2024, Gukesh Dommaraju became the world’s youngest winner after defeating the Russian player Ian Nepomniachtchi. Il. Abhimanyu Mishra, an American chess player, holds the record of becoming world’s youngest ever Grandmaster. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
subject: Current Affairs
detail: The 45th Chess Olympiad was held in Budapest, Hungary, in September 2024. It is a team event with no knockout final and no head-to-head 'finals' between two players, so the premise of Statement I is flawed. India won gold in both the Open and Women's sections for the first time. Gukesh Dommaraju played on board 1 for India and won an individual gold medal on that board. His record as youngest undisputed World Champion came in December 2024 at Singapore, where he beat China's Ding Liren (not Ian Nepomniachtchi) 7.5-6.5 in game 14, at age 18. Nepomniachtchi was the 2023 Candidates winner and lost the 2023 title match to Ding, and he plays under a neutral FIDE flag as a Russian player. Statement II is factually correct: Abhimanyu Mishra broke Sergey Karjakin's 2002 record (12 years, 7 months) in Budapest in June 2021. Elimination: since I is wrong, (a), (c) are out; since II is right, (d) is out, leaving (b).
explanations: Wrong: Statement I is incorrect because the Olympiad has no individual final and Gukesh's record win was over Ding Liren at the World Championship, so 'I only' cannot be right.
Correct: Statement II is true because Abhimanyu Mishra became the youngest Grandmaster ever in 2021, while Statement I is false.
Wrong: this needs Statement I to be true, but I conflates the Olympiad with the World Championship and names the wrong opponent.
Wrong: Statement II is accurate, so 'neither' is incorrect.
keyfact: Youngest GM ever is Abhimanyu Mishra (2021); Gukesh's youngest World Champion title (2024) came against Ding Liren, not Nepomniachtchi.
option_notes: Option (a) 'I only' would mean only the Gukesh statement is valid. It is not: the 45th Olympiad (Budapest, 2024) is a team event, and India won gold in both Open and Women's sections. Gukesh won individual gold on board 1. His youngest-ever World Champion title came later in December 2024, defeating China's Ding Liren in Singapore. Nepomniachtchi was not his opponent in that title match.

Option (b) 'II only' is the correct choice. It reflects that Abhimanyu Mishra, of the USA and of Indian descent, holds the record as the youngest GM, set in June 2021 at 12 years, 4 months, 25 days in Budapest. He surpassed Sergey Karjakin's 2002 record. FIDE awards the GM title for three norms and a 2500 rating. Mishra was born in 2009 in New Jersey.

Option (c) 'Both I and II' would require both statements to be true. Statement II is true but Statement I is not, because the Olympiad has no finals between two players and Gukesh did not beat Nepomniachtchi for a title. At the 2024 Olympiad, India's Open team scored a record 21 of 22 match points. Gukesh's title win was in the World Championship match against Ding Liren.

Option (d) 'Neither I nor II' would mean both are false. Statement II is actually true: Abhimanyu Mishra is the youngest GM in history. Statement I is the false one. Gukesh did become the youngest undisputed World Champion at 18 in 2024, but against Ding Liren, and not in an Olympiad. Nepomniachtchi is a Russian GM who has played Candidates tournaments and the 2021 and 2023 title matches, losing to Magnus Carlsen and Ding respectively.
related: Youngest GM ever: Abhimanyu Mishra (USA), 12 years, 4 months, 25 days, 2021.
