statements: 1 — Correct: PMMY targets non-corporate, non-farm small and micro enterprises.
2 — Correct: The loan categories are Shishu, Kishor and Tarun.
3 — Correct: The scheme was launched on 8 April 2015.
subject: Indian Economy
summary: All three statements are correct. PMMY, launched on 8 April 2015, provides collateral-free loans to non-corporate, non-farm micro and small enterprises in the Shishu, Kishor and Tarun categories.

detail: At its 47th session in Paris in July 2025, the World Heritage Committee inscribed the Maratha Military Landscapes of India, India's 44th World Heritage Site. The serial property covers twelve forts associated with the Maratha rulers of the 17th to 19th centuries. Eleven of them are in Maharashtra: Salher, Shivneri, Lohgad, Khanderi, Raigad, Rajgad, Pratapgad, Suvarnadurg, Panhala, Vijaydurg and Sindhudurg. The twelfth, Gingee (Senji) in Tamil Nadu, is the only one outside the State. For elimination, Chittorgarh Fort is already inscribed separately as part of the Hill Forts of Rajasthan (2013). Daulatabad Fort is a Yadava and Tughlaq-era fort that is not in this nomination. Vellore Fort is a Vijayanagara-era fort in Tamil Nadu and a plausible distractor, but it is not in this nomination.
explanations: Incorrect: Vellore Fort is a Vijayanagara-era fort and is not in the nomination.
Correct: Gingee Fort in Tamil Nadu is the only fort outside Maharashtra in the group.
Incorrect: Chittorgarh is part of the Hill Forts of Rajasthan inscribed in 2013.
Incorrect: Daulatabad Fort is in Maharashtra but is not among the twelve forts.
keyfact: Maratha Military Landscapes – 12 forts, 11 in Maharashtra plus Gingee in Tamil Nadu – inscribed July 2025.
question: In July 2025 UNESCO inscribed 'Maratha Military Landscapes of India' on the World Heritage List. Which one of the following forts located outside Maharashtra is part of this serial nomination?
related: The Maratha Military Landscapes is India's 44th World Heritage Site
The 47th World Heritage Committee session was held in Paris in July 2025
Moidams of the Ahom dynasty was inscribed in 2024 as India's 43rd site
The Maratha nomination has 12 forts: 11 in Maharashtra and 1 in Tamil Nadu
subject: Current Affairs
summary: Gingee Fort in Tamil Nadu is the one fort in the Maratha Military Landscapes nomination located outside Maharashtra. The serial site covers twelve forts, eleven in Maharashtra and one in Tamil Nadu.
topic: Art & Culture: UNESCO World Heritage Sites

detail: Debtors left after the further write-off = 8,00,000 − 40,000 = ₹7,60,000. The required closing provision is 5% of this, which is ₹38,000. The opening provision is ₹30,000, so the extra provision to be created is ₹8,000. Total bad debts are the ₹12,000 already in the trial balance plus the ₹40,000 further written off, which is ₹52,000. The P&L charge is 52,000 + 8,000 = ₹60,000. Common traps: forgetting the bad debts already in the trial balance (giving ₹48,000), ignoring the opening provision and charging the full new provision (giving ₹90,000), or omitting the provision change (giving ₹52,000). Provision is always computed on the debtors balance after the further bad debts are written off, and only the net change is charged to the P&L.
explanations: Incorrect: this charges the full new provision of ₹38,000 without adjusting for the opening provision of ₹30,000.
Incorrect: this is bad debts only and ignores the additional provision required.
Incorrect: this ignores the ₹12,000 bad debts already in the trial balance (40,000 + 8,000).
keyfact: P&L charge = total bad debts + (new provision − opening provision).
question: The trial balance of a firm as on 31 March 2026 shows: Trade receivables ₹8,00,000; Provision for doubtful debts (opening) ₹30,000; Bad debts ₹12,000. Further bad debts of ₹40,000 are to be written off. The firm wants a provision for doubtful debts of 5% on the receivables remaining after writing off these further bad debts. The total amount to be charged to the Profit and Loss Account for bad debts and provision will be:
related: Provision for doubtful debts is created on the basis of prudence or conservatism.
Provision is calculated on debtors after deducting further bad debts.
Bad debts recovered later are credited to the P&L account as income.
In the balance sheet, the provision is deducted from trade receivables.
subject: Accounting & Auditing
summary: The answer is ₹60,000. Total bad debts of ₹52,000 plus a net increase in provision of ₹8,000 are charged to the P&L account.
topic: Bad debts and provision for doubtful debts

detail: 'Stoic' derives from the Greek school of Stoicism, which taught that virtue and self-control matter more than pleasure or pain. In everyday usage it means someone who bears hardship calmly. 'Hedonist' is a person who pursues pleasure as the chief aim of life, so it is the opposite. 'Epicure' is a person who enjoys fine food and drink. 'Cynic' is a person who believes people are motivated only by self-interest and distrusts their sincerity. Learn such substitutions in contrasting pairs: stoic versus hedonist, ascetic versus epicure.
explanations: Incorrect: a hedonist pursues pleasure.
Correct: a stoic is indifferent to pleasure and pain and practises self-restraint.
Incorrect: a cynic distrusts human motives.
Incorrect: an epicure enjoys refined food and drink.
keyfact: Stoic = one who bears pain and pleasure with equal calm and self-restraint.
question: Select the option that is the correct one-word substitute for: 'A person who is indifferent to pleasure or pain and practises self-restraint'
related: Ascetic: one who practises severe self-discipline and abstains from pleasures
Misanthrope: one who hates mankind
Philanthropist: one who loves mankind and helps others
Sybarite: a person devoted to luxury
subject: General English
summary: A stoic is a person who endures pain or hardship without showing feelings or complaining, and who practises self-control. The other terms relate to pleasure-seeking or distrust.

detail: Metonymy replaces the name of a thing with the name of something closely associated with it (the crown for monarchy, the bench for judges). Here the pen represents persuasion through writing and the sword represents armed force. Synecdoche is a close relative, but it uses a part for the whole or the whole for a part (for example 'hands' for workers). Pen and sword are not parts of writing and war but associated instruments, so metonymy is the better fit. Oxymoron joins contradictory terms such as 'bitter sweet'. Hyperbole is deliberate exaggeration, and the proverb is a claim about relative power, not an exaggeration of a single quality. To eliminate, ask whether the words are literally parts of the thing (synecdoche) or merely associated with it (metonymy).
explanations: Correct: the pen and the sword are associated objects that stand for writing and force.
Incorrect: synecdoche needs a part-whole relation, which is absent here.
Incorrect: there are no contradictory terms joined together.
Incorrect: the proverb compares two kinds of power and does not exaggerate a quality.
keyfact: Metonymy uses an associated thing's name; synecdoche uses a part for the whole.
question: Which one of the following is the figure of speech in the expression, "The pen is mightier than the sword"?
related: Synecdoche: 'All hands on deck'.
Metonymy: 'The White House announced a policy'.
Oxymoron: 'deafening silence'.
Litotes is deliberate understatement, such as 'not bad'.
Personification gives human qualities to non-human things.
subject: General English
summary: The answer is Metonymy. 'Pen' stands for writing or the written word, and 'sword' stands for military force, because each is closely associated with the thing it names.

detail: Receipts are classified as revenue or capital depending on whether they create a liability or reduce an asset. Revenue receipts neither create a liability nor reduce assets; they include tax revenue and non-tax revenue such as interest receipts, dividends and profits, and fees. Capital receipts either create a liability (borrowings) or reduce assets (recovery of loans, disinvestment). Recovery of loans reduces the Government's financial assets. Disinvestment proceeds reduce the Government's equity holdings. Market borrowings create debt liabilities. Dividends from PSUs are returns on investment and do not reduce the asset base, so they are non-debt, non-tax revenue receipts. Hence option d is the exception.
explanations: Capital receipt: reduces financial assets.
Capital receipt: reduces the Government's asset holdings.
Capital receipt: creates a liability.
Correct: it is a non-tax revenue receipt, not a capital receipt.
keyfact: Dividends from PSUs are revenue (non-tax) receipts; disinvestment and loan recovery are capital receipts.
options: Proceeds from disinvestment of public sector undertakings
Dividends and profits received from public sector undertakings
question: Which one of the following is NOT a component of the 'Capital Account' of the Union Government's Budget receipts?
related: Fiscal deficit = total expenditure minus (revenue receipts + non-debt capital receipts)
Non-debt capital receipts include loan recoveries and disinvestment
Revenue deficit = revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts
Interest receipts are non-tax revenue
subject: Indian Economy
summary: Dividends and profits from PSUs are non-tax revenue receipts, so they belong to the Revenue Account rather than the Capital Account. The other three create liabilities or reduce assets, so they are capital receipts.

detail: The HRA was founded in 1924 by Sachindra Nath Sanyal, Ram Prasad Bismil and others, and it conducted the Kakori train action on 9 August 1925. Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan, Roshan Singh and Rajendra Lahiri were executed. The Chittagong Armoury Raid of April 1930 was led by Surya Sen (Masterda), not Bhagat Singh. The Alipore Bomb Case of 1908 concerned Aurobindo Ghose and the Barindra Ghosh group connected with the Yugantar, following the Muzaffarpur attempt on Kingsford by Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki, and was not a Ghadar matter. The Assembly bomb of 1929 was thrown by Bhagat Singh and B.K. Dutt of the HSRA (renamed in 1928). Hence only a is right.
explanations: Correct: HRA organised the Kakori action in 1925.
Wrong: the raid was led by Surya Sen, not Bhagat Singh.
Wrong: Alipore was linked to the Yugantar group and Aurobindo, not the Ghadar Party.
Wrong: the Assembly bomb was by the HSRA members Bhagat Singh and B.K. Dutt.
keyfact: Kakori (9 August 1925) was an HRA action; Bismil, Ashfaqulla, Roshan Singh and Lahiri were hanged.
options: Kakori Train Action (1925) – Hindustan Republican Association
Chittagong Armoury Raid (1930) – Anushilan Samiti led by Bhagat Singh
Assembly Bomb Case (1929) – Indian Independence League
question: Which one of the following pairs of a revolutionary event and the organisation associated with it is correctly matched?
related: HRA was renamed Hindustan Socialist Republican Association in 1928 at Feroz Shah Kotla.
Ghadar Party was founded in 1913 in San Francisco.
Surya Sen was hanged in 1934.
Saunders was shot in Lahore in December 1928.
subject: Indian Freedom Struggle & Culture
summary: The Kakori Train Action of 1925 was carried out by the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA), so option a is correct. The other pairs mismatch events and organisations.

detail: RBI's monetary aggregates, as compiled under the Second Working Group, are defined as follows. M1 (narrow money) = currency with the public + demand deposits with the banking system + other deposits with the RBI. M2 = M1 + savings deposits with post office savings banks. M3 (broad money) = M1 + time deposits with the banking system. M4 = M3 + total post office deposits (excluding NSCs). M1 is the most liquid form of money. Option (a) describes something close to M3, since it includes time deposits. Option (b) includes banks' cash reserves, which are not held by the public and are outside M1. Option (c) adds post office savings deposits, which push the total towards M2. Elimination: recognise M1 as the 'transactions money' aggregate with only liquid components.
explanations: Incorrect. Adding time deposits yields M3, not M1.
Incorrect. Banks' reserves with the RBI are not money held by the public and are not part of M1.
Incorrect. Post office savings deposits enter at M2, and this option also omits other deposits with the RBI.
Correct. This is the standard RBI definition of M1.
keyfact: M1 = currency with public + demand deposits + other deposits with RBI; M3 = M1 + time deposits.
options: Currency with the public plus all deposits of the public with banks, including time deposits
Currency with the public plus cash reserves of banks held with the RBI
Currency with the public plus demand deposits with banks plus savings deposits with post office savings banks
Currency with the public plus demand deposits with banks plus other deposits with the RBI
question: In the context of monetary aggregates compiled by the Reserve Bank of India, M1 comprises which one of the following?
related: M3 is also called broad money.
Reserve money (M0) = currency in circulation + bankers' deposits with the RBI + other deposits with the RBI.
The money multiplier is M3 divided by reserve money.
M1 is the most liquid aggregate.
RBI also publishes liquidity aggregates L1, L2 and L3.
subject: Economy
summary: M1 equals currency with the public plus demand deposits with banks plus other deposits with the RBI. The other options bring in time deposits, bank reserves or post office savings deposits, which belong to other aggregates or to none.

detail: The 52nd Amendment Act, 1985 added the Tenth Schedule, containing the anti-defection provisions, and amended Articles 101, 102, 190 and 191. The decision on disqualification rests with the Presiding Officer of the House. In Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu (1992), the Supreme Court upheld the Schedule's validity but held the Presiding Officer's decision subject to judicial review. The 91st Amendment, 2003 deleted the provision protecting a split of one-third of a legislature party, retaining only the merger exception with two-thirds of members. It also capped the Council of Ministers at 15 percent of the House strength. The 61st Amendment lowered the voting age to 18 and the 42nd Amendment is the 'mini-Constitution'.
explanations: Incorrect: the 42nd Amendment added Fundamental Duties and altered the Preamble.
Correct: the 52nd Amendment inserted the Tenth Schedule in 1985.
Incorrect: the 61st Amendment reduced the voting age from 21 to 18.
Incorrect: the 91st Amendment strengthened the anti-defection law but did not introduce the Schedule.
keyfact: Tenth Schedule: 52nd Amendment, 1985; split exception removed by 91st Amendment, 2003.
question: The Tenth Schedule to the Constitution of India, dealing with disqualification on grounds of defection, was inserted by which one of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts?
related: Kihoto Hollohan case (1992) upheld the Tenth Schedule.
91st Amendment limits the Council of Ministers to 15 percent of the lower House.
The Presiding Officer decides disqualification questions under Paragraph 6.
Merger requires two-thirds of the legislature party.
subject: Indian Polity
summary: The 52nd Amendment Act, 1985 inserted the Tenth Schedule. The 91st Amendment of 2003 later removed the exemption for splits and limited the size of Ministries.

detail: The Doppler effect is the change in observed frequency or wavelength due to relative motion between source and observer. When a source recedes, observed wavelength lengthens (redshift for light) and the frequency of sound falls. Hubble's observations that galaxies show redshift proportional to their distance underpin the expanding universe model. In the electromagnetic spectrum, wavelength decreases and photon energy increases in the order radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma ray. So X-rays have shorter wavelength and higher energy than UV. Elimination: option a calls recession blueshift, which is wrong; option b says frequency rises for a receding sound source, which is wrong; option d reverses the X-ray/UV ordering. Only c is correct.
explanations: Incorrect: a receding source produces redshift (longer wavelength), not blueshift.
Incorrect: a receding source lowers the observed frequency of sound.
Correct: the redshift of distant galaxies shows they are moving away, consistent with an expanding universe.
Incorrect: X-rays have shorter wavelength and higher photon energy than ultraviolet rays.
keyfact: Redshift of distant galaxies indicates recession and supports the expanding universe.
options: The Doppler shift of light from a distant galaxy moving away from Earth is towards shorter wavelengths, called blueshift
The frequency of sound heard by a stationary observer increases when the source moves away from the observer
The redshift observed in the spectra of distant galaxies is interpreted as evidence that the universe is expanding
X-rays have a longer wavelength than ultraviolet rays and a lower photon energy
question: Which one of the following statements about the Doppler effect and electromagnetic radiation is correct?
related: Approaching source: blueshift and higher observed frequency
Hubble's law: recession velocity is proportional to distance
Gamma rays have the shortest wavelength in the EM spectrum
All EM waves travel at the speed of light in vacuum
subject: General Science
summary: The redshift of distant galaxies indicates they are receding, which supports an expanding universe. The other options reverse the actual relationships.

detail: The idiom derives from the legend of the Gordian knot, tied by King Gordius of Phrygia. An oracle said whoever untied it would rule Asia. Alexander the Great, instead of untying it, is said to have sliced it with his sword. Hence the phrase means resolving a seemingly insoluble problem through a forceful, creative or unconventional solution. Elimination: creating a complication is the opposite. Abandoning a task from fear misses the decisive nature. Lengthy negotiation contradicts the idea of a quick, direct stroke.
explanations: Correct: captures the bold, decisive resolution of a difficult problem.
Incorrect: this describes causing a problem, not solving it.
Incorrect: the idiom implies decisive action, not giving up.
Incorrect: the idiom implies a swift solution, not prolonged negotiation.
keyfact: Cutting the Gordian knot = solving a tangled problem by bold, direct action (Alexander the Great).
options: To solve a complex problem by a bold, decisive action
To create a complicated problem deliberately
To abandon a task midway out of fear
To settle a dispute through lengthy negotiation
question: Select the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom 'To cut the Gordian knot':
related: Gordian knot = an extremely intricate problem.
To bell the cat = to undertake a risky task for the group's benefit.
Achilles' heel = a vulnerable point.
Pandora's box = a source of unforeseen troubles.
subject: General English
summary: 'To cut the Gordian knot' means to solve an intricate problem by a bold, direct stroke rather than by patient untangling.

detail: The Census is being conducted in two phases. The first is the houselisting and housing census, held between April and September 2026 during a 30-day window chosen by each State or Union Territory. The second is the population enumeration, which includes caste enumeration. Its reference date is 1 March 2027 for most of India. For the snow-bound areas of Ladakh, Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, the reference date is 1 October 2026, so that enumeration can be done before heavy snowfall. This is also India's first digital census, with a self-enumeration option. The trap in the options is 1 October 2026, which applies only to the snow-bound areas.
explanations: Wrong, because 1 October 2026 is the reference date only for the snow-bound areas.
Correct, because the population enumeration in most of the country has a reference date of 1 March 2027.
Wrong, because 1 January 2027 is not the reference date for any part of the country.
Wrong, because April 2026 is when the houselisting phase begins, not the population enumeration reference date.
keyfact: Census 2027: reference date 1 March 2027 (1 October 2026 for snow-bound areas).
question: In the Census of India scheduled to be conducted in 2026-27, what is the reference date for the population enumeration in most parts of the country, excluding the snow-bound areas?
related: Houselisting phase runs from April to September 2026.
Caste enumeration is included in the population enumeration phase.
This is India's first digital census, with self-enumeration.
The previous Census was held in 2011; the 2021 Census was postponed.
subject: Current Affairs
summary: The reference date is 1 March 2027 for most of India. The snow-bound areas use 1 October 2026.

detail: BOD is the oxygen consumed by aerobic microbes while decomposing biodegradable organic matter. The standard test uses a 5-day incubation at 20°C (BOD5). COD uses a strong chemical oxidant, such as potassium dichromate, to oxidise both biodegradable and non-biodegradable organic matter, and it takes only a few hours. COD is therefore usually higher than BOD. High BOD means heavy organic load, which causes oxygen depletion and threatens aquatic life. Unpolluted water has BOD of about 5 mg/L or less. Elimination: statement 4 is clearly reversed, so options claiming all four are wrong. Statements 1 to 3 describe standard definitions and methods, which makes the answer three. Under CPCB norms, drinking-water source water of Class A has BOD of 2 mg/L or less.
explanations: Wrong: three statements are correct.
Wrong: this undercounts, since statements 1, 2 and 3 are all correct.
Correct: statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct, and statement 4 is reversed.
Wrong: statement 4 is false, so not all four are correct.
keyfact: High BOD means more biodegradable pollution, and COD is generally at least as high as BOD.
question:
With reference to water quality indicators, consider the following statements:
1. Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) measures the amount of oxygen required by aerobic microorganisms to decompose organic matter in water.
2. Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD) of a sample is generally equal to or higher than its BOD because chemical oxidation also covers non-biodegradable organic matter.
3. The standard BOD test is conducted over five days at 20°C, whereas COD can be determined much faster.
4. A higher BOD value generally indicates cleaner water with less organic pollution.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
related: BOD5 means five days at 20°C.
High BOD leads to oxygen depletion.
COD uses chemical oxidants such as potassium dichromate.
The CPCB classifies surface water into classes A to E.
Dissolved oxygen falls as BOD rises.
statements: 1 — Correct: BOD is oxygen demand from aerobic microbial decomposition.
2 — Correct: COD includes chemically oxidisable but non-biodegradable matter, so it is generally at least as high as BOD.
3 — Correct: BOD5 is a 5-day test at 20°C, and COD takes only hours.
4 — Incorrect: A higher BOD signals more organic pollution and lower water quality.
subject: Environment
summary: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct, so the answer is 'Only three'. A higher BOD means more biodegradable organic pollution, not cleaner water.

detail: A digital twin links a physical entity, such as a turbine, a factory, a building or even a city, to a virtual model through sensors and data flows, often over the Internet of Things. Because the model is continuously updated, engineers can test changes, predict failures and optimise operations without disturbing the real system. Applications include predictive maintenance, urban planning and healthcare modelling. Elimination: option a confuses it with ledger replication, option c invents a quantum link, and option d refers to biology and cloning. Only option b describes a live virtual counterpart used for simulation and prediction.
explanations: Incorrect: it is not a ledger duplicate.
Correct: this is the standard definition.
Incorrect: it has nothing to do with quantum entanglement.
Incorrect: it is a computational model, not a biological clone.
keyfact: A digital twin is a data-updated virtual replica of a physical asset or process.
options: A blockchain-based duplicate of a financial ledger maintained on two separate servers
A virtual replica of a physical object, system or process that is updated with real-world data and used for simulation, monitoring and prediction
A pair of quantum-entangled computers used to double processing power
A cloned biological cell line used for drug testing
question: Which one of the following best describes 'Digital Twin' technology?
related: The Internet of Things connects sensors and devices.
Predictive maintenance uses data to anticipate failures.
Edge computing processes data near its source.
Simulation models support smart-city planning.
subject: Science & Tech
summary: A digital twin is a virtual replica of a physical asset or process that is fed with real-world data. It is used to simulate, monitor and predict performance.

detail: The MPC was given statutory status through the 2016 amendment to the RBI Act, 1934 (Section 45ZB), which operationalised flexible inflation targeting. It has six members: the Governor (chairperson), the Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy, one other RBI officer nominated by the Central Board, and three external members appointed by the Central Government. Decisions are by majority of members present and voting, each having one vote, and the Governor has a second, casting vote in a tie. It is statutory, not constitutional, so Article 280 (Finance Commission) is irrelevant. The Finance Minister does not chair it. Option c is wrong because the Governor votes in every decision, not only in ties.
explanations: Correct: six members, three from the RBI, three external, with a Governor's casting vote in a tie.
Incorrect: there are six members and the RBI Governor chairs the committee.
Incorrect: the Governor has an ordinary vote plus a casting vote in a tie.
Incorrect: the MPC is statutory under the RBI Act, and Article 280 concerns the Finance Commission.
keyfact: MPC: 6 members (3 RBI, 3 external), Governor chairs with a casting vote; target 4% +/-2%.
options: It has six members, three from the RBI and three appointed by the Central Government, and the RBI Governor has a casting vote in case of a tie
It has seven members, with the Finance Minister as chairperson
It has six members, and the Governor has no vote except in the case of a tie
It is a constitutional body established under Article 280
question: In the context of monetary policy in India, which one of the following statements about the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is correct?
related: Section 45ZB of the RBI Act provides for the MPC.
The inflation target is 4% with a tolerance band of +/-2%.
The Centre notifies the inflation target every five years.
The MPC must meet at least four times a year.
If inflation stays outside the band for three consecutive quarters, the RBI must report to the government.
subject: Indian Economy
summary: The MPC has six members, three from the RBI and three nominated by the Centre. The Governor chairs it and has a casting vote only in the event of a tie, in addition to his ordinary vote.

detail: The FRBM Act, 2003 set the goals of eliminating the revenue deficit and bringing the fiscal deficit down to 3% of GDP, with targets later pushed back repeatedly. The N.K. Singh Committee (2017) recommended debt-to-GDP as the main anchor, with a target of 40% for the Centre and 20% for States (60% general government), with the fiscal deficit as the operating target. It also proposed a Fiscal Council. The Finance Act 2018 amended the FRBM Act and enshrined a debt target, and the escape clause allows deviation on grounds such as national security, war, national calamity, collapse of agriculture, structural reforms and a sharp fall in real output. Since all three statements match the legal and committee provisions, the answer is all three.
explanations: Wrong: at least two statements are correct, so only one cannot be right.
Wrong: all three statements are correct, not just two.
Correct: all three statements accurately describe the FRBM Act and the N.K. Singh Committee.
Wrong: the statements are accurate, so none is not valid.
keyfact: The N.K. Singh Committee made debt-to-GDP the anchor of fiscal policy, with the fiscal deficit as the operating target.
question:
With reference to the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) framework in India, consider the following statements:
1. The FRBM Act, 2003 as originally enacted required the Union Government to eliminate the revenue deficit and reduce the fiscal deficit to 3 per cent of GDP.
2. The N.K. Singh Committee (2017) recommended that debt-to-GDP ratio be used as the primary anchor of fiscal policy.
3. The FRBM Act as amended permits deviation from the fiscal targets only on grounds specified in the Act, such as national security, war, national calamity or a sharp fall in real output.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
related: N.K. Singh Committee recommended a debt-to-GDP target of 60% for general government.
The Committee proposed a Fiscal Council, which has not been constituted.
The FRBM Act was enacted in 2003 and came into force in 2004.
The escape clause was invoked in FY2020-21 during COVID-19.
statements: 1 — Correct: the original Act aimed at revenue deficit elimination and a 3% fiscal deficit.
2 — Correct: the Committee recommended debt as the anchor, with the fiscal deficit as an operating target.
3 — Correct: the Act lists the grounds for deviation (escape clause), including war, national security and calamity.
The 2018 amendment placed a debt ceiling for the Centre in the law, while the Committee's proposed Fiscal Council was not set up.
subject: Economy
summary: All three statements are correct. The FRBM Act targeted revenue deficit elimination and a 3% fiscal deficit, the N.K. Singh Committee made debt the anchor, and escape clauses are limited to specified grounds.

detail: In equatorial rainforests, warmth and moisture drive rapid microbial decomposition, so litter is broken down quickly and humus does not accumulate. Heavy rain leaches soluble bases such as calcium, magnesium and potassium out of the topsoil. This leaves iron and aluminium oxides, giving the characteristic red Oxisols and Ultisols, which are acidic and infertile. Roots and mycorrhizal fungi recycle nutrients straight from litter into the trees, so the nutrient cycle runs mainly through the biomass. This is why clearing the forest for agriculture quickly exhausts the soil. Since Statement-II gives the mechanism behind Statement-I, option a is correct and the other options fail.
explanations: Correct: both are true and the second explains the first.
Wrong: Statement-II is the direct explanation of Statement-I.
Wrong: Statement-II is accurate.
Wrong: Statement-I is accurate.
keyfact: In tropical rainforests, nutrients are stored in the living biomass, not in the soil.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: Soils under tropical rainforests are generally low in nutrients, although the vegetation they support is very dense and luxuriant.
Statement-II: In the hot and humid conditions of tropical rainforests, dead organic matter decomposes rapidly and heavy rainfall leaches soluble nutrients, so most nutrients are held in the living biomass rather than in the soil.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: Laterite soils form under heavy rain with alternating wet and dry seasons, through leaching.
Oxisols are typical of the Amazon and Congo basins.
Slash-and-burn (shifting) cultivation is common on poor tropical forest soils.
Mollisols of temperate grasslands are among the most fertile soils.
statements: 1 — Correct: Rainforest soils are generally nutrient-poor despite dense vegetation.
2 — Correct: Rapid decomposition and leaching leave nutrients in the biomass, and this explains Statement-I.
subject: Geography
summary: Both statements are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I. Rapid decomposition and intense leaching keep nutrients in the vegetation rather than in the soil.

detail: Mansabdari ranked officials by zat (personal rank, determining pay and status) and sawar (number of horsemen maintained). Dahsala (also called Zabti) was a revenue assessment system perfected by Todar Mal around 1580, using ten years of crop yields and prices to fix cash rates for different crop-land categories. Both are accurate. However, Dahsala concerns land revenue, while mansabdari concerns rank and service; neither causally explains the other. Hence option b. In statement-I/II questions, test separately for truth and then for explanatory relationship.
explanations: Wrong: both are true, but Dahsala does not explain the zat-sawar structure.
Correct: both true and unrelated causally.
Wrong: Statement-II is also correct.
Wrong: Statement-I is correct.
keyfact: Zat = personal rank and pay; sawar = cavalry obligation; Dahsala = ten-year average revenue assessment.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: Under Akbar's Mansabdari system, the zat rank indicated a mansabdar's personal status and salary, while the sawar rank indicated the number of cavalrymen he was obliged to maintain.
Statement-II: Akbar introduced the Dahsala system of land revenue assessment, associated with Raja Todar Mal, based on average produce and prices of the preceding ten years.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: Akbar's Zabt system was based on measurement of land (bigha).
Jagirs were assignments of revenue to mansabdars.
Du-aspah sih-aspah was an Jahangir-era enhancement of sawar rank.
Sher Shah's revenue system used measurement and fixed rates (rai).
subject: Medieval History
summary: Both statements are correct, but they describe different institutions: the military-administrative ranking and the revenue system. One does not explain the other.

detail: Chapter V of the Code on Wages, 2019 deals with bonus and replaces the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965. Every employee drawing wages up to the notified ceiling is entitled to bonus for an accounting year, provided he has worked for not less than thirty days in that year. The minimum bonus is 8.33 per cent of wages earned, and the maximum is 20 per cent, as under the earlier Act. Candidates often confuse the thirty-day rule with the 240-day condition used for annual leave or retrenchment protection. Sixty and ninety days are invented distractors that look plausible. The rule is a low threshold designed to extend bonus to short-service and seasonal employees.
explanations: Correct: the Code requires work of not less than thirty days in the accounting year.
Incorrect: sixty days is not the statutory minimum.
Incorrect: ninety days is not the statutory minimum.
Incorrect: 240 days is associated with continuous service for other benefits, not bonus eligibility.
keyfact: Code on Wages: bonus needs at least 30 days of work in the accounting year; 8.33% minimum, 20% maximum.
question: Under the Code on Wages, 2019, an employee is entitled to be paid bonus in an accounting year only if he has worked for not less than how many days in that year?
related: Minimum bonus is 8.33 per cent of wages earned.
Maximum bonus is 20 per cent of wages earned.
The Code on Wages replaces the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965.
The Code on Wages also subsumes the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 and the Minimum Wages Act, 1948.
subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: The correct answer is thirty days. Under the Code on Wages, 2019, an eligible employee must have worked for at least thirty days in the accounting year to be entitled to bonus. The annual limit of 240 days relates to other statutory benefits, not bonus.

detail: Under the IBC, a financial creditor, operational creditor or the corporate debtor itself can apply to the Adjudicating Authority, which for companies is the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), not the Debt Recovery Tribunal. The minimum default needed to trigger CIRP was raised from ₹1 lakh to ₹1 crore in March 2020 to shield small businesses. The Committee of Creditors is made up of financial creditors, and it takes the key decisions, including approval of the resolution plan. Operational creditors do not have voting rights in it. The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India was established under the IBC itself in 2016 as the regulator. Elimination logic: option (a) names the wrong forum, (c) reverses the composition of the Committee of Creditors, and (d) names the wrong parent statute.
explanations: Wrong: the Adjudicating Authority for corporate insolvency is the NCLT, and the DRT handles insolvency of individuals and partnership firms.
Correct: the minimum default threshold is ₹1 crore.
Wrong: the Committee of Creditors comprises financial creditors, and operational creditors do not have voting rights in it.
Wrong: the IBBI was set up under the IBC, 2016, and not under the Companies Act, 2013.
keyfact: Under the IBC, CIRP needs a minimum default of ₹1 crore and is heard by the NCLT.
options: Corporate insolvency resolution process for companies is initiated before the Debt Recovery Tribunal.
The minimum amount of default required to initiate a corporate insolvency resolution process is ₹1 crore.
The Committee of Creditors consists exclusively of operational creditors.
The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India is a regulatory body established under the Companies Act, 2013.
question: With reference to the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 in India, which one of the following statements is correct?
related: The IBC consolidated earlier insolvency laws and replaced the SICA and the Presidency Towns Insolvency Act.
The Code provides a moratorium once CIRP is admitted.
The Adjudicating Authority for individuals and partnership firms is the Debt Recovery Tribunal.
Resolution plan approval requires the vote of the Committee of Creditors by the prescribed majority.
subject: Economy
summary: The minimum default threshold for initiating CIRP is ₹1 crore, following the 2020 notification raising it from ₹1 lakh. Corporate insolvency matters go to the NCLT, the Committee of Creditors is based on financial creditors, and the IBBI was set up under the IBC itself.

detail: Article 324 vests superintendence, direction and control of elections to Parliament, State Legislatures and the offices of President and Vice-President in the Election Commission. Under Article 324(5), the CEC cannot be removed except in like manner and on like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court. Other Election Commissioners can be removed only on the CEC's recommendation. Option b is wrong because the Constitution leaves the number to the President to fix. Option c is wrong because State Election Commissions conduct local body elections under Articles 243K and 243ZA. Option d is wrong because the Speaker and Deputy Speaker are elected by the members of the Lok Sabha themselves.
explanations: Correct: Article 324(5) proviso gives this protection to the CEC.
Wrong: the number is fixed by the President, not the Constitution.
Wrong: local body elections are conducted by State Election Commissions.
Wrong: the Speaker and Deputy Speaker are elected by Lok Sabha members.
keyfact: CEC is removable like a Supreme Court Judge; other ECs only on CEC's recommendation.
options: The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from office in the same manner as a Judge of the Supreme Court.
The Constitution fixes the number of Election Commissioners at two in addition to the Chief Election Commissioner.
The Election Commission conducts elections to Panchayats and Municipalities.
The Election Commission conducts elections to the offices of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the Deputy Speaker.
question: With reference to the Election Commission of India, which one of the following statements is correct?
related: Article 324 establishes the Election Commission.
Article 325 bars exclusion from electoral rolls on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex.
Article 326 provides adult suffrage.
Voting age was lowered to 18 by the 61st Amendment.
subject: Indian Polity
summary: The Chief Election Commissioner enjoys security of tenure and can be removed only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court Judge, under the proviso to Article 324(5).

detail: Check MANAGER against NZOZHFS: M+1 = N, A-1 = Z, N+1 = O, A-1 = Z, G+1 = H, E-1 = D, R+1 = S. The code would then be NZOZHDS, but the given code has F in the sixth place, which does not fit. The given code NZOZHFS is therefore only consistent if the sixth letter E goes to F, meaning +1. So the pattern is not strictly alternating. The pattern that fits is +1, -1, +1, -1, +1, +1, +1. Applying the same rule to OFFICER gives O+1 = P, F-1 = E, F+1 = G, I-1 = H, C+1 = D, E+1 = F, R+1 = S, which is PEGHDFS. Option a matches.
explanations: Correct. It follows the +1, -1, +1, -1, +1, +1, +1 pattern deduced from MANAGER.
Wrong. The fifth letter C+1 should be D, not J, and the sixth should be F.
Wrong. The sixth letter E+1 should be F, not D.
Wrong. The second letter F-1 should be E, not G.
keyfact: In letter coding, derive the shift for every position from the example before applying it.
question: In a certain code language, 'MANAGER' is written as 'NZOZHFS'. Using the same logic, how will 'OFFICER' be written?
related: Check each position separately in coding-decoding questions.
Look for alternating shifts of +1 and -1.
Opposite-letter coding pairs A with Z, B with Y and so on.
Write out letter positions (A=1 to Z=26) to check shifts.
subject: Quantitative Aptitude & Reasoning
summary: The answer is PEGHDFS. The letters alternately move one step forward and one step backward: +1, -1, +1, -1, and so on. Applying this to OFFICER gives P, E, G, H, D, F, S.

detail: Lagrange points are positions where the gravitational pulls of two large bodies and the orbital motion of a small object balance. L1 lies between the Sun and the Earth, about 1.5 million km from Earth. A spacecraft there can watch the Sun continuously without eclipses or occultations. Aditya-L1 was launched by PSLV-C57 in September 2023 and inserted into its halo orbit on 6 January 2024. L2 lies on the far side of Earth from the Sun and suits deep-space telescopes such as JWST. Earth-Moon points are used for lunar communication relays. A sun-synchronous polar orbit suits Earth-observation satellites, not solar observatories. To eliminate options, identify the target (the Sun) and the need for an uninterrupted sunward view. That leaves only L1.
explanations: Correct. Aditya-L1 is in a halo orbit around the Sun-Earth L1 point, giving continuous solar viewing.
Incorrect. Sun-Earth L2 is on the anti-Sun side and is used for space telescopes such as JWST.
Incorrect. The Earth-Moon points relate to lunar missions and are not used by Aditya-L1.
Incorrect. A low Earth sun-synchronous orbit is used for remote-sensing satellites, and Earth would intermittently block the Sun.
keyfact: Aditya-L1 is in a halo orbit around the Sun-Earth L1 point, reached on 6 January 2024.
options: A halo orbit around the Sun-Earth L1 Lagrange point, roughly 1.5 million km from Earth
A halo orbit around the Sun-Earth L2 Lagrange point, roughly 1.5 million km from Earth
A halo orbit around the Earth-Moon L2 Lagrange point
A sun-synchronous polar orbit about 800 km above Earth
question: India's first dedicated solar observatory mission, Aditya-L1, which reached its final operational position in January 2024, is placed in which of the following?
related: Aditya-L1 was launched on PSLV-C57 on 2 September 2023.
Chandrayaan-3 landed near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023, which is now celebrated as National Space Day.
The Chandrayaan-3 landing site is named Shiv Shakti Point.
Aditya-L1's payloads include VELC, a coronagraph, among its seven instruments.
subject: Current Affairs
summary: The answer is (a). Aditya-L1 sits in a halo orbit around the Sun-Earth L1 point, which gives it an uninterrupted view of the Sun.

detail: Chronology questions on reform and political organisations require accurate dates. The Prarthana Samaj was founded in Bombay in 1867 by Atmaram Pandurang, with M.G. Ranade and R.G. Bhandarkar later associated with it; it was inspired by the Brahmo Samaj and emphasised monotheism and social reform. Jyotirao Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in Pune in 1873 to secure equality for lower castes and challenge Brahmin dominance. Dayananda Saraswati established the Arya Samaj in Bombay in 1875, with the slogan 'Back to the Vedas'. The Indian Association was formed in Calcutta in 1876 by Surendranath Banerjee and Anandamohan Bose, a precursor of the Indian National Congress. Arranging them as 1867, 1873, 1875, 1876 shows that Prarthana Samaj precedes all others.
explanations: Incorrect: the Satyashodhak Samaj was founded in 1873, later than the Prarthana Samaj.
Incorrect: the Arya Samaj was founded in 1875.
Correct: the Prarthana Samaj was founded in 1867, earlier than all the others listed.
Incorrect: the Indian Association was established in 1876, the latest in the list.
keyfact: Prarthana Samaj 1867, Satyashodhak Samaj 1873, Arya Samaj 1875, Indian Association 1876.
question: Which one of the following organisations was founded the earliest?
related: The Brahmo Samaj was founded in 1828 by Raja Ram Mohan Roy.
The Ramakrishna Mission was founded in 1897.
The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885.
The Deccan Education Society was set up in 1884.
subject: Modern History
summary: The Prarthana Samaj, founded in Bombay in 1867, is the earliest. The Satyashodhak Samaj came in 1873, the Arya Samaj in 1875 and the Indian Association in 1876.

detail: Intransigent comes from the Latin 'in-' (not) plus 'transigere' (to come to an agreement). It describes a person or stance that refuses to compromise or abandon a position, typically in negotiations such as wage settlements or policy talks. To answer synonym questions, first work out the core sense of the word, then test each option. 'Flexible' is an antonym because it denotes willingness to adapt. 'Hesitant' indicates reluctance or uncertainty, which is not the same as firm refusal. 'Gullible' means easily deceived and has no link to rigidity. Only 'Uncompromising' matches the sense of rigid, unyielding firmness. Related words are obdurate, adamant, inflexible and implacable.
explanations: Flexible is the opposite in meaning, so it is wrong.
Uncompromising means refusing to make concessions, which is exactly what intransigent means.
Hesitant means slow to act through uncertainty, which is not the same as stubborn refusal.
Gullible means easily tricked and is unrelated.
keyfact: Intransigent = refusing to compromise; synonym uncompromising.
question: Select the option that is most nearly the SYNONYM of the word: "INTRANSIGENT"
related: Antonym of intransigent: amenable, accommodating, pliant
Obdurate and adamant are close synonyms of intransigent
Ephemeral means short-lived
Laconic means using few words
subject: General English
summary: INTRANSIGENT means unwilling to change one's views or to compromise, so 'Uncompromising' is the closest synonym. The other options describe qualities that are opposite or unrelated.

detail: Article 66 provides that the Vice-President is elected by an electoral college consisting of the members of both Houses of Parliament. The Article does not restrict this to elected members. Therefore nominated members of the Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha can vote, which is why Statement-II explains Statement-I. The election uses proportional representation by the single transferable vote, and the ballot is secret. In contrast, the President's electoral college under Article 54 includes only the elected members of both Houses and of the State Legislative Assemblies, including those of Delhi and Puducherry. Nominated members and members of Legislative Councils do not vote there. State legislators take no part in the Vice-President's election. To eliminate options, since Statement-II is true, option (c) is wrong, and since Statement-I is also true, option (d) is wrong. The remaining choice between (a) and (b) depends on whether the college definition explains the right of nominated members. It does, because the college includes all members.
explanations: Correct: both are true, and the inclusion of all members in the electoral college is exactly why nominated members vote.
Incorrect: Statement-II does explain Statement-I.
Incorrect: Statement-II is also correct.
Incorrect: Statement-I is correct.
keyfact: Vice-President is elected by all members of both Houses, including nominated ones; for the President, only elected members vote.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: Nominated members of both Houses of Parliament are entitled to vote in the election of the Vice-President of India.
Statement-II: The Vice-President is elected by an electoral college consisting of all the members of both Houses of Parliament.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: Only elected members of Parliament and State Assemblies vote in the Presidential election.
State legislators have no role in the Vice-President's election.
Vice-President's term is five years, but he continues until his successor enters office.
Vice-President is ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha under Article 89.
Disputes about the election are decided by the Supreme Court under Article 71.
statements: 1 — Correct: Nominated members of both Houses are part of the electoral college for the Vice-President and can vote.
2 — Correct: Article 66 constitutes the electoral college from all members of both Houses, so it explains why nominated members vote.
subject: Polity
summary: Both statements are correct, and Statement-II explains Statement-I. Under Article 66, the electoral college for the Vice-President comprises all members of both Houses, elected and nominated, so nominated members vote. This differs from the Presidential election, where nominated members cannot vote.

detail: The WTO Agreement on Agriculture sorts domestic support into boxes. The Amber Box covers trade-distorting support, such as market price support and input or output subsidies linked to production, and is subject to reduction commitments. Procurement at administered prices such as MSP is treated as market price support. A de minimis exemption allows support below a threshold percentage of the value of production: 5 per cent for developed countries and 10 per cent for developing countries. Statement 2 gives the developed-country figure, so it is incorrect. The Green Box covers measures with no or minimal trade-distorting effect, such as research, extension services and decoupled income support, and these are exempt from reduction commitments. Hence only 1 and 3 are correct.
explanations: Correct: statements 1 and 3 are correct and 2 is wrong.
Wrong: statement 2 is incorrect because the limit is 10 per cent for developing countries.
Wrong: statement 1 is also correct, and statement 2 is incorrect.
Wrong: statement 2 is incorrect.
keyfact: De minimis under AoA: 5% for developed countries, 10% for developing countries.
question:
With reference to the WTO Agreement on Agriculture, consider the following statements:

1. Market price support given through administered prices such as procurement at minimum support prices is generally categorised under the Amber Box.
2. For developing countries, the de minimis threshold for Amber Box support is 5 per cent of the value of agricultural production.
3. Green Box subsidies are not subject to reduction commitments, as they are meant to cause no more than minimal trade distortion.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: The Blue Box covers payments linked to production-limiting programmes.
Public stockholding for food security has special conditions under Green Box rules and a related peace clause arrangement at the 2013 Bali Ministerial.
The Agreement on Agriculture came into force in 1995 with the WTO.
The de minimis limit is 5 per cent for developed and 10 per cent for developing countries.
statements: 1 — Correct: administered-price procurement is classified as market price support in the Amber Box.
2 — Incorrect: the developing-country de minimis limit is 10 per cent; 5 per cent applies to developed countries.
3 — Correct: Green Box measures are exempt from reduction commitments as they cause minimal trade distortion.
subject: Economy
summary: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The de minimis limit for developing countries is 10 per cent, not 5 per cent, which is the limit for developed countries.

detail: The Forty-second Amendment Act, 1976 inserted Article 43A in Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy). It directs the State to take steps, by suitable legislation or in any other way, to secure the participation of workers in the management of undertakings, establishments or other organisations engaged in any industry. It is the constitutional basis for workers' participation in management, for example through works committees and joint management councils. Elimination: option a describes Article 43 (living wage and decent standard of life). Option c describes Article 42 (just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief). Option d describes Article 39(d) (equal pay for equal work for men and women). All four are labour-related Directive Principles, so the article numbers must be memorised accurately.
explanations: Incorrect: this is Article 43, which deals with living wage and conditions of work.
Correct: Article 43A deals with participation of workers in management.
Incorrect: this is Article 42, which deals with humane conditions of work and maternity relief.
Incorrect: this is Article 39(d), which deals with equal pay for equal work.
keyfact: Article 43A (42nd Amendment, 1976) is the Directive Principle on workers' participation in management.
options: secure a living wage and conditions of work ensuring a decent standard of life for all workers
secure the participation of workers in the management of undertakings, establishments or other organisations engaged in any industry
make provision for securing just and humane conditions of work and for maternity relief
ensure equal pay for equal work for both men and women
question: Article 43A of the Constitution of India, inserted by the Constitution (Forty-second Amendment) Act, 1976, directs the State to take steps to:
related: Article 43 directs the State to secure a living wage and a decent standard of life for workers, and promotes cottage industries.
Article 42 deals with just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief.
Article 39(d) deals with equal pay for equal work for men and women.
Article 43B, on cooperative societies, was added by the Ninety-seventh Amendment, 2011.
Article 19(1)(c) guarantees the right to form associations or unions.
subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: The correct answer is option b. Article 43A, a Directive Principle, directs the State to secure workers' participation in the management of industrial undertakings.
topic: Constitution - Directive Principles relating to Labour

detail: Parliament's financial committees are the Public Accounts Committee (PAC), the Estimates Committee and the Committee on Public Undertakings (COPU). The PAC has 22 members, 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha. It scrutinises the CAG's audit reports and the appropriation accounts. A Minister cannot be a member, which keeps the committee independent of the executive. Its Chairman is appointed by the Speaker, and by convention since 1967 the post has gone to a member of the Opposition. The Estimates Committee has 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha, and Rajya Sabha has no representation on it. It examines the estimates and suggests economies, so it is sometimes called a 'continuous economy committee'. COPU has 22 members (15 Lok Sabha, 7 Rajya Sabha). To eliminate options, note that statement 3 is false, which rules out 'All three'. Statements 1 and 2 are both true, which leaves 'Only two'.
explanations: Incorrect: two statements are correct, not one.
Correct: statements 1 and 2 are correct and statement 3 is wrong.
Incorrect: statement 3 is wrong because Ministers cannot be PAC members.
Incorrect: statements 1 and 2 are correct.
keyfact: Estimates Committee: 30 Lok Sabha members only; PAC: 15 LS + 7 RS, with no Ministers.
question:
With reference to the Financial Committees of the Parliament of India, consider the following statements:
1. The Estimates Committee consists exclusively of members elected from the Lok Sabha.
2. The Public Accounts Committee includes members of the Rajya Sabha.
3. A Minister can be elected as a member of the Public Accounts Committee.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
related: The PAC is often called the 'twin sister' of the Estimates Committee.
The PAC was first set up in 1921 under the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms.
The CAG is regarded as the friend, philosopher and guide of the PAC.
The Estimates Committee is exclusively a Lok Sabha committee.
COPU has 22 members: 15 from Lok Sabha and 7 from Rajya Sabha.
statements: 1 — Correct: The Estimates Committee has 30 members, all elected by the Lok Sabha from among its own members.
2 — Correct: The PAC has 15 Lok Sabha and 7 Rajya Sabha members, 22 in all.
3 — Incorrect: A Minister cannot be a member of the PAC, and a member who becomes a Minister ceases to be a member. The committee examines the executive's accounts, so Ministers are kept off it.
subject: Polity
summary: Only statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Estimates Committee has 30 Lok Sabha members only, and the PAC has 22 members (15 from Lok Sabha and 7 from Rajya Sabha). A Minister cannot be a member of the PAC.

detail: Punch-marked coins, the earliest widely circulated Indian coinage, are generally dated from about the 6th century BCE onwards (some scholars say 5th-4th century). They are mostly silver, bear symbols punched onto them (sun, hill, crescent, animals) and have no legends. Coins from regions of the Mahajanapadas such as Kashi, Kosala, Avanti, Gandhara and Magadha belong to the pre-Mauryan period. The Mauryan state did issue large numbers of such coins, but issuing authority was not exclusive. Regional kingdoms, republics and possibly traders or guilds also issued punch-marked coins. 'Exclusively' is a typical UPSC trap word. So Statement-I is true, Statement-II is false, and option c is right.
explanations: Wrong: Statement-II is false, so it cannot explain Statement-I.
Wrong: Statement-II is incorrect, not merely non-explanatory.
Correct: pre-Mauryan circulation is established, but the Mauryan state was not the exclusive issuer.
Wrong: Statement-I is correct.
keyfact: Punch-marked coins predate the Mauryas and were not a Mauryan monopoly.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
question:
Consider the following two statements:
Statement-I: Punch-marked silver coins were in circulation in the Indian subcontinent before the rise of the Mauryan Empire.
Statement-II: Punch-marked coins were issued exclusively by the Mauryan imperial state and by no other authority.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: Punch-marked coins are called Karshapana or Purana in texts.
Indo-Greeks issued the first coins with royal portraits and legends.
Kushans issued extensive gold coinage.
Guptas issued many gold coins called Dinaras.
Satavahanas issued many lead coins.
subject: Ancient History
summary: Statement-I is correct, since punch-marked coins circulated from the Mahajanapada period. Statement-II is incorrect because they were also issued by janapadas, other kingdoms and possibly by merchants or guilds.

detail: Article 76 provides for the Attorney General of India, who is the first law officer of the Government. The appointee must be qualified to be a Judge of the Supreme Court. This means he must be a citizen and have been a High Court Judge for five years, a High Court advocate for ten years, or a distinguished jurist in the President's opinion. He holds office during the pleasure of the President, so no impeachment-type procedure applies. Under Article 88 he may speak in and take part in the proceedings of either House, joint sittings and committees of which he is named a member, but he has no right to vote. He is not a member of the Council of Ministers. The Constitution does not fix his tenure or remuneration, which the President determines. Option d is the only one that is fully consistent with Article 76.
explanations: Incorrect: the Attorney General is not a member of the Council of Ministers and is not collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
Incorrect: Article 88 gives him a right to speak and take part, but expressly not to vote.
Incorrect: he holds office during the pleasure of the President and has no judge-like removal procedure.
Correct: Article 76(1) requires the person to be qualified for appointment as a Supreme Court Judge.
keyfact: The Attorney General can speak in Parliament but cannot vote, and holds office during the President's pleasure.
options: He is a member of the Union Council of Ministers and is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
He has the right to vote in the proceedings of Parliament when he is nominated a member of a parliamentary committee.
He can be removed from office only by a procedure similar to that for the removal of a Judge of the Supreme Court.
He is appointed by the President from among persons qualified for appointment as a Judge of the Supreme Court.
question: Which one of the following statements about the Attorney General of India is correct?
related: Article 76: Attorney General of India; Article 165: Advocate General of a State
Article 88: right of Ministers and the Attorney General to speak in Houses
Article 76(3): right of audience in all courts in India
Advocate General is appointed by the Governor from persons qualified to be a High Court Judge
The Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General are statutory-level law officers assisting him, not constitutional posts under Article 76
subject: Polity
summary: The Attorney General is appointed by the President from among persons qualified to be a Supreme Court Judge (Article 76). The other options misstate his status, voting rights or removal.

detail: CRISPR-Cas9 began as a bacterial adaptive immune system. Spacers taken from past phage infections are stored in CRISPR arrays and transcribed into guide RNAs. The guide RNA leads Cas9 to a matching DNA sequence that sits next to a PAM, where Cas9 makes a double-strand break. Base editors use a catalytically impaired Cas9 fused to a deaminase, so they change a single base without a double-strand break. Prime editing is a related technique. In India, the MoEFCC exempted SDN-1 (small indels from repair without a template) and SDN-2 (small template-guided edits) genome-edited plants from the rules for GM organisms, provided they have no exogenous DNA. SDN-3 involves inserting larger DNA and stays under the GM regulatory framework. To eliminate options, first confirm statements 1-3 as standard biology, then spot the SDN-3 trap in statement 4. That leaves exactly three correct.
explanations: Wrong: three statements are correct, not one.
Wrong: three statements are correct, not two.
Right: statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct, and statement 4 wrongly includes SDN-3 among the exempted categories.
Wrong: statement 4 is incorrect because SDN-3 was not exempted.
keyfact: India exempts SDN-1 and SDN-2 genome-edited plants without foreign DNA from GM rules, but SDN-3 stays regulated.
question:
With reference to CRISPR-Cas9 and genome editing, consider the following statements:
1. The Cas9 enzyme is directed to its DNA target by a guide RNA, and cleavage requires a short protospacer adjacent motif (PAM) next to the target site.
2. Base editors can convert one nucleotide into another without creating a double-strand break in DNA.
3. In bacteria, CRISPR arrays store spacer sequences derived from the genetic material of previously encountered invading viruses.
4. In India, genome-edited plants of the SDN-3 category, involving insertion of foreign DNA, were exempted from the GM-crop regulatory regime by the 2022 notification.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
related: SDN-1 and SDN-2 genome-edited plants without foreign DNA were exempted from GM rules by MoEFCC in 2022.
Emmanuelle Charpentier and Jennifer Doudna received the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for CRISPR-Cas9.
Prime editing uses a Cas9 nickase fused to a reverse transcriptase and a pegRNA.
Casgevy, a CRISPR-based therapy for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia, was the first such therapy approved.
statements: 1 — Correct: Cas9 is an RNA-guided endonuclease, and the PAM is needed for target recognition and cutting.
2 — Correct: Base editors chemically convert one base to another using a nickase or dead Cas9 fused to a deaminase, so no double-strand break occurs.
3 — Correct: Spacers in CRISPR arrays are snippets of past invaders' DNA, which gives the bacterium sequence-specific immune memory.
4 — Incorrect: Only SDN-1 and SDN-2 plants without foreign DNA were exempted in 2022. SDN-3 remains regulated. India released two genome-edited rice varieties in 2025.
subject: Science & Tech
summary: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct and statement 4 is incorrect, so only three are correct. India's 2022 exemption covers only SDN-1 and SDN-2 plants, which carry no foreign DNA.

detail: Srimanta Shankaradeva (15th-16th century) preached Vaishnavism in Assam through Ekasarana Dharma, which centres on devotion to Krishna and uses namghars, borgeets and Ankiya Nat. The Varkari tradition is associated with Pandharpur and saints such as Jnaneshwar, Namdev and Tukaram. Vallabhacharya propounded Shuddhadvaita, not Advaita, which is Shankara's philosophy.

question: Which one of the following pairs of a Bhakti or Sufi saint and the associated tradition or text is correctly matched?

Ramanuja propounded Vishishtadvaita.

Shankaradeva's Ankiya Nat is a form of one-act play.

detail: Tropical rainforest soils, often oxisols or ultisols, are typically nutrient-poor and acidic, yet the vegetation is highly productive. The reason is tight, near-closed nutrient cycling. Warm, moist conditions let decomposers break down litter within weeks. Dense, shallow root mats and mycorrhizal associations absorb the released nutrients almost immediately, so they do not accumulate in the soil. Heavy rainfall also leaches whatever remains. As a result, the biomass becomes the main nutrient reservoir. This is why clearing forest for agriculture quickly exhausts the soil, as in shifting cultivation. Elimination logic: Statement-I is a well-established fact. Statement-II lists the mechanisms that produce that condition, so it is a direct explanation. Options b, c and d are therefore eliminated.
explanations: Correct: Statement-II gives the mechanisms that explain why nutrients are concentrated in biomass.
Incorrect: Statement-II is not unrelated. It directly causes the pattern in Statement-I.
Incorrect: Statement-II is accurate.
Incorrect: Statement-I is accurate.
keyfact: Tropical rainforests: nutrients sit in biomass, not soil, because decomposition and re-uptake are rapid and leaching is high.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
question:

Statement-II: High temperature and humidity cause rapid decomposition, and the nutrients released are quickly taken up again by shallow roots and associated mycorrhizal fungi, while heavy rainfall leaches nutrients from the soil.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: In temperate forests and grasslands, a larger share of nutrients is stored in soil organic matter.
Mycorrhizae are symbiotic associations between fungi and plant roots that help nutrient uptake.
Laterisation is common in humid tropics and produces iron- and aluminium-rich soils.
Decomposition is faster in warm, moist conditions with nitrogen-rich litter.
Jhum cultivation is a form of shifting cultivation in northeast India.
statements: 1 — Correct: In tropical rainforests the biomass holds most of the nutrients, not the soil.
2 — Correct: Rapid decomposition, quick re-uptake and leaching are the mechanisms behind this pattern.
subject: Environment
summary: Both statements are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I. Fast decomposition, rapid re-uptake and leaching leave little nutrient stock in the soil.

detail: Spring tides are tides of maximum range, with higher high tides and lower low tides. They occur when the Sun, Earth and Moon are in a syzygy, a straight line. This happens at new moon, when the Moon lies between the Sun and Earth, and at full moon, when the Earth lies between them. In both cases the tide-raising forces of the Sun and Moon add together. Neap tides occur at the quarters (first and last), when the Sun and Moon are at right angles to each other and their pulls partly cancel. The word 'only' in Statement-I is the trap, because it excludes new moon. Statement-II is a correct description of the mechanism, but it cannot explain a statement that is itself wrong, so option (d) is the answer.
explanations: Wrong, because Statement-I is incorrect; it ignores spring tides at new moon.
Wrong, because Statement-I is factually incorrect, so there is no explanatory link to assess.
Wrong, because Statement-II is correct, not incorrect.
Correct: Statement-I is wrong because of 'only', and Statement-II is a correct description of how alignment reinforces tidal forces.
keyfact: Spring tides occur at both new moon and full moon; neap tides occur at the quarters.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
question:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-II: When the Sun, the Earth and the Moon are aligned, the gravitational pulls of the Sun and the Moon act along the same line and reinforce each other.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: Neap tides occur at the first and last quarter of the Moon.

The Bay of Fundy has one of the highest tidal ranges in the world.

The Hooghly river is known for tidal bores.
statements: Statement-I — Incorrect: spring tides occur at both new moon and full moon, not only at full moon.
Statement-II — Correct: the Sun's and Moon's gravitational pulls combine when the three bodies are aligned, giving a larger tidal range.
subject: Geography
summary: Statement-I is incorrect because spring tides occur at both full moon and new moon. Statement-II is correct, since alignment makes the Sun's and Moon's pulls reinforce each other.

detail: Parliament passed the Income-tax Act, 2025 in August 2025, and it received Presidential assent that month. It replaces the six-decade-old Income-tax Act, 1961. It came into force on 1 April 2026. The aim of the rewrite was to simplify language and structure, with fewer sections and less complexity. The most visible conceptual change is the 'tax year', which replaces the dual 'previous year' and 'assessment year'. Income earned in a tax year is taxed for that same year. Elimination: since all three statements are correct, only the option covering all three, (d), is right. Each partial option drops at least one true statement. Remember that the Act is a rewrite for simplification, not a new tax regime.

Incorrect. It omits statement 1, which is correct.
Correct. All three statements are accurate.
keyfact: The Income-tax Act, 2025 replaced the 1961 Act from 1 April 2026 and introduced the single 'tax year'.

subject: Current Affairs

detail: Viruses lack their own metabolic machinery and ribosomes, so they must use a host cell to replicate. Fungi are heterotrophs that feed by absorption, and their cell walls are made of chitin, not cellulose, so option a is wrong. Bacteria are prokaryotes with no membrane-bound nucleus; their genetic material lies in a nucleoid, so option b is wrong. Amoeba, Paramecium and Euglena are unicellular eukaryotes placed in kingdom Protista, not Monera, which contains only prokaryotes, so option d is wrong. The safest approach is to eliminate the options with firm errors, such as cellulose in fungi and a nucleus in bacteria, which leaves the statement about viruses.
explanations: Incorrect: fungi are heterotrophic and have chitin cell walls.
Incorrect: bacteria are prokaryotes without a true nucleus.
Correct: viruses are obligate intracellular parasites and reproduce only in living host cells.
Incorrect: these organisms are protists, not monerans.
keyfact: Viruses reproduce only inside living host cells; fungal walls are chitin; bacteria are prokaryotes.
options: Fungi are autotrophic and have cell walls made of cellulose
Bacteria are eukaryotic organisms with a well-defined nucleus

subject: General Science
summary: Viruses are obligate intracellular parasites and replicate only within living host cells. The other options misstate basic features of fungi, bacteria and protists.

It recommended an umbrella legislation for workers in the unorganised sector and consolidation of central labour laws into broad groups. Pair 2 wrongly gives Varma as the chairperson of the First Commission. Eliminating pair 2 leaves option b.

detail: AB PM-JAY is a publicly funded health assurance scheme giving cover of Rs 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary hospitalisation at empanelled hospitals. In 2024 the scheme was extended to all citizens aged 70 and above regardless of income, under the Ayushman Vay Vandana initiative. The scheme is a hospitalisation benefit, so statement 2 fails. detail: The Code on Social Security, 2020 for the first time defines 'gig worker', 'platform worker' and 'aggregator' in statute. It provides for schemes for these workers covering life and disability cover, health and maternity benefits, old-age protection and so on. detail: Under SA 580 (Written Representations), the auditor requests written representations from management to confirm that it has fulfilled its responsibility for preparing the financial statements and for providing complete information. detail: Since 2022, the RBI's liquidity adjustment corridor has had the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) as its floor. It replaced the fixed-rate reverse repo as the effective floor, and the SDF rate sits below the repo rate. The Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) is the ceiling of the corridor, and the MSF rate is above the repo rate. Banks use MSF in emergencies, when they have exhausted other options. It allows them to borrow overnight against government securities, including by dipping into the SLR holdings up to a specified limit. Because it is a last-resort window, its rate is higher than repo, which makes Statement-II incorrect. The SDF allows the RBI to absorb liquidity without giving collateral in return. Hence option (c).
explanations: Incorrect: Statement-II is false, so it cannot be a correct explanation.
Incorrect: Statement-II is false, so 'both correct' fails.
Correct: Statement-I is correct and Statement-II is incorrect because the MSF rate is above repo.
Incorrect: Statement-I is correct, so this option cannot hold.
keyfact: SDF rate < repo rate < MSF rate: SDF is the floor, MSF the ceiling of the LAF corridor.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
question:

Statement-II: The Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) rate is set below the repo rate so as to encourage banks to borrow overnight by dipping into their Statutory Liquidity Ratio holdings.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

The SDF does not require the RBI to provide collateral against absorbed funds.
The MSF is an emergency overnight window against government securities.

Facts: Repo is the middle of the corridor. The SDF absorbs liquidity without collateral. The MSF lets banks borrow overnight against government securities, including by dipping into SLR holdings.
subject: Economy
summary: Statement-I is correct because the SDF rate is the floor of the LAF corridor and lies below the repo rate. Statement-II is incorrect because the MSF rate is above the repo rate and works as a penal rate.

detail: Article 108 provides for a joint sitting when a Bill (other than a Money Bill or a Constitution Amendment Bill) is rejected by one House, the Houses disagree on amendments, or more than six months pass without the other House passing it. The President summons it. The Speaker presides; in the Speaker's absence the Deputy Speaker, then the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, or another person decided by the members present. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha never presides. Money Bills are excluded because the Lok Sabha has overriding power over them, and Constitution Amendment Bills need special majorities under Article 368. The three joint sittings were for the Dowry Prohibition Bill (1961), the Banking Service Commission (Repeal) Bill (1978) and the Prevention of Terrorism Bill (2002). Statements 2 and 3 are wrong, leaving option (a).
explanations: Correct: statements 1 and 4 are right, and statements 2 and 3 are wrong.
Wrong: statement 2 is incorrect because the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha does not preside.
Wrong: both statements 2 and 3 are incorrect, and neither 1 nor 4 is excluded.
Wrong: statement 3 is incorrect because Constitution Amendment Bills are outside the joint sitting provision.
keyfact: Joint sittings: Art 108, presided by the Speaker, held only 3 times (1961, 1978, 2002), not for Money or Constitution Amendment Bills.
