A convex lens has positive focal length.
An object at 2F gives a real, inverted image of the same size at 2F.
A concave lens always forms a virtual, erect, diminished image.
subject: General Science
summary: Using the lens formula, the image distance is 60 cm on the other side, so the magnification is -2. The negative sign shows that the image is real and inverted.

detail: The IR Code, 2020 merges the Trade Unions Act, 1926, the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946 and the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. Its definition of 'worker' covers any person, including a working journalist, sales promotion employee or skilled, unskilled, technical, operational, clerical or supervisory worker, employed in an industry for hire or reward. It excludes members of the armed forces, police or prison service, and persons mainly in managerial or administrative roles. A person in a supervisory capacity is excluded if he draws wages above Rs 18,000 per month or if his duties are mainly managerial in nature. Under the old Industrial Disputes Act the supervisory ceiling was Rs 10,000 per month. That makes Rs 10,000 the tempting distractor. Rs 15,000 and Rs 24,000 correspond to no relevant ceiling here, so they can be eliminated.
explanations: Incorrect. Rs 10,000 was the supervisory wage ceiling under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, which the Code replaced.
Incorrect. Rs 15,000 is not the supervisory ceiling in the IR Code. It is a figure associated with the EPF wage ceiling.
Correct. The IR Code excludes supervisory employees drawing wages above Rs 18,000 per month from the definition of worker.
Incorrect. Rs 24,000 is not the figure stated in the IR Code's definition of worker.
keyfact: IR Code: a supervisor drawing wages above Rs 18,000 per month is not a 'worker'.
question: Under the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, a person employed in a supervisory capacity is excluded from the definition of 'worker' if he draws wages exceeding a specified amount per month. What is that amount?
related: The IR Code, 2020 subsumes the Trade Unions Act 1926, the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act 1946 and the Industrial Disputes Act 1947.
Working journalists and sales promotion employees are included within 'worker'.
Persons mainly in managerial or administrative roles are not workers under the Code.
The four Labour Codes were brought into force on 21 November 2025.
subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: The correct answer is Rupees eighteen thousand. The IR Code's definition of 'worker' excludes a person employed mainly in a managerial or administrative capacity. It also excludes a person in a supervisory capacity who draws wages exceeding Rs 18,000 per month, or who performs mainly managerial functions.
topic: Definition of Worker under IR Code

detail: The Convention on Biological Diversity (1992) has three objectives: conservation, sustainable use, and fair and equitable sharing of benefits. Two protocols implement parts of it. The Cartagena Protocol (2000) covers biosafety and living modified organisms. The Nagoya Protocol (2010) covers access and benefit-sharing (ABS) for genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge. The Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) replaced the Aichi Targets. It has 23 targets for 2030, including the '30 by 30' target (Target 3). The trap is Statement 3. The name 'Kunming' reflects China's presidency of COP15. Because of COVID-19, the first part was held in Kunming (virtually and in person in 2021) and the second part in Montreal (December 2022). The framework was adopted in Montreal. In multi-statement questions, one subtly wrong place or date detail is a typical UPSC device.
explanations: Wrong. Three of the four statements are correct, so 'only one' undercounts.
Wrong. Only Statement 3 is incorrect, so more than two are correct.
Correct. Statements 1, 2 and 4 are accurate; Statement 3 misplaces the adoption venue (Montreal, not Kunming).
Wrong. Statement 3 is incorrect, since the framework was adopted at the Montreal session.
keyfact: The Kunming-Montreal GBF was adopted in Montreal (December 2022), not in Kunming.
question:
With reference to the international framework on biodiversity, consider the following statements:
1. The Nagoya Protocol deals with access to genetic resources and the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from their utilisation.
2. The Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety regulates the transboundary movement of living modified organisms resulting from modern biotechnology.
3. The Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework was adopted at a session of the Conference of the Parties to the CBD physically held in Kunming, China.
4. The Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework includes a target to effectively conserve and manage at least 30 per cent of the world's land, inland waters, coastal areas and oceans by 2030.
How many of the above statements are correct?
related: The Cartagena Protocol's supplementary protocol on liability and redress is the Nagoya-Kuala Lumpur Supplementary Protocol.
Aichi Biodiversity Targets (2011-2020) were adopted at COP10 in Nagoya in 2010.
India's Biological Diversity Act, 2002 set up the National Biodiversity Authority, headquartered in Chennai.
GBF Target 3 is the '30 by 30' target for protected and conserved areas.
statements: 1 — Correct: Nagoya Protocol is the ABS instrument under the CBD; India's Biological Diversity Act, 2002 gives effect to ABS provisions.
2 — Correct: Cartagena Protocol (2000) addresses safe handling, transport and use of LMOs, using advance informed agreement.
3 — Incorrect: The GBF was adopted at COP15 Part II in Montreal (December 2022), though China held the presidency.
4 — Correct: Target 3 of the GBF is the '30 by 30' goal for protected and conserved areas.

Facts: Aichi Targets were adopted in 2010 at COP10 in Nagoya, Japan. The GBF has 4 goals and 23 targets for 2030. The GBF also targets mobilising at least USD 200 billion per year from all sources for biodiversity.
subject: Environment
summary: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct, so the answer is 'Only three'. Statement 3 is wrong because COP15 was presided over by China but its second part, where the framework was adopted in December 2022, was held in Montreal, Canada.

detail: Under the OSH Code, 2020, an employee who works for more than the prescribed hours in a day or week is entitled to overtime wages at twice the normal rate of wages. This is the same standard that applied under the Factories Act, 1948, which provided for overtime at twice the ordinary rate. The Code also provides that a worker cannot be required to work overtime without consent in the case of certain categories, and that the overtime is subject to the prescribed limits. A rate of 1.5 times is a common distractor and is not the Code's rate. Ordinary-rate payment applies to regular hours, and three times is not provided for. Hence option b is correct.
explanations: Incorrect: The ordinary rate applies to regular hours, not to overtime.
Correct: The OSH Code, 2020 provides overtime wages at twice the normal rate of wages.
Incorrect: One and a half times is a distractor and is not the Code's rate.
Incorrect: Three times is not provided for under the OSH Code.
keyfact: The OSH Code, 2020 pays overtime at twice the normal rate of wages.
options: Overtime is paid at the ordinary rate of wages
Overtime is paid at twice the normal rate of wages
Overtime is paid at one and a half times the normal rate of wages
Overtime is paid at three times the normal rate of wages
question: Under the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020, which one of the following is the maximum number of hours of overtime-inclusive work that is generally permitted, with the overtime wages payable at what rate?
related: The OSH Code, 2020 subsumes 13 labour laws, including the Factories Act, 1948, and the Mines Act, 1952.
The Factories Act, 1948 also provided overtime at twice the ordinary rate.
Under the OSH Code, a woman may work at night only with her consent and subject to prescribed safety conditions.
The Code covers inter-State migrant workers, contract labour and the beedi and cigar sector.
subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: The correct answer is twice the normal rate of wages. The OSH Code, 2020 requires the employer to pay overtime for work beyond the prescribed hours at twice the normal rate of wages.

detail: Article 355 places a duty on the Union to protect each State against external aggression and internal disturbance and to ensure that State governments function according to the Constitution. Article 352 deals with proclamation of national emergency on grounds of war, external aggression or armed rebellion. Article 356 deals with President's Rule on failure of constitutional machinery in a State, and Article 365 states the consequence of failure to comply with Union directions: the President may hold that the State government cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution. The question's wording matches the duty clause, so Article 355 is correct; the others are operative powers rather than the duty.
explanations: Wrong: Article 352 deals with national emergency proclamation.
Correct: Article 355 states the Union's duty to protect States.
Wrong: Article 356 deals with President's Rule on failure of constitutional machinery.
Wrong: Article 365 deals with the effect of failure to comply with Union directions.
keyfact: Article 355 is the Union's duty to protect States; Article 356 is the power to impose President's Rule.
question: Which one of the following Articles of the Constitution of India provides that the Union shall protect every State against external aggression and internal disturbance and ensure that the government of every State is carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution?
related: Article 352: National Emergency.
Article 356: State Emergency (President's Rule).
Article 360: Financial Emergency.
S. R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994) made proclamations under Article 356 subject to judicial review.
Article 356 proclamation must be approved by both Houses within two months.
subject: Indian Polity
summary: Article 355 imposes this duty on the Union. It is the basis on which the Union can act under Article 356 when a State's constitutional machinery fails.

detail: Ephemeral describes things that are short-lived, such as morning dew, a fad or a fleeting fame. Transient carries the same sense of passing quickly. 'Perpetual' is the opposite, meaning never-ending, and so is an antonym trap. 'Fragile' means easily broken and describes physical delicacy, not duration; a distractor such as this works because short-lived things often feel delicate. 'Ornate' means elaborately decorated and has no link to time. In synonym questions, first fix the core meaning of the word, then test each option for the same meaning and not merely a related association. Other synonyms of ephemeral include fleeting, momentary and evanescent.
explanations: Correct: transient means lasting only briefly, which matches ephemeral.
Incorrect: perpetual means everlasting, the opposite of ephemeral.
Incorrect: fragile refers to breakability, not duration.
Incorrect: ornate means richly decorated and is unrelated.
keyfact: Ephemeral = short-lived, transient; opposite of perpetual.
question: Select the option that is most nearly the SYNONYM of the word: "EPHEMERAL"
related: Evanescent is a synonym of ephemeral.
Perennial means lasting through the years, an antonym of ephemeral.
Ephemeral derives from the Greek word for 'lasting a day'.
Fleeting and momentary are close synonyms.
subject: General English
summary: EPHEMERAL means lasting for a very short time, so 'transient' is the closest synonym. The word derives from the Greek 'ephemeros', meaning lasting only a day.

detail: Ozone depletion over Antarctica is seasonal. During the dark polar winter, a stable vortex forms and temperatures drop low enough for polar stratospheric clouds. On their surfaces, chlorine reservoirs such as HCl and ClONO2 are converted into reactive chlorine forms. When sunlight returns in spring, these forms rapidly destroy ozone, producing the ozone hole in September-October. The Montreal Protocol (1987) controls ozone-depleting substances such as CFCs and halons. HFCs were introduced as substitutes and contain no chlorine, so they do not meaningfully deplete ozone, but they have high global warming potential. The Kigali Amendment (2016) therefore phases down HFCs as a climate measure. Elimination: statement 3 confuses ozone and climate objectives. Rejecting it removes options (c) and (d), and statement 1 being correct removes (a)'s exclusivity, leaving (b).
explanations: Incorrect: statement 2 is also correct, so 'statement 1 only' is incomplete.
Correct: statements 1 and 2 are right, and statement 3 misstates the reason for the Kigali Amendment.
Incorrect: statement 3 is wrong, and it also leaves out the correct statement 1.
Incorrect: statement 3 is not correct, so all three cannot be true.
keyfact: The Kigali Amendment phases down HFCs for climate reasons, not because they deplete ozone.
question:
With reference to stratospheric ozone depletion, consider the following statements:
1. The Antarctic ozone hole is most pronounced during the southern hemisphere spring (roughly September to October).
2. Polar stratospheric clouds provide surfaces on which chlorine reservoir compounds are converted into reactive forms that destroy ozone.
3. The Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol seeks to phase down hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) mainly because they are potent ozone-depleting substances.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: The Montreal Protocol was adopted in 1987 and is widely regarded as a successful environmental treaty.
The Kigali Amendment was adopted in 2016 and targets HFCs.
Ozone is measured in Dobson Units.
CFCs release chlorine atoms in the stratosphere under UV radiation.
statements: 1 — Correct: the ozone hole peaks in southern spring, after sunlight returns to the polar stratosphere.
2 — Correct: polar stratospheric clouds enable heterogeneous reactions that activate chlorine.
3 — Incorrect: HFCs contain no chlorine and do not significantly deplete ozone; Kigali targets them for their high global warming potential.
subject: Science & Tech
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong because HFCs do not significantly deplete ozone. The Kigali Amendment targets them because they are powerful greenhouse gases.

detail: The word comes from Latin 'aequus' (equal) and 'vox' (voice), meaning to give equal voice to two meanings. A person who equivocates is deliberately vague or evasive, especially to hide the truth or avoid a firm position. The context clue 'answers that could be read in more than one way' points directly to ambiguity. Option (b) describes apologising, which has no link to the evasive behaviour described. Option (c) describes advocacy, which is the opposite of non-commitment. Option (d) is a distractor playing on the 'equi-' prefix, which suggests equality or balance and might tempt a candidate toward accounting-related meanings.
explanations: Correct: it captures deliberate ambiguity and avoidance of commitment.
Incorrect: apologising is a direct, committed act, not evasion.
Incorrect: forceful argument is the opposite of hedging.
Incorrect: it is a distractor built on the 'equi-' root and has nothing to do with the word's meaning.
keyfact: Equivocate = to speak ambiguously to avoid committing oneself; equivocal = open to more than one interpretation.
options: To speak with deliberate ambiguity so as to avoid commitment
To apologise sincerely for an oversight
To argue forcefully in favour of a proposal
To calculate a loss with precision
question:
Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the word 'EQUIVOCATE' as used in the sentence:
"When questioned about the missing records, the manager began to equivocate, giving answers that could be read in more than one way."
related: Prevaricate: to speak evasively or deviate from the truth.
Tergiversate: to be evasive or change one's stance repeatedly.
Obfuscate: to make something unclear or obscure.
Forthright: direct and frank, the opposite of equivocal.
subject: General English
summary: 'Equivocate' means to use ambiguous language to avoid committing oneself or telling the truth directly. The sentence itself hints at this with 'answers that could be read in more than one way'.

detail: Vector-borne diseases are a favourite UPSC area, and the usual trap is to confuse the genera of mosquitoes. Kala-azar is caused by the protozoan Leishmania donovani and spread by the female Phlebotomus sandfly. Scrub typhus is caused by the bacterium Orientia tsutsugamushi and passes to humans through the bite of infected chigger larvae. Japanese encephalitis is a flavivirus infection transmitted mainly by Culex tritaeniorhynchus, with pigs and wading birds as amplifying hosts. Zika, dengue, chikungunya and yellow fever are transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, chiefly Aedes aegypti. Elimination: knowing that Zika is an Aedes-borne virus rules out 'All four'. Recognising any two of the others as correct rules out 'Only one' and then 'Only two'.
explanations: Incorrect: three pairs are correct, not one.
Incorrect: three pairs are correct, not just two.
Correct: pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct and only pair 4 is wrong.
Incorrect: pair 4 is wrong because Zika is an Aedes-borne disease.
keyfact: Zika, dengue and chikungunya are Aedes-borne; Japanese encephalitis is Culex-borne.
question:
Consider the following pairs:
   Disease : Vector or transmitting agent
1. Kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis) : Sandfly
2. Scrub typhus : Larval trombiculid mites (chiggers)
3. Japanese encephalitis : Culex mosquito
4. Zika virus disease : Culex mosquito
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
related: Dengue, chikungunya, Zika and yellow fever are Aedes-borne.
Malaria is transmitted by female Anopheles mosquitoes.
Lymphatic filariasis is mainly transmitted by Culex in India.
Scrub typhus is caused by a bacterium, not a virus.
statements: 1 — Correct: Leishmania donovani is transmitted by the sandfly Phlebotomus argentipes in India.
2 — Correct: Orientia tsutsugamushi is spread by the bite of larval trombiculid mites.
3 — Correct: JE virus is spread mainly by Culex species; pigs are amplifying hosts.
4 — Incorrect: Zika spreads mainly through Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus, not Culex.
subject: Science & Tech
summary: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct, so the answer is 'Only three pairs'. Zika is transmitted mainly by Aedes mosquitoes, not Culex.

detail: Net realisable value is the estimated selling price less the estimated costs necessary to make the sale. For item B, NRV = 34,000 − 6,000 = ₹28,000, which is below its cost of ₹30,000, so B is valued at ₹28,000. Item A is valued at cost (₹40,000) because its NRV is higher, since gains are not anticipated. Item C is valued at its NRV (₹22,000), which is below cost. The total is 40,000 + 28,000 + 22,000 = ₹90,000. Total cost is ₹95,000 and total NRV is also ₹95,000, so a comparison on a total basis would wrongly give ₹95,000. The comparison is made item by item, or for groups of similar items, and not on the stock as a whole. This rests on the convention of conservatism: provide for all probable losses but do not anticipate profits.
explanations: Incorrect: this is the aggregate cost (and also the aggregate NRV), so it ignores item-by-item comparison.
Incorrect: this deducts the loss on item B twice or uses wrong NRVs.
Incorrect: this does not correspond to the lower of cost and NRV for each item.
keyfact: Value each item at the lower of cost and NRV; do not set off gains on one item against losses on another.
question:
A trader holds three items of stock at the year end:
Item A: cost ₹40,000; net realisable value ₹45,000
Item B: cost ₹30,000; estimated selling price ₹34,000; estimated selling expenses ₹6,000
Item C: cost ₹25,000; net realisable value ₹22,000
Applying the principle of lower of cost and net realisable value, item by item, the value of closing inventory will be:
related: NRV = estimated selling price − estimated costs of completion − selling costs.
Inventory write-downs are charged to the P&L in the period of the write-down.
FIFO and weighted average are permitted cost formulas; LIFO is not permitted under Ind AS 2.
Conservatism underlies the lower of cost or NRV rule.
subject: Accounting & Auditing
summary: The answer is ₹90,000. Each item is valued at the lower of its cost and NRV: A at 40,000, B at 28,000 and C at 22,000.

detail: From 29 October 2024 the government extended Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY to all senior citizens aged 70 and above, with no income test, under the Ayushman Vay Vandana card. Eligible families receive health cover of Rs 5 lakh per year on a family floater basis. Where a family has other members already covered, the Rs 5 lakh is shared, and the senior citizen is not given a separate Rs 5 lakh cover. Seniors already covered under CGHS, ECHS or CAPF schemes may choose to remain in them or opt for PM-JAY. Seniors with private insurance or ESIC cover are also eligible. To solve this, remember the figure Rs 5 lakh, which is the standard PM-JAY cover. Statement 2 is therefore wrong, so options (a), (b) and (d) are eliminated.
explanations: Incorrect: it includes statement 2, which gives the wrong cover amount.
Incorrect: it includes statement 2 and leaves out statement 1.
Correct: statements 1 and 3 are accurate.
Incorrect: statement 2 is false.
keyfact: Ayushman Vay Vandana covers all aged 70+ regardless of income, with a Rs 5 lakh family floater cover.

detail: Karst topography forms by solution of limestone. Small depressions are sinkholes or dolines, and when several merge they form an uvala. A still larger, flat-floored depression is a polje. Glacial deposits fall into two groups. Unstratified till builds moraines and drumlins, while sorted meltwater deposits build eskers, kames and outwash plains. Eskers are sinuous and stratified. Barchans are crescent-shaped dunes formed under a fairly constant wind direction with limited sand supply. The windward side has a gentle slope, the slip face is steep on the leeward side, and the horns extend downwind. Longitudinal (seif) dunes are aligned with the wind. Transverse dunes lie at right angles to it. So 1 and 2 stand and 3 falls, which gives option (a).
explanations: Correct. Statements 1 and 2 are right and statement 3 is wrong.
Incorrect. It includes the wrong statement 3 and omits the correct statement 1.
Incorrect. It includes statement 3, which is wrong, and omits statement 2.
Incorrect. Statement 3 is wrong, so not all three can be correct.
keyfact: Barchan horns point downwind. Eskers are stratified meltwater ridges, while moraines are unsorted till.
question:
With reference to certain landforms, consider the following statements:
1. An uvala is a large depression in karst terrain formed by the coalescence of several sinkholes (dolines).
2. An esker is a long, winding ridge of stratified sand and gravel deposited by meltwater streams flowing in or under glacial ice.
3. In a barchan dune, the horns of the crescent point toward the direction from which the prevailing wind blows.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: Polje is a large flat-floored karst basin.
Drumlins are streamlined hills of till, often found in swarms.
Seif dunes are longitudinal dunes parallel to the wind.
Loess is wind-deposited fine silt.
Cirque, arete and horn are glacial erosional features.
statements: 1 — Correct: coalescing dolines form an uvala, and larger ones form a polje.
2 — Correct: eskers are stratified meltwater deposits, unlike unsorted till.
3 — Incorrect: barchan horns point downwind (leeward), not toward the wind.
subject: Geography
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong because the horns of a barchan point downwind, away from the wind source.
topic: Geomorphology: karst, glacial and aeolian landforms

detail: An inverted 'Had + subject + past participle' structure is a third conditional. It expresses an unreal past situation and an imagined past result, so the main clause needs 'would/could/might have + V3'. 'Will not have approved' is a future perfect and does not fit an unreal past. 'Would not approve' is a second-conditional form for present or future unreality and does not match the past perfect in the if-clause. 'Had not approved' is a past perfect that cannot form a main clause here, because the main clause needs a modal. Only 'would not have approved' completes the conditional correctly.
explanations: Correct: the third conditional needs 'would + have + V3' in the main clause.
Wrong: 'will have' is a future perfect and does not suit a hypothetical past.
Wrong: 'would not approve' is a present or future unreal form and does not match 'had disclosed'.
Wrong: 'had not approved' has no modal, so it cannot form the main clause of the conditional.
keyfact: 'Had + subject + V3' is an inverted third conditional and takes 'would have + V3'.
question:
Select the option that correctly fills the blank:

Had the management disclosed the liabilities earlier, the investors _______ the merger.
related: First conditional: If + present, will + base verb.
Second conditional: If + past, would + base verb.
Third conditional: If + past perfect, would have + V3.
'Had I known' is the same as 'If I had known'.
subject: General English
summary: The sentence is a third conditional ('Had ... disclosed' means 'If ... had disclosed'), which takes 'would have + past participle' in the main clause. So 'would not have approved' is correct.

detail: NABARD was set up in July 1982, taking over the agricultural credit functions of the RBI and refinance functions of the Agricultural Refinance and Development Corporation, on the recommendation of the Committee to Review Arrangements for Institutional Credit for Agriculture and Rural Development (CRAFICARD) chaired by B. Sivaraman. Earlier, the RBI held a small stake, and this was transferred to the Government, making NABARD fully owned by the Government of India. NABARD is the apex development finance institution for agriculture and rural development. It refinances cooperative banks and Regional Rural Banks, and it supervises them, as well as State Cooperative Banks and District Central Cooperative Banks. Urban Cooperative Banks, however, are regulated and supervised by the RBI, which is why statement 3 is wrong. So only options with 1 and 2 survive.
explanations: Correct: statements 1 and 2 are correct and 3 is incorrect.
Wrong: it includes statement 3, which is false, and leaves out statement 1.
Wrong: statement 3 is false.
Wrong: statement 3 is false, so all three cannot be correct.

detail: The CACP is an attached office of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare. It has no statutory backing, so option (a) is wrong. MSP is a policy announcement and not a legal entitlement, since there is no law guaranteeing procurement at MSP.

Correct: the CACP recommends and the CCEA approves the MSP.
Wrong: the CACP does not recommend prices for fruits and vegetables under the Market Intervention Scheme.
Wrong: the CACP is under the agriculture ministry, not finance, and covers only the mandated crops.

MSP for the mandated crops is approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs after considering the recommendations of the CACP
MSP is announced for fruits and vegetables under the Market Intervention Scheme on the recommendation of the CACP
The CACP functions under the Ministry of Finance and recommends MSP for all agricultural commodities
question: With reference to the Minimum Support Price (MSP) system in India, which one of the following statements is correct?
related: MSP is announced for 22 mandated crops, namely 14 kharif, 6 rabi and 2 commercial crops.
The CACP was set up in 1965 as the Agricultural Prices Commission and was renamed in 1985.

detail: In tropical rainforests, warm and humid conditions cause fast decomposition of litter by microbes and fungi. Released nutrients are quickly absorbed by shallow roots and mycorrhizal networks, so the bulk of nutrients is stored in living vegetation rather than soil. Heavy rainfall also leaches nutrients and the soils are often highly weathered, such as laterites and oxisols. Hence soils are nutrient-poor even though the biome is highly productive and diverse. This is why clearing forest for agriculture quickly exhausts soil fertility. Statement-II gives the mechanism underlying Statement-I, so option a is correct. Options c and d fail because both statements are factually accurate. Option b fails because the causal link holds.
explanations: Correct: both are true and rapid cycling into biomass explains the poor soils.
Incorrect: Statement-II does directly explain Statement-I.
Incorrect: Statement-II is correct.
Incorrect: Statement-I is correct.
keyfact: In rainforests nutrients sit mostly in biomass, not soil, because decomposition and uptake are rapid.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I

question:
Statement-I: Tropical rainforests have high species diversity but their soils are generally nutrient-poor.
Statement-II: In tropical rainforests, most nutrients are held in the living biomass and are rapidly recycled from decomposing litter, because high temperature and moisture accelerate decomposition.

related: Rainforest soils are often laterite or oxisol types.
Shifting cultivation exploits short-lived fertility after clearing.
Detritus food chains dominate nutrient return in forests.
Mycorrhizae help plants absorb nutrients in poor soils.
subject: Environment
summary: Both statements are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I. Rapid decomposition and uptake keep nutrients in biomass, leaving soils poor.

detail: In order of increasing frequency, the spectrum runs: radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays. Wavelength falls as frequency rises. X-rays lie beyond ultraviolet, so they have the higher frequency. Microwaves lie between radio waves and infrared, so they have longer wavelengths than infrared. Statement 2 reverses this order. All electromagnetic waves, whatever their frequency, travel at the speed of light, about 3 x 10^8 metres per second in vacuum. To eliminate options, spot that statement 2 is false, which removes (b), (c) and (d) together, and then confirm statements 1 and 3 are true.
explanations: Correct: statements 1 and 3 are true and statement 2 is false.
Incorrect: it includes statement 2, which is false.
Incorrect: it includes statement 2 and omits statement 1.
Incorrect: statement 2 is false.
keyfact: Frequency rises from radio to gamma; wavelength falls, but all travel at c in vacuum.
question:
With reference to the electromagnetic spectrum, consider the following statements:
1. X-rays have a higher frequency than ultraviolet rays.
2. Infrared radiation has a longer wavelength than microwaves.
3. In vacuum, all electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
related: Gamma rays have the highest frequency in the electromagnetic spectrum.
Radio waves have the longest wavelength.
Ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays are ionising radiation.
Energy of a photon is proportional to its frequency.
Microwave ovens use radiation of about 2.45 GHz.
statements: 1 — Correct: X-rays lie beyond ultraviolet and have higher frequency.
2 — Incorrect: Infrared has shorter wavelength than microwaves, not longer.
3 — Correct: All electromagnetic waves travel at the speed of light in vacuum.
subject: Science & Tech
summary: Statements 1 and 3 are correct, so the answer is (a). Infrared has a shorter wavelength than microwaves, so statement 2 is wrong.

detail: Article 270 provides that taxes levied and collected by the Union are distributed between the Union and the States. Surcharges and cesses levied for specific purposes are excluded from the divisible pool, so the States do not get a share of them. Article 271 empowers Parliament to levy surcharges for Union purposes on duties and taxes in Articles 269 and 270, and the proceeds belong wholly to the Union. A cess is levied for a specific purpose, but the Constitution does not say that the proceeds must be credited to the Public Account. Cess proceeds are first credited to the Consolidated Fund of India, and the government may later transfer them to a dedicated fund. To eliminate options, rejecting statement 2 leaves only the option with 1 and 3.
explanations: Wrong. Statement 3 is also correct, so 1 only is incomplete.
Wrong. It includes statement 2, which is incorrect.
Wrong. It includes statement 2 and omits the correct statement 3.
Correct. Statements 1 and 3 are correct and statement 2 is wrong.
keyfact: Cesses and surcharges are outside the divisible pool, and Article 271 allows Union surcharges.
question:
With reference to cesses and surcharges levied by the Union Government in India, consider the following statements:
1. The proceeds of cesses and surcharges levied by the Union are excluded from the net proceeds of taxes that are shared with the States under Article 270.
2. The Constitution mandates that the proceeds of every cess must be credited to the Public Account of India.
3. Parliament may levy a surcharge on taxes for Union purposes under Article 271.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: Article 270 deals with taxes shared between the Union and the States.
Article 271 allows surcharges for Union purposes.
Cesses and surcharges are not part of the divisible pool.
The Health and Education Cess is levied at 4 per cent on income tax.
Cess proceeds are first credited to the Consolidated Fund of India.
statements: 1 — Correct: Cesses and surcharges are excluded from the divisible pool shared with the States.
2 — Incorrect: There is no constitutional rule that every cess be credited to the Public Account.
3 — Correct: Article 271 allows Parliament to levy surcharges for Union purposes.
Cess proceeds are first credited to the Consolidated Fund of India.
subject: Economy
summary: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong because the Constitution does not require all cess proceeds to go to the Public Account.
topic: Cess and surcharge in Union finances

detail: The Western Ghats form a nearly continuous escarpment, broken only by the Palghat Gap, and are cut by few rivers on the western side. The Eastern Ghats are discontinuous and dissected by the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri. Anamudi (2,695 m) in the Anamalai hills of Kerala is the highest peak of the Western Ghats and of peninsular India. The Eastern Ghats have a lower average elevation, with Arma Konda (Jindhagada) in Andhra Pradesh the highest peak. So statement 3 is wrong, and the answer is 1 and 2 only.
explanations: Wrong: statement 2 is also correct.
Correct: statements 1 and 2 are correct.
Wrong: statement 3 is incorrect.
Wrong: statement 3 is incorrect.
keyfact: Western Ghats are higher and continuous, with Anamudi (2,695 m) the highest; the Eastern Ghats are broken by rivers.
question:
With reference to the Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats of India, consider the following statements:
1. The Western Ghats are more continuous than the Eastern Ghats, which are broken by rivers such as the Godavari, Krishna and Mahanadi.
2. Anamudi is the highest peak of the Western Ghats.
3. The Eastern Ghats are higher on average than the Western Ghats.

related: The Palghat Gap lies between the Nilgiris and the Anamalai hills.
Anamudi is in Kerala.
Eastern Ghats' highest peak is Arma Konda.

statements: 1 — Correct: The Eastern Ghats are dissected by large east-flowing rivers while the Western Ghats are largely continuous.
2 — Correct: Anamudi at 2,695 m is the highest peak of the Western Ghats.
3 — Incorrect: The Western Ghats are higher on average than the Eastern Ghats.
subject: Geography

detail: Ecological pyramids represent numbers, biomass or energy at successive trophic levels. The pyramid of energy is always upright because energy is lost as heat at each transfer, in line with the second law of thermodynamics, so each higher level receives less. Pyramids of biomass and numbers can be inverted. In ponds and oceans, phytoplankton have very short lifespans and high turnover, so their standing biomass at a given moment is smaller than that of the zooplankton and fish feeding on them. The cause is the difference between standing crop and rate of production. Statement-II is a true general law about energy flow, but it does not account for the inversion of biomass. Elimination logic: option (a) is tempting, but the energy pyramid being upright says nothing about turnover rates. Options (c) and (d) wrongly declare one statement false.
explanations: Incorrect: the upright energy pyramid does not explain the biomass inversion, which is caused by rapid turnover of producers.
Correct: both statements are true, and the inversion is explained by turnover rate, not by the energy law.
Incorrect: Statement-II is correct, since energy pyramids are never inverted.
Incorrect: Statement-I is correct, since biomass pyramids in aquatic systems can be inverted.
keyfact: Energy pyramids are always upright, but aquatic biomass pyramids can be inverted because of fast producer turnover.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: In a pond ecosystem, the pyramid of biomass can be inverted.

Statement-II: The pyramid of energy in any ecosystem is always upright.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: Pyramid of numbers is inverted in a tree ecosystem with many insects feeding on one tree.
Pyramid of biomass is upright in most terrestrial ecosystems.
Roughly 10 per cent of energy passes from one trophic level to the next (Lindeman's rule).
Gross primary productivity minus respiration gives net primary productivity.
subject: Environment
summary: Both statements are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I. An inverted biomass pyramid arises because phytoplankton reproduce rapidly and are consumed quickly, so standing biomass is low even though energy flow is high.

detail: Trade remedies come in three forms. Anti-dumping duty responds to dumping, meaning exports at below normal value, and is applied against specific exporters or countries. Countervailing duty offsets subsidies given by the exporting country. Safeguard duty responds to a surge in imports that causes or threatens serious injury to domestic producers. It is a measure against fairly traded imports, so there is no unfair trade practice to prove. Safeguards are applied on a non-discriminatory (MFN) basis to imports from all sources, with some exemptions for developing countries below de minimis shares. In India, the Directorate General of Trade Remedies (DGTR) in the Commerce Ministry investigates and recommends, and the Finance Ministry imposes the duties. Statement-I confuses safeguard with anti-dumping, so it is wrong. Statement-II is correct. Hence option (d).
explanations: Incorrect: Statement-I is false, so it cannot be explained by Statement-II.
Incorrect: Statement-I is false.
Incorrect: it reverses the correctness of the two statements.
Correct: Statement-I confuses safeguards with anti-dumping, while Statement-II describes safeguards accurately.
keyfact: Safeguard duty is applied against import surges on an MFN basis. Anti-dumping and countervailing duties are applied against specific unfair trade.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is not correct
Statement-I is not correct but Statement-II is correct
question:
Consider the following two statements:
Statement-I: Under India's trade remedy framework, a safeguard duty is imposed only on imports from those countries that are found to be dumping the product.
Statement-II: Safeguard measures are meant to address a surge in imports that causes or threatens serious injury to the domestic industry, and they do not require the imports to be unfairly traded.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: The DGTR works under the Department of Commerce.
Anti-dumping duty targets goods sold below normal value.
Countervailing duty offsets subsidies given by the exporting country.
The WTO Agreement on Safeguards allows safeguards only for limited periods.
The Central Government, through the Finance Ministry, imposes the duties on DGTR's recommendation.
statements: I — Incorrect: safeguard duties apply to imports from all sources and are not tied to dumping.
II — Correct: safeguards respond to an import surge causing serious injury, without any need for unfair trade.
Anti-dumping and countervailing duties are country- or exporter-specific, while safeguards are applied on an MFN basis.
subject: Economy
summary: Statement-I is incorrect and Statement-II is correct. Safeguard duties are applied on imports from all sources, without regard to dumping or unfair practice, so they are not limited to dumping countries.

detail: In the nitrogen cycle, Nitrosomonas oxidises ammonia to nitrite and Nitrobacter oxidises nitrite to nitrate. Together these two steps make up nitrification. The cyanobacterium Anabaena lives inside the leaf cavities of the water fern Azolla and fixes nitrogen, which is why Azolla is used as a biofertiliser in paddy fields. Denitrification, which returns nitrogen to the atmosphere, is carried out mainly by bacteria such as Pseudomonas and Thiobacillus under anaerobic conditions. Clostridium is a free-living anaerobic nitrogen fixer, so pair 3 is wrong on both the process and the conditions. Elimination: confirming pair 1 rules out 'None', and rejecting pair 3 rules out 'All three'.
explanations: Wrong: two pairs are correct, so one is too few.
Correct: pairs 1 and 2 are correct and pair 3 is not.
Wrong: pair 3 mismatches Clostridium with denitrification in aerated soils.
Wrong: pairs 1 and 2 are accurate.
keyfact: Nitrosomonas: ammonia to nitrite; Nitrobacter: nitrite to nitrate; denitrification is anaerobic.
question:
Consider the following pairs of organisms and their role in nutrient cycles:
1. Nitrobacter : Oxidation of nitrite to nitrate
2. Anabaena (in association with Azolla) : Symbiotic fixation of atmospheric nitrogen
3. Clostridium : Denitrification in aerated soils
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
related: Rhizobium forms root nodules in legumes and fixes nitrogen symbiotically.
Azotobacter is a free-living aerobic nitrogen fixer.
Denitrifying bacteria such as Pseudomonas return nitrogen to the atmosphere.
Nitrification is a two-step process carried out by Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter.
statements: 1 — Correct: Nitrobacter converts nitrite to nitrate in nitrification.
2 — Correct: Anabaena in Azolla fixes atmospheric nitrogen symbiotically.
3 — Incorrect: Clostridium is a free-living anaerobic nitrogen fixer, and denitrification occurs mainly in anaerobic conditions.

Nitrosomonas converts ammonia to nitrite and Nitrobacter converts nitrite to nitrate. Rhizobium fixes nitrogen symbiotically in legume root nodules. Azotobacter is a free-living aerobic nitrogen fixer.
subject: Environment
summary: Pairs 1 and 2 are correctly matched, so the answer is 'Only two pairs'. Clostridium is a free-living anaerobic nitrogen-fixer, not a denitrifier of aerated soils.

detail: Munificent describes lavish, large-hearted giving, as in 'a munificent donation'. Its antonyms include stingy, miserly, niggardly, parsimonious and tight-fisted. Generous and benevolent are synonyms, so they are eliminated immediately in an antonym question. Opulent means wealthy or luxurious; it is a distractor because it is loosely linked to richness, but it does not express the opposite of giving freely. Always separate the meaning (generosity) from association (wealth). When two options are synonyms of the given word, they are almost certainly wrong in an antonym question.
explanations: Synonym of munificent, not antonym.
Correct: stingy means unwilling to give, the opposite of munificent.
Opulent means rich or lavish; it is not the opposite of generous.
Benevolent means kind and charitable, a near-synonym.
keyfact: Munificent = lavishly generous; antonym = stingy or miserly.
question: Select the option that is most nearly the ANTONYM of the word 'MUNIFICENT':
related: Parsimonious means extremely unwilling to spend; its antonym is lavish.
Ephemeral means short-lived; its antonym is permanent.
Magnanimous means generous in forgiving; antonym: petty.
Frugal means economical, not necessarily stingy.
subject: General English
summary: The answer is (b) Stingy. 'Munificent' means very generous, so its opposite is miserly or stingy.

detail: Phishing uses deceptive communication, such as e-mails, SMS (smishing) or calls (vishing), that appears to come from a trusted source, to lure victims into giving credentials, OTPs or financial details, often through a fake website. Elimination: option (a) describes a Denial-of-Service (DoS/DDoS) attack. Option (c) describes ransomware. Option (d) describes a keylogger, a type of spyware. Only option (b) matches phishing, which exploits human trust rather than a technical flaw alone.
explanations: Incorrect: This is a Denial-of-Service attack.
Correct: Phishing deceives users into revealing confidential information.
Incorrect: This is ransomware.
Incorrect: This describes a keylogger.
keyfact: Phishing = tricking users via fake messages or sites to steal sensitive information.
options: Flooding a server with traffic so that legitimate users cannot access it
Deceiving users, typically through fake e-mails or websites, into revealing sensitive information such as passwords or card details
Encrypting a user's files and demanding payment for the decryption key
Secretly recording the keys pressed by a user on a keyboard
question: Which one of the following best describes a 'phishing' attack?
related: DDoS uses many compromised systems to flood a target.
A firewall monitors and controls network traffic based on rules.
Two-factor authentication adds a second verification step.
Spyware secretly gathers user information.
Encryption converts plain text into cipher text.
subject: Computers
summary: Phishing is a social-engineering attack that tricks people into disclosing sensitive information using fraudulent messages or websites. Option (b) describes this.

detail: The Montreal Protocol (1987), under the Vienna Convention (1985), controls ozone-depleting substances. CFCs were replaced by HCFCs, which are less damaging but still deplete ozone, so they are being phased out. HFCs were then used as replacements. They contain no chlorine, so their ozone depletion potential is effectively zero, but many are very potent greenhouse gases. The Kigali Amendment (2016) therefore brought HFCs under the Protocol to phase them down for climate reasons. Both the Vienna Convention and the Montreal Protocol were ratified by every UN member state in 2009, which is a rare distinction. The Kigali Amendment follows the Protocol's principle of common but differentiated responsibilities, with separate baselines and schedules for non-Article 5 countries and for Article 5 countries, which are split into two groups. India is in the later-starting group and ratified Kigali in 2021. Statement 4 fails on this differentiation, so only three statements are correct.
explanations: Incorrect: three statements are correct, not one.
Incorrect: three statements are correct, not two.
Correct: statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct and statement 4 is incorrect.
Incorrect: statement 4 is false because the schedules are differentiated.
keyfact: HFCs do not deplete ozone but are potent greenhouse gases; Kigali phases them down with differentiated schedules.
question:
With reference to the Montreal Protocol and its Kigali Amendment, consider the following statements:
1. Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) controlled under the Kigali Amendment have negligible ozone depletion potential but high global warming potential.
2. The Vienna Convention for the Protection of the Ozone Layer and the Montreal Protocol have both achieved universal ratification.
3. Hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFCs) were adopted as transitional substitutes for CFCs and are themselves subject to phase-out under the Montreal Protocol.
4. The Kigali Amendment prescribes an identical HFC phase-down schedule for all Parties, irrespective of their level of development.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
related: Kigali Amendment was adopted in 2016 and ratified by India in 2021.
India is in the later-starting developing-country group for HFC phase-down.
Ozone depletion potential of CFC-11 is the reference value of 1.
The Vienna Convention (1985) has no binding control targets; the Montreal Protocol does.
Article 5 countries are developing countries with differentiated schedules.
statements: 1 — Correct: HFCs contain no chlorine or bromine, so they do not deplete ozone, but many have very high global warming potential. This is why Kigali treats them as a climate measure.
2 — Correct: Both the Vienna Convention and the Montreal Protocol have been ratified by all UN member states. The Kigali Amendment has not reached universal ratification.
3 — Correct: HCFCs are transitional substitutes for CFCs. They have lower but non-zero ozone depletion potential and are being phased out.
4 — Incorrect: Kigali sets different baselines and schedules for developed countries and for the two groups of developing countries. India is in the later-starting group.
subject: Environment
summary: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct, so the answer is 'Only three'. Statement 4 is wrong because the Kigali Amendment sets differentiated schedules for different groups of countries.

detail: The EPF Act has several similar-looking provisions that are often confused. Section 7A deals with the determination of money due from employers, which is an inquiry into the amount owed. Section 7I provides for an appeal to the Employees' Provident Fund Appellate Tribunal against orders under the Act. Section 7Q provides for interest on delayed payment of dues. Section 14B provides for damages on default, which are a separate penal-compensatory levy, and the Act caps them at the rate specified in the Scheme. Section 14 deals with penalties and prosecution. Elimination: first separate assessment (7A), appeal (7I), and interest (7Q). Damages is a distinct concept, which leaves 14B.
explanations: Incorrect: Section 7A deals with determination of money due from employers.
Incorrect: Section 7Q provides for interest on delayed payment of dues, not damages.
Correct: Section 14B empowers recovery of damages for default or delay in payment of contributions.
Incorrect: Section 7I provides for appeals to the Appellate Tribunal.
keyfact: EPF Act: 7A = determination of dues, 7I = appeal, 7Q = interest, 14B = damages.
question: Under the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952, the power to levy damages on an employer who defaults in the payment of contributions is conferred by which one of the following Sections?
related: Section 7A: determination of moneys due from employers.
Section 7I: appeal to the Employees' Provident Fund Appellate Tribunal.
Section 7Q: interest on delay in payment of dues.
Section 14: penalties for offences under the Act.
Section 6: contributions and matters that may be provided for in the Scheme.
subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: Section 14B is the correct answer. It empowers the Central Provident Fund Commissioner or an authorised officer to recover damages from an employer who defaults in paying contributions or other dues. The other sections cover different matters.

detail: For people facing the centre, left means the clockwise direction and right means the anticlockwise direction. Fix A at seat 1 and number the seats clockwise. D sits opposite A, so D is at 4. B is second to the right of A, so we go anticlockwise two places, 1 → 6 → 5, and B is at 5. C must be an immediate neighbour of D, whose neighbours are seats 3 and 5. Seat 5 is taken by B, so C is at 3. C is opposite F, so F is at 6. The only seat left is 2, which is E. Third to the left of E means moving clockwise three seats from 2: 3, 4, 5. Seat 5 is B. Always fix the direction convention first, since reversing it gives D as the wrong answer.
explanations: Correct. Seat 5 is B, and it is three places clockwise from E at seat 2.
Incorrect. D is at seat 4, which is second to the left of E, not third.
Incorrect. F is at seat 6, which is third to the right of E (anticlockwise from E it is seat 1, then 6; this is not the third-left seat).
Incorrect. A is at seat 1, which is the immediate right of E, not third to the left.
keyfact: Facing the centre: left is clockwise and right is anticlockwise.
question:
Six persons A, B, C, D, E and F are sitting around a circular table, all facing the centre.
A is sitting opposite D.
B is sitting second to the right of A.
C is an immediate neighbour of D.
C is sitting opposite F.
Who is sitting third to the left of E?
related: When facing the centre, left = clockwise and right = anticlockwise.
When facing outward, left and right are reversed.
In a circle of n people, the person opposite is n/2 seats away.
Fix one person first and place the others relative to that person.
subject: Quantitative Aptitude & Reasoning
summary: The answer is B. Number the seats 1 to 6 clockwise with A at 1. Then D is at 4, B is at 5, C is at 3, F is at 6 and E is at 2. Third to the left of E (moving clockwise) is seat 5, which is B.

detail: The EPF Act, 1952 provides an appellate mechanism through the Employees' Provident Fund Appellate Tribunal under Section 7D, with appeals lying under Section 7I. Under Section 7O, an employer cannot appeal against an order under Section 7A, 7B (review), 7C or 14B unless he deposits 40 per cent of the amount due from him as determined by the order. This was introduced by the 2016 amendment, which replaced the earlier requirement of 75 per cent. The pre-deposit prevents delaying appeals purely to avoid payment. Option 25% and 30% are invented figures. Option 50% might tempt a candidate who recalls that a higher figure applied earlier, but 75% was the earlier figure, not 50%.
explanations: Incorrect. 25% is not the pre-deposit requirement under Section 7O.
Incorrect. 30% is not the prescribed percentage.
Correct. Section 7O requires deposit of 40% of the amount due before an appeal is entertained.
Incorrect. 50% is not the statutory figure; the earlier figure was 75%, since reduced to 40%.
keyfact: EPF Act, Section 7O: pre-deposit of 40% of the amount due for appeal to the EPFAT.
question: Under the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952, an employer who wishes to prefer an appeal before the Employees' Provident Fund Appellate Tribunal against an order under Section 7A (determination of dues) must deposit with the Tribunal a specified percentage of the amount due from him. This percentage is:
related: Section 7A of the EPF Act deals with determination of money due from employers.
Section 14B empowers recovery of damages for default in payment of contributions.
Section 7D provides for constitution of the EPF Appellate Tribunal.
Section 7I provides for appeals to the Tribunal.
subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: The correct answer is 40 per cent. Section 7O of the EPF Act requires an employer to deposit 40% of the amount due, as determined under Section 7A, before an appeal to the Tribunal is entertained.

detail: Ascent of sap in tall plants is explained by the cohesion-tension (transpiration pull) theory. Water evaporates from mesophyll cells, creating tension that pulls a continuous water column up through the xylem, with cohesion between water molecules and adhesion to xylem walls maintaining the column. Phloem carries sucrose from sources such as mature leaves to sinks such as roots, fruits and growing tips, as explained by the pressure-flow hypothesis. Stomatal opening depends on guard cells becoming turgid as they take up water. Under water stress, abscisic acid triggers loss of turgor, so stomata close. Elimination: statement 3 is false, so options b, c and d are all ruled out, leaving a.
explanations: Correct: statements 1 and 2 are true and statement 3 is false.
Wrong: it includes statement 3, which is false.
Wrong: it includes statement 3 and leaves out statement 2, which is true.
Wrong: statement 3 is false, so not all three are correct.
keyfact: Water stress closes stomata via abscisic acid; guard cells turn flaccid.
question:
Consider the following statements about plant physiology:
1. Transpiration pull, generated by evaporation of water from leaf mesophyll cells, is the main force for the ascent of sap in tall trees.
2. Phloem transports sugars mainly from source to sink and the process is called translocation.
3. Guard cells of stomata lose turgor and the stomata open during water stress.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
related: Abscisic acid is the stress hormone that closes stomata.
Xylem conducts water, phloem conducts food.
Auxin promotes cell elongation and apical dominance.
Cytokinin promotes cell division.
statements: 1 — Correct: transpiration pull with cohesion of water in xylem lifts sap to great heights.
2 — Correct: translocation of sugars in phloem runs from source to sink.
3 — Incorrect: guard cells that lose turgor close the stomata; abscisic acid mediates this under stress.
Related facts: xylem carries water and minerals upward, mostly in one direction. Phloem transport is bidirectional. Stomata are mostly open in daylight, when guard cells are turgid.
subject: General Science
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong because loss of turgor in guard cells closes the stomata, which reduces water loss.

detail: The Code on Social Security, 2020 subsumed the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 and eight other social security laws. It keeps the threshold of twenty employees for compulsory EPF coverage. The Central Government may reduce this number by notification. Employers below the threshold may also opt in voluntarily, with the Central Provident Fund Commissioner's approval. Do not confuse this with ESI, where coverage applies to establishments with ten or more employees. The Code also allows ESI to be extended more widely, including to hazardous occupations even for a single employee. Option (a) is the ESI figure. Options (c) and (d) are not thresholds under the Code for EPF, though 50 is the lay-off compensation threshold and 100 was the old prior-permission threshold in industrial law.
explanations: Incorrect: ten employees is the usual ESI threshold, not the EPF one.
Correct: EPF applies to establishments employing 20 or more employees.
Incorrect: 50 is not the EPF threshold; it relates to lay-off compensation in the IR Code.
Incorrect: 100 is not the EPF threshold.
keyfact: EPF coverage under the Social Security Code: 20 or more employees; ESI: 10 or more.
question: Under the Code on Social Security, 2020, the provisions relating to the Employees' Provident Fund apply, as a general rule, to an establishment employing at least how many employees?
related: The Code on Social Security, 2020 subsumed the EPF and MP Act, 1952 and the ESI Act, 1948 among others.
Establishments below 20 employees can join EPF voluntarily.
ESI generally applies to establishments with 10 or more employees.
The Central Provident Fund Commissioner is the chief executive officer of the EPFO.
subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: Option (b) is correct. The Employees' Provident Fund provisions apply to an establishment employing 20 or more employees, as under the earlier EPF Act, 1952. The Central Government may notify a lower number.

detail: The keystone species concept was introduced by Robert Paine, based on his work with the predatory sea star Pisaster in rocky intertidal zones. When Pisaster was removed, mussels dominated and species diversity dropped sharply. A keystone species is defined by the disproportionate impact it has relative to its abundance, not by being dominant in numbers or biomass. Examples include sea otters controlling sea urchins in kelp forests, and elephants and tigers in many landscapes. A species that dominates by numbers or biomass is called a dominant species and is a different concept. To solve such questions, test Statement-II against the definition. Since 'always the most abundant' contradicts the idea of disproportionate effect, it is incorrect, leaving option c.
explanations: Wrong: Statement-II is incorrect, so it cannot explain Statement-I.
Wrong: Statement-II is incorrect, so both cannot be correct.
Correct: Statement-I is true by definition, while keystone species are defined by impact, not by abundance.
Wrong: Statement-I is correct, so it cannot be the incorrect one.
keyfact: Keystone species are defined by disproportionate ecological impact, not by abundance.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: The removal of a keystone species from an ecosystem can cause disproportionately large changes in community structure.
Statement-II: A keystone species is always the most abundant species in its ecosystem by number and biomass.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: The keystone species concept was proposed by Robert Paine in 1969, using the sea star Pisaster.
Sea otters are a keystone species in kelp forest ecosystems.
A dominant species is one with the greatest abundance or biomass, which is a different concept.
An umbrella species is one whose protection also protects many other species.
subject: Environment
summary: Statement-I is correct and Statement-II is incorrect. A keystone species has an effect on its ecosystem far greater than its abundance would suggest, so it is often not the most abundant species.

detail: The IUCN Red List uses nine categories: Extinct, Extinct in the Wild, Critically Endangered, Endangered, Vulnerable, Near Threatened, Least Concern, Data Deficient and Not Evaluated. Only the three categories Critically Endangered, Endangered and Vulnerable count as 'threatened'. Data Deficient means there is too little information to assess extinction risk, so it is not a threat category. 'Extinct in the Wild' covers species surviving only in captivity, cultivation or as a naturalised population outside their range. The Red List is a scientific, authoritative assessment, not a treaty. It has no binding legal force, although many national laws and policies refer to it. Elimination: statement 1 is a classic trap, and statement 4 is wrong because the Red List is advisory. With 2 and 3 correct and 1 and 4 wrong, the count is two.
explanations: Incorrect: two statements are correct, not one.
Correct: statements 2 and 3 are correct, and 1 and 4 are incorrect.
Incorrect: this would require statement 1 or 4 to be correct, and neither is.
Incorrect: Data Deficient is not threatened and the Red List is not binding.
keyfact: Threatened = CR + EN + VU only; Data Deficient is not threatened, and the Red List is not legally binding.
question:
With reference to the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species, consider the following statements:
1. 'Data Deficient' is one of the three categories classified as 'threatened'.
2. A species is listed as 'Extinct in the Wild' when it is known to survive only in cultivation, in captivity or as a naturalised population well outside its past range.
3. 'Critically Endangered', 'Endangered' and 'Vulnerable' together constitute the threatened categories.
4. A species' listing on the Red List is legally binding on all member countries of the IUCN.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
related: The nine IUCN categories run from Extinct to Not Evaluated.
Near Threatened and Least Concern are not threatened categories.
IUCN is a membership union of governments and NGOs, with its headquarters in Gland, Switzerland.
The Red List criteria include population decline, geographic range and population size.
statements: 1 — Incorrect: Data Deficient is a separate category and not part of the threatened group. It means information is inadequate for assessment.
2 — Correct: This is the IUCN definition of Extinct in the Wild (EW).
3 — Correct: CR, EN and VU together form the threatened categories.
4 — Incorrect: The Red List is a scientific assessment without legal force. Legal protection comes from national laws or treaties such as CITES.
subject: Environment
summary: Only statements 2 and 3 are correct, so the answer is 'Only two'. Data Deficient is not a threatened category, and Red List status carries no legal force.

detail: Cold currents generally flow from higher to lower latitudes, or along the west coasts of continents in the tropics and subtropics, where upwelling occurs. The Peru (Humboldt) Current runs along the west coast of South America and the Benguela Current along the south-west coast of Africa, and both are cold. Option (a) pairs the warm Kuroshio with the cold Oyashio. Option (c) pairs the warm Agulhas, which flows along the south-east coast of Africa, with the cold Falkland (Malvinas) Current. Option (d) pairs the warm Norwegian Current, an extension of the North Atlantic Drift, with the cold Labrador Current. Only option (b) has two cold currents. A good strategy is to remember which current in each pair is warm: Kuroshio, Agulhas and Norwegian are all warm.
explanations: Wrong: Kuroshio is a warm current, while Oyashio is cold.
Correct: both the Peru (Humboldt) and Benguela currents are cold currents.
Wrong: Agulhas is warm, while Falkland is cold.
Wrong: Norwegian is warm, while Labrador is cold.
keyfact: Warm: Kuroshio, Agulhas, Norwegian. Cold: Oyashio, Falkland, Labrador, Peru, Benguela.
question: Which one of the following pairs consists of two cold ocean currents?
related: Kuroshio is a warm current in the North Pacific.
The Canary and California currents are cold currents.
The Gulf Stream and North Atlantic Drift are warm currents.
The West Australian Current is cold.
subject: Geography
summary: The Peru (Humboldt) and Benguela currents are both cold currents, so the answer is (b). In each of the other pairs one current is warm.

detail: India has signed Social Security Agreements with a number of countries to protect the interests of workers who move across borders. The agreements have two main objectives. The first is to avoid double coverage and double contribution. The second is to allow portability of benefits. A detached worker is an employee of an establishment in one contracting country who is sent to work in the other country for a limited period. He continues to be covered under the social security law of his home country and is exempt from contributing in the host country, usually for a specified period. A certificate of coverage is issued as proof. Option (b) describes permanent migration, which is not detachment. Option (c) describes an unorganised worker, and option (d) confuses the term with an international worker under the EPF scheme.
explanations: Correct. This is the standard meaning of a detached worker under an SSA: temporary posting, home-country coverage, and exemption in the host country.
Incorrect. Permanent migration does not make a person a detached worker, because detachment is temporary.
Incorrect. A detached worker is defined by temporary posting abroad, not by sector or absence of an employer.
Incorrect. This confuses the term with international workers and foreign employees in India, who fall under separate EPF scheme provisions.
keyfact: A detached worker is a temporary posting abroad who stays under the home country's social security and is exempt in the host country.
options: an employee sent by an establishment in one SSA partner country to work temporarily in the other, who stays covered under the home country's social security system and is exempt from contribution in the host country
an Indian employee who has permanently migrated to a country with which India has an SSA and has surrendered his EPF membership
a worker who is employed in the unorganised sector and has no employer-employee relationship
a foreign national employed in India who is exempted from EPF coverage because of his salary level
question: In the context of India's Social Security Agreements (SSAs) with other countries, the term 'detached worker' refers to
related: SSAs avoid double contribution and allow exportability of pension benefits.
A certificate of coverage is the proof of exemption in the host country.
India's first SSA was with Belgium.
International workers under the EPF scheme contribute on full wages without the wage ceiling.
subject: Social Security
summary: The answer is (a). A detached worker is one sent temporarily by an employer in one SSA country to another and who stays covered by the home country's system. This avoids dual contribution.

detail: Kanishka is traditionally associated with the Fourth Buddhist Council in Kashmir, held under Vasumitra and Ashvaghosha. Gautamiputra Satakarni's achievements are described in the Nasik Prashasti issued by his mother Gautami Balashri. Samudragupta's conquests are described by Harishena in the Allahabad (Prayag) Pillar inscription. Pulakeshin II's victories, including over Harshavardhana, are recorded in the Aihole inscription composed by Ravikirti. Knowing any two pairs, such as Samudragupta with Allahabad and Pulakeshin II with Aihole, eliminates all other options.
explanations: Right: all four pairs are correctly matched.
Wrong: Gautamiputra is not linked to the Allahabad Pillar, and Samudragupta is not linked to the Nasik Prashasti.
Wrong: Kanishka is not linked to the Aihole inscription.
Wrong: Kanishka is not linked to the Nasik Prashasti, and Pulakeshin II is not linked to the Allahabad Pillar.
keyfact: Aihole inscription (Ravikirti) records Pulakeshin II; Allahabad Pillar (Harishena) records Samudragupta.

detail: BRICS expanded in 2024 to include Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the UAE, and Saudi Arabia was invited. Indonesia was formally admitted as a full member in January 2025, a decision announced by Brazil, which held the 2025 chairship. A separate 'partner country' category was created at the Kazan Summit in October 2024. Nigeria joined as a partner in January 2025, and Vietnam became a partner in June 2025. Malaysia was also a partner country. Partners take part in discussions but are not full members. To solve this, separate the two categories. Full members after 2024 are Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, the UAE and Indonesia, and Saudi Arabia's status is ambiguous. Nigeria and Vietnam are partners. Only Indonesia fits the question. India chairs BRICS in 2026.
explanations: Incorrect: Nigeria joined as a partner country in January 2025, not as a full member.
Correct: Indonesia was admitted as a full member in January 2025.
Incorrect: Vietnam became a partner country in June 2025.
Incorrect: Malaysia is a partner country, not a full member.
keyfact: Indonesia became a full BRICS member in January 2025, while Nigeria and Vietnam are partner countries.

related: India holds the BRICS chairship in 2026

The Great Stupa at Sanchi was commissioned by Ashoka in the third century BCE and later enlarged and embellished with gateways under the Shungas and Satavahanas. Jainism's first Tirthankara was Rishabhanatha (Adinatha); Mahavira was the 24th and last, and Parshvanatha was the 23rd. Hence option (b) is correct.
explanations: Incomplete: statement 2 is also correct.

detail: The IPCC was set up in 1988 by the WMO and UNEP to provide governments with scientific assessments on climate change, its impacts and options. It is open to all member countries of the UN and WMO. It does not carry out original research or monitor climate data; instead, thousands of scientists volunteer to review published literature and produce policy-relevant but policy-neutral reports. The Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5°C was released in 2018 and fell within the Sixth Assessment cycle, along with the Special Report on Climate Change and Land (2019) and on the Ocean and Cryosphere in a Changing Climate (2019). Hence statement 2 is incorrect, and 1 and 3 are correct.
explanations: Incorrect: statement 3 is also correct.
Correct: statements 1 and 3 are correct, and 2 is incorrect.
Incorrect: statement 2 is wrong because the IPCC does not do original research.
Incorrect: statement 2 is wrong.
keyfact: The IPCC assesses published science; it does not conduct its own research.
question:

3. The Sixth Assessment Report cycle included three Special Reports, one of which was on Global Warming of 1.5°C.

related: The IPCC won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2007 jointly with Al Gore.

statements: 1 — Correct: The IPCC was created in 1988 by WMO and UNEP.
2 — Incorrect: It assesses published literature and does not conduct its own research or monitoring.
3 — Correct: The 1.5°C report (2018), the land report and the ocean and cryosphere report (both 2019) belonged to the AR6 cycle.
subject: Environment
summary: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The IPCC does not conduct its own research; it assesses published scientific literature.

detail: Jagdeep Dhankhar resigned as Vice-President in July 2025, which led to a fresh election, held in September 2025. The Vice-President is elected under Article 66 by an electoral college of all members of both Houses of Parliament, including nominated members, through proportional representation by single transferable vote with a secret ballot. C. P. Radhakrishnan, a former Governor of Maharashtra and earlier a Lok Sabha member from Coimbatore, was the NDA candidate and won. The opposition fielded B. Sudershan Reddy, a former Supreme Court judge. M. Venkaiah Naidu was the 13th Vice-President (2017-22), and Om Birla is the Lok Sabha Speaker, so neither fits. For elimination, the vacancy arose in 2025, so previous office-holders and the Speaker can be removed. The Vice-President is the ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
explanations: Correct: he was elected the 15th Vice-President in September 2025.
Wrong: he was the opposition's joint candidate and was defeated.
Wrong: he served as Vice-President from 2017 to 2022 and is a former holder of the office.
Wrong: he is the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, not a Vice-Presidential candidate.
keyfact: C. P. Radhakrishnan became the 15th Vice-President of India in September 2025.
question: Following the resignation of Jagdeep Dhankhar in July 2025, who was elected as the 15th Vice-President of India in September 2025?
related: Article 63 provides that there shall be a Vice-President of India.
